full_judgment:
Mr. Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, J: This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 1004.2008 passed by the Joint District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.162 of 2005 decreeing the suit brought under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1887. 

2. Facts in a nutshell, giving rise to this revisional application are that the opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.102 of 2001 before the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) 3rd   Court, Dhaka under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act praying for recovery of possession in respect of the land described in the schedule to the plaint, impleading the petitioners as defendants. 

3. In their plaint, the plaintiffs disclosed their case stating inter alia that the Ka schedule property disclosed in the plaint originally belonged to Nezabot Ali Khan, Abdul Hakim and others and while they had been in possession of this land it was recorded in their favour during C.S. operation appertaining to khatian No.174 and Plot No.67 within Mouza Dhanmondi; Mirza Abdul Kadir one of the co-sharer of the Jamaindari Estate settled five bigas of land in favour of Sree Aboni Mohon Dey and Aboni Mohon executed a registered kabuliyat on 18-12-1940 and in course of such settlement Aboni Mohon being in possession of the said five bigas of land settled three bighas out of the same in favour of one Abdul Barek by a registered Addi Barga kabuliyat, subsequently, Aboni Mohon entered into an agreement for sale of one acres of land from the south western part of C.S. Plot No.67 with one Abdul Mazid Howlader and Begum Ayesha Noor on 29.07.47 at a consideration of Tk.3000/00 out of the said amount of Tlc.3000/00 the purchasers paid Tk.750/00 as earnest money whereupon possession was delivered in favour of the purchasers but due to partition of the country, the executant left for India so they subsequently arranged to execute and register a sale deed through an appointed attorney; meanwhile process of acquisition by the government was started through L.A. Case No.6 of 1948-49 in respect of part of Plot No.67; then one Sufia Khatun filed Writ Petition No.145 of 1965 challenging the notice issued in said L.A. Case and Rule was issued initially but subsequently the same was discharged on 19.08.1966 thereafter Sufia Khatun preferred an appeal to the Supreme Court of Pakistan being Appeal No.63-D of 1966 whereupon Pakistan Supreme Court vide its judgment and order dated 01.12.1967 allowed the appeal declaring the notice of acquisition as a defective one; it is also disclosed in the plaint that husband of Begum Aysha Nur was assured by the then C&B by its letter No.104 TP dated 15.01.53 for making construction on the suit property upon receipt of Government plan; thereafter, it is also stated in the plaint, that Ka schedule property along with some other properties were relieved from the acquisition process; on 26-10-56 one Ashutosh Dey Sarker being appointed as attorney of Aboni Mohon Dey executed and registered a sale deed in favour of Abdul Mojid Howlader and Ayesha Nur, thereafter Abdul Mojid Howlader transferred a area of 8 khatas of land from the suit plot in favour of one M. A. Goni and Afaiuddin Khan by a kabala dated 31.07.57 subsequently Mojid Howlader transferred the remaining 22 khatas of land by oral gift to predecessor of the 'plaintiffs Begum Ayesha Noor and since then Ayesha Noor had been possessing the schedule property till 03-10-2000 on which date she died leaving behind the plaintiffs as her legal heirs; the plaintiffs and their predecessors had been in possession of the suit property by constructing 16 shop rooms inducting tenants for more than 48 years and those shop rooms were rented in favour of different persons as tenants who had been running their business concerns in those rooms; while the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land as aforesaid RAJUK in collusion with the defendants demolished the structures constructed by the plaintiffs over the suit land and in the process RAJUK obtained an Aungikemama (bond) from the plaintiff No.1 under pressure; thereafter RAJUK again demolished the structures of the plaintiffs over the suit land by bulldozer in collusion with the husband of defendant No.6 with the aid of hired miscreants; after demolishing plaintiffs structures in the suit land on 30-03-2001 defendants dis-possessed the plaintiffs from the Ka schedule property by installing fencing with tin around it; they also constructed some rooms in the site; it is also stated in the plaint that the police did not take action against the influential invaders; lastly on 20.04.2001 a G.D. Entry could be made by the plaintiffs over the act of their dispossession on 30.03.2001. It is also stated in the plaint that the defendants are strangers who have dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land using RAJUK as a tool for their mischief. 

4. Defendant Nos.1-6 entered appearance upon filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that one Gopeshor Paul was the C.S. recorded tenant of C.S. khatian No.174; he died leaving two sons Nil Kanta and Horn Krishna Paul; Hore Krishna died leaving only son Debraj Paul and Debraj Paul sold away 1.33 acres of land (three bighas by local measurement) including the structures thereon in favour of Kiron Chandra Banarjee on 17.07.33, thereafter on 18.04.48 Kiron Chandra transferred the said land to the predecessor of defendant Shahjahan Bhuiyan and immediately after his purchase 16.78 acres of suit C.S. Plot No.67 was acquired by the government in L.A. Case No.06 of 1948-49, compensation award was prepared in the name of Shahjahan Bhuiyan to the tune of Tk.3976.11 but the defendants predecessors did not withdrawn that compensation money as a result the said amount was deposited with the Government Revenue Account. It is also stated in the written statement that the said 1.33 acres of land of suit C.S. Plot No.67 remained in possession of the answering defendants since no formal possession was taken over by the L.A. Department.' The plaintiffs taking advantage of the land being vacant had illegally trespassed into a portion of the land and made some unauthorized construction which was subsequently demolished by RAJUK; the answering defendants have 14 semi pucca rooms in their portion of the land having been let out to different tenants; out of 4 bighas i.e. 133 acres of land these defendants am now in actual physical possession of 37 khathas encircled by C.I. sheet fencing and the remaining 43 khatha of land are in illegal possession of some unauthorized persons including the plaintiffs. These defendants are compelled to file suit for recovery of khan possession. it has also been specifically averred in the written statement that it appears on the face of the plaint that huge allegations have been made by the plaintiffs against the RAJUK and its officers but the RAJUK Chairman and other concerned officers have not been impleaded in the suit and no relief whatsoever have been sought for against the RAJUK and that under the Building Construction Act and the Rules framed thereunder RAJUK has its authority and statutory power to demolish unauthorized construction and in exercise of such power RAJUK with its Magistrate demolished the unauthorized structures and question of collusion and conspiracy with RAJUK by the answering defendants did never arise. It was also asserted in the written statement that the answering defendants inherited from their predecessor Shahjahan Bhuiyan a valid and good title in respect of the said 1.33 acres of land in suit C.S. Plot No.67 by virtue of inheritance from their predecessor Shahjahan Bhuiyan who purchased the same by virtue of a registered deed of sale dated 18.08.48 and that the claim of the plaintiffs is based on so called purchase in the year 1956 after acquisition of 16.78 acres of land in L.A. Case No.06 of 1948-49 is absolutely illegal and the present suit filed by the plaintiffs on the basis of the plaintiffs so-called claim is not entertainable in law, therefore, defendants prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

5. Eventually the suit was taken up for hearing by the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka where 6 witnesses were examined on behalf of the plaintiffs while 4 witnesses on behalf of the defendants and upon consideration of the evidence and the materials available on record the learned Joint District Judge decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 10.04.2008. 

6. As against the aforesaid decree the 41 defendants as petitioners preferred this revisional application (since no appeal lies) and obtained the present Rule. 

7. Mr. Md. Ashadullah the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits at the outset that the description of the suit land as given in the plaint is vague in that the R.S. Plot and R.S. khatian numbers are different in Ka and Kim schedule of the plaint and that the Kalmi Naksha filed with the plaint and the plot number shown therein do not tally with the description of the Kha schedule land of the plaint, therefore, Mr. Ashadullah pointing out the provision of law i.e. Order 7 Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that in the absence of clear description of the suit land in the plaint the impugned decree is not sustainable and in substantiating Mr. Ashadullah placed reliance in the case of Nazrul Islam and others Vs. Santi Ram Duphi and others reported in 12 MLR (AD) 105. 

8. The learned Advocate for the petitioners referring to paragraphs 6 and 7 of the plaint and Order No.3 I dated 8.4.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, in the instant suit, submits that both RAJUK and government are necessary parties in the suit and in the absence of those parties, the instant suit for mere recovery of possession under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act is not maintainable. In this connection the learned Advocate has also referred to the deposition of the witnesses examined on behalf of the plaintiffs. 

9. Referring to Exhibit 10 the judgment of a Writ Petition, Mr. Ashadullah submits that the plaintiffs cannot claim a different C.S. plot in the present suit than that they claimed in their writ petition Exalt) rather they are estopped from raising any claim in a land beyond Ext.10. 

10. The learned Advocate for the petitioners submits further that in view of the pleadings of the parties and the evidence lead the learned Joint District Judge ought to have arrived at a clear finding to the effect that the plaintiffs were not evicted from the suit land in due course of law as contemplated under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act. 

11. In substantiating the submission to that effect Mr. Ashadullah placed reliance in the case of Jebun Nessa Zaman Vs. Hosne Ara Lili reported in 53 DLR 394 and in the case of Year Mahmud Vs. Laxmi Das reported in AIR 1959(All) FB 1 land in the absence of any finding to that effect the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law. 

12. The learned Advocate for the petitioners also submits that the court below erred in law in not framing specific issue as to whether the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land or not and in view of absence of any evidence to that effect the impugned decree under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act is not sustainable. 

13. On the contrary Mr. Md. Serajul Huq, the teamed Advocate appearing for the respondents submits that since the question of maintainability has been decided in Civil Revision No.2535 of 2002 the same question about maintainability cannot be raised again. 

14. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits further that the question of possession and dispossession and the evidence thereto is a simple requirement of section 9 of the Specific Relief Act and nothing beyond. 

15. In substantiating his submissions the teamed Advocate refers to the case of Md. Sumzzaman Vs. Md. Ahmed Ali and others reported in 13 MLR (AD) 69 as also the case of Maruf Hossain Vs. Dil Jan Bibi reported in 13 MLR (AD) 196. As to the objection raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner with respect to order 7 Rule 3 of the Code of civil Procedure Mr. Md. Serajul Hug submits that vagueness of the suit land is a mixed question of facts and law such objection ought to have been raised at the trail court and some having not been raised before the trial court the defendants are now estopped from raising any such question before the revisional court. 

16. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties that the plaintiffs having given boundary in describing the land and in the event of any discrepancy with respect to the plot numbers and the boundary-and boundary shall prevail. 

17. In substantiating his submission the learned Advocate refers to the case of Abul Kalam Vs. Abu Taher and others reported in 8 BLC 265.It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for respondents that no objection as to the identity of the land having been raised in the trial court by the defendants no prejudice can be said to have been caused by mis-description therefore the decree passed is a valid one. 

18. Substantiating his submission the learned Advocate for the opposite patties placed reliance in the case of S. Nagaraj vs. Kalluramma reported in AIR 1996 (Knat) 125. 

19. In the form of reply the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits further that in the instant suit the written statement was filed by the defendant on 07.04. 06 while the application under order 7 Rule 11 was filed much earlier whereupon the order of rejection of the plaint was passed on 08-04-2002 against which the plaintiffs as petitioners preferred Civil Revision no.2535 of 2002 where the High Court Division made the Rule absolute on17-05-04, therefore, it is not correct to say that the defendant are now estopped from raising the question of maintainability in suit in view of the judgment and order dated 17-05-04 passed in Civil Revision No.2535of 2002. 

20. Heard the learned Advocates from both sides, perused the materials on record including the exhibits which were filed before the trial court from both sides whereupon it transpires that the trial court before passing the impugned decree and upon taking up the suit for trial framed as many as 5 issues which read as follows:-
1. Is the suit maintainable in its present forms? 
2. Is the suit barred by limitation? 
3. Is the suit bad for defect of parties? 
4. Weather the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit property without their consent on 30-3-2001? 
5. Can the plaintiff get the relives as prayed for? 

21. In this connection we feel it proper to quote Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act which reads as under:- 

"9. Suit by person dispossessed of immoveable property- If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immoveable property otherwise then in due course of law he or any person claiming through him may, by suit recover possession thereof, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such suit. 
Nothing in this section shall bar any person from suing to establish his title to such property and to cover possession thereof. 

No suit under this section shall be brought against (the government). 

No appeal shall be from any order or decree passed in any suit instituted under this section nor shall any review of any such orders or decree be allowed." 

22. From a plain reading of the aforesaid provision of law, we find that the mandate of the law also requires a finding to the effect that the plaintiffs were dispossessed from immoveable property not only without their consent but also otherwise than in due course of law. It is more so when we find that the defendant in their written statement specially averred that at some stage namely in the year 1948-49 the suit land along with other land was acquired by the government in L.A. Case No.06/1948-49 and that RAJUK having found the plaintiffs as unauthorized occupants in the suit land demolished the structures raised by the plaintiffs over the suit land. The fact acquisition has also been admitted by the plaintiffs in their plaint of course both the plaintiffs and the defendants claimed that the government did not take over possession of the suit land despite acquisition thereof. In view of the pleadings of the parties and the evidence lead by them we find that it was incumbent upon the trial court to arrive at a finding to the effect that RAJUK did not demolish the structure of the plaintiffs available on the suit land otherwise than in due course of law. 

23. True it is such a finding also not possible by the trial court unless the government and RAJUK are brought to the suit as defendants but the difficulty arises when there is a specific bar in bringing a suit under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act against the government or any functionary thereunder, therefore, a suit in the present form merely for recovery of possession under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act is not at all maintainable. Instead the plaintiffs are at liberty to bring a suit for recovery of khan possession upon declaration of their title over the suit land in a regular suit as contemplated under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and not otherwise, If they are so advised. In a summary proceeding under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act the relief cannot be claimed by plaintiffs as they did in present suit more so the learned trial court over looked this position of law and decreed the suit by his impugned judgment and decree. 

24. In this connection we may refer to the case of Jebun Nessa Zaman and others Vs. Hosne Ara Lili reported in 53 DLR 394 and the case of Yar Mahmud and another Vs. Lakshmi Das and another reported in AIR 1959(A11) FB 1. 

25. In view of the facts and circumstances disclosed before us we find that the restoration of possession in such a suit however always subject to a regular title suit and the person who has the real title or even the better title cannot therefore be prejudiced in any way by a decree in such a suit it will always be open to him or them establish his or their title in a regular suit and to recover back possession of course subject to the of limitation. 

26. From a plain reading of the six witnesses available on record examined on behalf of the plaintiffs we find all the witnesses in a chorus admitted that it is the RAJUK which demolished the structures available the suit land raised by the plaintiffs, therefore, it was also necessary for the trial court to frame an issue as to whether the defendant in fact dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land but we do not find any such issue framed by the trial court. Referring to the decision reported in 13 MLR (AD)196 and 13 MLR (AD)96 Mr. Md. Sirajul Huq the learned Advocate for the opposite parties pointed out that no such finding is necessary to the effect that the plaintiffs were dispossessed otherwise than without due course of law. 

27. We find with the premises under which the cited two cases arose do not however warrant such a finding as we have pointed out therefore, their lordships rightly refrained from making any comment on the same but the facts involved in the instant case is completely different where the pleadings and the deposition of the witnesses clearly indicate that it was RAJUK which demolished the structures raised by the plaintiffs, therefore the facts invoked in the present case before us warrant such a finding as we have already pointed out. 

28. In view of the position as disclosed above, we do not feel it necessary to go into other raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and replied by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties because of the simple reason that we do find that the instant suit as framed, is not maintainable, therefore, the impugned judgment and decree calls for interference by this court as such the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, The Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.162 of 2005 is hereby set aside. 

29. Send down the lower court record at once along with a copy of this judgment.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1430 of 2009
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. Quamrul Islam Siddique, Advocate instructed by Mr. Mohd. Nawab Ali Advocate-on-record
For rho Respondent: Mr. Fida M. Karnak Advocate Instructed by Mr. 
Shamsul Alam, Advocate-on-record
parties:
Ayurvedia Pharmacy (Dhaka) Ltd. ------ Petitioner
Versus
Meher Banu Bibi and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Anwarul Haque.J.:-  'This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 25'h of March, 2009 passed by Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3219 of 2006 under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 where the rule is rotund to have been discharged with a positive observation that plaintiff of Title Suit No. 145 of 2006 pending before the Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka has failed to comply the provision laid down in section 21 A(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. 

2. In short the case of the plaintiff-petitioner is as follows: 

Ayurvedia Pharmacy (Dhaka) Ltd., represented by its Managing Director, A.F.M. Fakrul Islam Munshi of 8/I and 8/2, Armenian Street under P.S. Kotwali, Dhaka entered into an agreement on 02.01.2000 to purchase the land described in the schedule at a consideration of Tk.2,34,00,000/- out of which Tk.78,00,000/- was paid in advance with a further commitment to pay the rest of the amount by ,315 December,2007. Subsequently on the incorporation of section I7A and 17B in the Registration Act. 1908 vide Act 25 of 2004 with the incorporation of section 2IA in the Specific Relief Act,1877 vide Act 27 of 2004 the plaintiff, the present petitioner finding no other alternative but to file a Title Suit No.I45 of 2006 for Specific Performance of Contract on 28.06.2006 where the learned Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) issued a direction to deposit the balance amount of Tk.1,34,00,000/within IS days in pursuance of the provision laid down in section 21 A of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 in default the suit shall stand not maintainable in the present form. 

3. Being aggrieved 'and dissatisfied with the said order No.6 dated 31.7.2006 the plaintiff, the present petitioner preferred the Civil Revision No.3219 or 2006 under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 where the High Court Division also echoed the view of the trial court and discharged the Rule. 

4. Thereafter the plaintiff-petitioner has filed this petition for leave to appeal alleging inter aria- that since in terms of agreement plaintiff-petitioner was given an opportunity to pay the balance amount on or before 31.12.2007 the court cannot direct to pay the such amount before such date in pursuance of the subsequent legislation. 

5. Mr. Quamrul Islam Siddiqui the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner submits that High Court Division has totally misconceived the spirit of the amended provisions of law incorporated in the Registration Act by Act 25 of 2004, and Specific Relief Act,1877 by Act 27 of 2004. In fact section I 7B is found to have been in contradiction with the provision of section 21A of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 where continuance of the right of the plaintiff by virtue of agreement has been denied. Mr. Siddiqui further submits that in no way court cannot direct to pay the balance amount before the expiry of 31.12.2007 which is the terms of the agreement made between the parties. 

6. On the other hand, Mr. Fida M. Kamal the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents has strongly opposed it alleging that the High Court Division has rightly pointed out the mandatory provision of section 21A of the Specific Relief Act where two pre-conditions have been imposed to file a suit for Specific Performance of Contract and such legislation has come into force from July, 2005 with a non-obstante clause. Moreover section 214A of the Specific Relief Act does not, at all, allow the court to entertain any plaint unless a registered agreement is annexed with the plaint and the balance amount is paid. The learned counsel for the respondent has also brought to our notice about the provision of section 17A and I7B of the Registration Act where all pending unregistered agreement at the time of enforcing the law on P' July, 2005 were required to be registered within the prescribed period of six months. 

In the instant case without compliance of such provision plaintiff-petitioner filed this suit for Specific Performance of Contract on the basis of unregistered deed of agreement and without payment of balance amount as required by law. So the court below and the High Court Division has taken a right decision which cannot be interfered with. 

7. On such submission let us quote the provision laid down in section 21 A of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. 

21A. Unregistered contract for sale not specifically enforceable-"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force no contract for, sale of any immovable property can be specifically enforced unless-

(a) the contract is in writing and registered under the Registration Act,1908, whether or not the transferee has been taken possession of the property or any part thereof; and (hi the balance amount of consideration of the contract is deposited in, the court at the time of filing the suit for specific performance of the contract."

The above provision of law clearly mandated to deposit the balance amount irrespective of any condition available in the agreement which is not also registered one as required under section 17A and I7B of the Registration Act. 

8. It will not be out of place to mention that plaintiff petitioner was required to deposit the balance amount in terms of agreement on or before 31.12.2007 but till now he has not deposited the same though he filed the suit for equitable relief in the form of the Specific Performance of Contract. However since both the trial court and the High Court Division are on the same view relating to deposit of the balance amount at the time of filing of the suit for Specific Performance of Contract under section 21 A of the Specific Relief Act we find no illegality or infirmity therein which deserves our interference. 

9. In that view of the matter the petition for leave to appeal is hereby dismissed. 

End.

lawyer:
Dr. Md. Eunus Ali Akond with Mr. Fazlul Haque -- For the petitioners 
Mr. Md. Rafiqul Islam (Heru) with Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin -- For the opposite party
parties:
Most. Alom Taj begum @ Monowar Begum and others ----- Petitioners 
Versus
Sree Nimai Chandra Roy ----- Opposite party
full_judgment:
Mr. Faruque Ahmed J.:- This rule at the instance of the defendant petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 29.01.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Borguna in Title Appeal No. 02 of 2001 reversing the Judgment and decree dated 15.11.2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Borguna Sadar, Borguna in Title Suit No. 115 of 1998 should not be set aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Short facts of the case arc as follows:- The opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 115/98 before the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Borguna Sadar, Borguna praying for declaration of title stating inter-alia that the suit land is 6 decimals of land of Plot No. 351 which belonged to Rajendra Chandra who died leaving 4 (four) sons namely (1) Suchil, (2) Monindra (3) Sudhir (4) Nimai and one wife; that after death of Rajendra his heirs have been living separately; that at the time of death of Rajendra his son Nimai Chandra Roy was a minor who is the plaintiff of the instant suit and that when the plaintiff has been living separately then his other 3 brothers transferred the 18 decimals of land on 17.02.73 by 4 deeds to the defendant No. 1-4; that the plaintiff's name was shown in the serial number 4 of the said deed dated 17.02.73 which are illegal, without lawful authority; that the 6 decimals of land showing in the aforesaid deeds and showing the defendant No.5 as guardian of the plaintiff is illegal; that the defendant No.5 is not the legal guardian of the minor; he was not appointed as guardian by the court; the plaintiff could not know any thing earlier about aforesaid deeds; the plaintiff could know on 12.10.98 about the aforesaid deeds and accordingly instituted the instant suit.

3. The defendant No. 1-4 contested the denying all material allegation of the plaint and stating inter-alia that the suit is not maintainable; the suit is barred by Limitation, the suit is bad for defect of parties; that after death of Rajendra, his sons had been living jointly and that on 17.02.73 the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 5-7, transferred the 24 decimals of land of Plot No. 351 to the defendant No. 1-4 vide 4 needs Nos. 391/392/393/394 and handed over possession of the suit land; the defendant No. 1-4 had been possessing the said 24 decimals of land; the defendant No. 1-4 mutated their names vide mutation case No. 249/73-74, 250/73-74, 251/73-74, and 252/73-74; that the defendant No. 5 Monindra Chandra Roy was appointed guardian of the plaintiff; the plaintiff had knowledge about the aforesaid deeds; the plaintiff's claim is false and the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The suit was heard by the Senior Assistant Judge, Borguna who dismissed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 15.11.2000 and 21.11.2000, against which the plaintiff preferred title Appeal No.02/2001 before the District Judge, Borguna and the same appeal was beard by the joint district Judge, 1st Court, Borguna who allowed in appeal vide judgment and decree dated 29.01.2002 and 05.02.2002 and decreed the suit.

5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid appellate judgment and decree, the defendant petitioners obtained the present rule.

6. Dr. Md. Enus Ali Akond Advocate along with Mr. Fazlul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners placed the revisional application, the impugned judgments and decrees, and the depositions of the P.Ws and D.Ws on record and submitted that the learned trial Court on considering the evidence and materials on record having found that the plaintiff could not prove his case and having dismissed the suit, the learned appellate Court on misreading the evidence and materials on record illegally allowed the appeal. The learned Advocate further submitted that the learned appellate Court without considering the facts and circumstances of the case illegally held that the disputed deeds were obtained by the defendant petitioners by practicing fraud upon the plaintiff who was minor at the relevant time and illegally held that the when fraud is proved the question of limitation does not arise. The learned Advocate further submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the case, Article 44 of the Limitation Act is applicable, but the learned appellate Court illegally held that Article 120 of the Limitation Act is applicable in the present case and accordingly committed error in law in allowing the appeal. The learned Advocate further submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the present case Article 44 of the Limitation Act is applicable and under the said Article there is no provision for counting the limitation from the alleged knowledge of the plaintiff about the disputed deed and as such the learned appellate Court committed gross error in allowing the appeal holding that from the date of knowledge of the plaintiff the suit has been filed within time.

7. Mr. Md. Rafiqul Islam (Hem), the learned advocate along with Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party, on the other hand, submitted that the learned appellate Court on considering the evidence of the P.Ws and D.Ws on record rightly allowed the appeal and in the absence of any misreading or non consideration of the material evidence on record, the finding of fact as arrived at by the learned appellate Court being final it cannot be interfered with by this Court in revision. The learned Advocate further submitted that having regard to the fact that the mother of the plaintiff being alive at the relevant time none of the other brothers can be the natural guardian of the minor Nimai and in the present case Monindra one of the three adult brothers of Nimai having executed and registered the disputed deed on behalf of minor Nimai, the deed is a void one and in the present case Article 120 of the Limitation Act is applicable and the learned appellate Court rightly found that the plaintiff's suit is not barred by limitation. The learned Advocate further submitted that in the deed there is no reference of legal necessity of the minor, no such evidence also has been adduced by the defendant to prove that the disputed transfer was for legal necessity of the minor and as such the learned appellate Court rightly allowed the appeal holding that the disputed deed is a void one.

8. On perusal, it appears, the learned trial Court held that the plaintiff as P.W.1 deposed in the case and his present age is 40 years, his age at the time of execution of the disputed deed dated 17.02.1973 was 13 years and that the plaintiff attained the majority in 1978 and he filed the present suit in 1998 so according to the learned trial Court he filed suit after 20 years of his attaining majority and after 25 years of the date of execution and registration of the deed. The learned trial Court held that the plaintiff did not file the suit within three years of his attaining majority and 12 years from the date of the disputed deed and as such the suit is barred by limitation. The learned trial Court further found that the defendant No. 5 brother of the plaintiff being the karta of the Hindu family executed and registered the deed on behalf of the minor and as such the deed is a genuine and valid one and that by the said deed defendant acquired good title in the suit land and that the deed has been acted upon. The learned trial Court further held that the suit as framed is not maintainable without praying for cancellation of the disputed deed under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act. On these findings the learned trial Court dismissed the suit.

9. On appeal, the learned appellate Court, on the other hand, held that there is no reference in the deed itself and that there is no evidence also to show that the suit land was transferred for legal necessity of the minor and as such the deed is a void abinitio. The learned appellate Court further found that the defendant No. 5 the brother of the minor plaintiff at the relevant time had no locus-standi or legal authority to transfer the suit land on behalf of the minor. 'The learned appellate Court further held that the suit as framed is maintainable without prayer for cancellation of the disputed deed. The learned appellate Court further found that the present suit being a suit for declaration that the disputed deed is a void one Article 120 of the Limitation Act is applicable and held that the suit having been filed within 6 years from the date of his knowledge dated 12.10.1998 suit is not barred by limitation. The learned appellate Court further found that the plaintiff was able to prove his possession in the suit land. The learned appellate Court further found that the defendants initially having claimed title in the suit land by the disputed 4 deeds dated 17.02.1973 cannot claim title by adverse possession subsequently as there is a legal bar in claiming title at the same time by two alternative ways. The learned appellate Court then held that the disputed 4 deeds dated 17.02.1973 are void and the defendants did not acquire any title in the suit land. With these findings the learned appellate Court allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial Court.

10. On perusal of the judgment passed by the Courts below and pleading of the parties, it appears, admittedly 4 deeds were jointly executed and registered on 17.02.1973 by 4 brothers namely Sudhir Chandra Roy, Sushil Chandra Roy, Monindra Chandra Roy and Nimai Chandra Roy (minor), admittedly by these 4 deeds 24 decimals of land has been transferred out of 35 decimals of land of plot No. 351, admittedly in each of the 4 deeds said 4 brothers including the minor were the executants, so each deed was for 6 decimals of land. Admittedly Nimai was a minor at that time and admittedly Monindra Chandra Roy executed each deed for himself as well as natural guardian of minor Nimai. It appears, in the schedule of the plaint in schedule-Ka reference of said 4 separate deeds have been given, In schedule-Kha 13 separate plots have been mentioned out of which the suit land has been shown to be 6 decimals of land only in plot No. 351 and no boundary of said 6 decimals has been given in the schedule of the plaint. It may be noted that in each of the 4 deeds the area of land has been mentioned as 6 decimals and minor Nimai has been named in each deed, so it cannot be said with certainty, that which 6 decimals of land which is the share of the plaintiff is covered by which deed. Thus, it appears, the specification of the suit land was not proper. Order 7 Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that the description of the suit land must be specific and if necessary the specific boundary should be given. The present suit is a suit for declaration of title as well as the 4 deeds are void. So it is a suit for declaration simpliciter in which specification of the suit land is a must. Thus I find that the suit land is vague, unspecified and for this defect also the suit should fail, however this aspect of the case was not considered by any of the Courts below.

11. Moreover, in this suit the factum of possession is a very material thing and the learned trial Court held that the plaintiff could not prove his possession in the suit land, but the learned appellate Court held that the plaintiff could prove his possession in the suit land. Admittedly by the said 4 deeds 24 decimals of land have been transferred by 4 brothers including the plaintiff and out of this 24 decimals plaintiff's claim is for 6 decimals. In the schedule of the plaint the plaintiff has shown this 6 decimals in plot No.351 out of 13 plots. There is no case by the plaintiff that by amicable portion among the brothers the plaintiff got said 6 decimals of land and he is in possession of that 6 decimals of land. The plaintiff in his examination in-chief stated that he is in possession of the suit land. To the query of the Court, plaintiff stated that there is a `doba' in suit plot No. 351 and that the plaintiff along with his other brothers are the owners of that ditch and the defendants do not use the said ditch and that the defendants land is to the eastern side of that ditch. In cross-examination he could not say how much land he got from his father and he could not say how much land he sold out. He also could not tell how much nal land he got. He denied the suggestion that at the instance of his brothers he filed the present suit. He further stated that he paid tax including municipal tax for the suit land, but he had not pay tax for the present year. He stated that he cannot produce the rent receipt for the suit land. He stated that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 made a wall in the north southern direction in the suit land for their share. He also stated that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 made a wall in the southern side of plot no. 351. P.W.2 who is the husband of the sister of the plaintiff in his cross-examination stated that he cannot tell how much land the plaintiff possesses in the suit dag. He stated that the defendant Nos.1- 4 have a house in the northern bank of the ditch and that they are in possession by placing a fence. He stated that he does not know how much land of the disputed deed the plaintiff possesses. P.W.3 Monindra Chandra Roy stated in his examination in-chief that the plaintiff possesses the suit land, but in cross-examination he stated that he does not know the dag and khatian number of the suit land. The defendant examined 2 D.Ws including the defendant No. 3. It appears, regarding possession of the defendants they corroborated each other and no material contradiction came out from their cross-examination.

12. Admittedly the defendants purchased 24 decimals of land by 4 deeds in which plaintiff claims 6 decimals of land. In the schedule of the plaint 6 decimals of land out of plot No. 351 is the suit land. Admittedly no boundary of the suit land has been given. In the plaint and deposition of the plaintiff nothing has been stated that by amicable portion he got the 6 decimals of land in Plot no.351.

13. It appears, the case of the plaintiff is that the defendants posses the rest 18 decimals of land out of 24 decimals of land. Plaintiff as P.W.1 admitted in his deposition that the defendants are in possession of some portion of suit land by constructing wall. P.W.2 stated in his deposition that the defendants No. 1 and 2 also are in possession of some portion of the suit land by constructing wall. All the D.Ws also corroborated each other regarding possession of the defendants in the suit land. Thus from the deposition of the P.Ws and D.Ws it is clear that the plaintiff could not prove his exclusive possession in the suit land of which no specific boundary (of said 6 decimals out of 24 decimals) has been given. So, in my opinion, the finding of possession as arrived at by the learned appellate Court is illegal and not sustainable in law.

14. Regarding limitation the learned trial Court found that the suit is barred by limitation, the learned appellate Court, on the other hand, found that the suit is not barred by limitation. According to the appellate Court Article 120 is applicable in the case and the suit having been filed within 6 years from the date of knowledge of the deed dated 12.10.1998 the suit is well within time.

15. Now let me consider the question of limitation. It appears, the specific case of the plaintiff is that during his minority, his brother Monindra Chandra Roy executed the deed on his behalf as natural guardian and he had no earlier knowledge about the said deed and that on 12.10.1998 he for the first time came to know about the disputed deed and accordingly filed the suit on 29.11.1998. Article 44 of the Limitation Act provides for setting aside a transfer of property by guardian of the minor which reads as follows:

"By a ward who has attained majority, to set aside a transfer of property by his guardian, period of limitation is 3 years and the period will run when the ward attains majority."

<u>16. It appears, in the said article there is no provision for filing a suit from the date of knowledge of such disputed deed. In other words, in order to challenge a transfer of the property of the minor by the guardian, the minor can file a suit within 3 years of his attaining majority. Reference may be given to the case of Sultan Ahmed vs Fazlul Kabir reported in 5 DLR 383. Wherein it has been held that limitation for filing a suit is 3 years from the date when the disability ceases. In the present case in view of article 44 of the Limitation Act, in my opinion, the limitation will be 3 years from the date of attaining majority of the plaintiff. It appears, the plaintiff was aged 13 years when the disputed deed dated 17-2-1973 was executed and, as such, he attained majority in the year 1978-1979 and he could file a suit by 1981 or 1982, but it appears, the present suit was filed on 29-11-1992, after about 10/12 years of his attaining majority. So, in my opinion, the suit is barred by limitation.</u>

17. Since I have found above that suit is bad for want of specification, and that the plaintiff failed to prove his possession in the suit land and that the suit is barred by limitation, in my opinion, the learned appellate Court committed gross error in law in allowing the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree which are liable to be set aside.

18. In the result; the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court are set aside and those of the trial Court dismissing the suit are affirmed and maintained.

19. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.

Send down the LC Records immediately.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Mantazuddin Ahmed, Advocate -- For plaintiff-appellants 
No one appears -- For the defendant-respondents
parties:
Abu Jafar and others ----- Appellants
Versus
Md. Eshaque and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J:- This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 14_9.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No.32 of 2007 heard analogously with the Other Suit No.33 of 2007. Other Suit No.32 of 2007 was instituted for declaration of title with prayer for permanent injunction. On the other hand Other Suit No.33 of 2007 was filed for declaration and for correction of B.S. record. 

2. The short facts for disposal of both the suits are that, while Ali Hossain and his sister, Asia Khatun had been in possession - of the suit property, the property was transferred in favour of Abdul Motaleb and Ali Ahmed in 1930. Abdul Motaleb transferred his portion of land vide deed No.451 of 1947 in favour of All Ahmed and on getting mutation in his name opened P.S. Khatian and depositing rents and taxes. Ali 4, Ahmed died leaving behind plaintiff Nos.7- 13 and Md. Ibrahim and accordingly their names were duly published in B.S. Khatian. Md. Ibrahim died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 1-6, Plaintiffs have been enjoying the property by depositing rents and taxes in respective offices and by construction of houses therein and other means. The defendants have threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them from the suit land on 14.03.2005 and as such the plaintiffs filed the instant suit. Accordingly the plaintiff prayed for declaration of title with a further prayer for an order of permanent injunction in the suit property. 

3. On the other hand, defendants by filing power entered their appearance and contested the suit denying the material allegations brought against the defendants and also prayed that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and bad for defect of parties and also barred by limitation; the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest in the suit land of Other Suit No.33 of 2007. Since the value of the suit land has been increased by leaps and bounds the original defendants on 14.03.2005 threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess and as such the plaintiffs finding no other alternative filed the Suit being No.32 of 2007 with a prayer for declaration of title and for permanent injunction and accordingly denied the material allegations in the Other Suit No.33 of 2007 since the suit is not maintainable in the present form and defect of parties and barred by limitation and as such the said suit shall stand dismissed. 

4. On the other hand, the short facts of Other Suit No.33 of 2007 are that, R.S. Khatian Nos.399 and 1045 were prepared in the name of Ali Hossain. Ali Hossain died leaving behind 3 sons, namely Ibrahim Khali @ Hachi MM, Mohammad Hossain and Mohammad Rafiq and one daughter Sakina Khatun and his wife, Nabijan Bibi. Ibrahim Khalil @ Hachi Mia died leaving behind 2 sons, 3 daughters and one wife i.e. defendant Nos.2-7, Sakina Khatun died leaving behind 2 daughters and 2 sons i.e. the defendant Nos.8-I I. All Hossain and his wife died issueless and their property was inherited by the plaintiffs of Other Suit No.33 of 2007. The plaintiffs of Other Suit No.33 of 2007 have been owning and possessing the suit land by planting, fishing and other means to the full knowledge of other persons. Thereafter on 02.02.2005 plaintiff No.1, Mohammad Rafiq went to deposit rents to the concerned office but to his utter despair he found that the names of other persons have been included in the B.S. Khatian and as such, the official denied to take the rents. Subsequently the plaintiffs obtained certified copy on 22.02.2005. However it is mentionable that they have been owning and possessing the suit land peacefully to the full knowledge of all though the names of strangers have been written mistakenly in the said Khatian. Wrongly record of R.S. Khatian has been prepared in collusion with predecessor of defendant Nos.l-6 Ibrahim Khalil and other defendants and accordingly the plaintiffs requested the defendants to make a Mukti Nama but with an ulterior motive they had been killing the valuable time and ultimately they refused to execute any sort of Mukti Nama and step aside from their erroneous. The plaintiffs filed the suit praying for declaration of title with correction of P.S. record on the other hand Other Suit No.33 of 2007 shall stand dismissed since the same is not maintainable and bad for defect of parties and barred by limitation with cost. 

5. Mr. Mantazuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant. On the other hand no one appears to contest the appeal. 

6. Mr. Mantazudding Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that, the judgment and decree of the trial Court are contrary to law, evidences on record and circumstances of the case are liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate for the appellant further submits that the learned Joint District Judge failed to appreciate the legal aspect of the case properly and thereby the finding and decision arrived at by the Court below are perverse and are liable to be set aside. He further submits that the finding of the learned Joint District Judge that " সুতরাং অপর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলার বাদীগণের নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে দখল নাই অপর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলায় বাদীপক্ষের স্বীকৃতি মতে বাংলাদেশ স্বাধীন হওয়ার পর থেকে অপর ৩২/০৭ নং মামলার বাদীগণ তথা অপর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলার বাদীগণ নালিশী সম্পত্তি দখল করিতেছে। উপযুক্ত পর্যালোচনান্তে নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে অপর ৩২/০৭ নং মামলার বাদীগণের নিরংেকুশ দখল আছে এবং অপর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলা বাদীগণের নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে তাহাদের স্বীকৃতমতে দখল নাই মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহন করা arrived wrongly and as such findings and decision to the effect that the suit is maintainable in the present form is also not tenable in law and as such the impugned judgment and decree so far not giving decree of title are liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate 'for the appellant also submits that the learned Joint District Judge has failed to consider the evidence on record as to cause of action in as much as the plaintiffs stated " মূল বিবাদীগণ ধনে-জনে বলিয়ান। সম্পত্তির মূল্য বৃদ্ধি পাওয়ায় বাদীগণের দুর্বল পাইয়া গায়ের জোরে অন্যায় ও বে-আইনীভাবে তপশীলের সম্পাত্তি হইতে বাদীগণকে বেদখল করার পায়তারা করিতেছে” The PW.I deposed on 26.09.2007 in Court and stated


that the defendants threatened to forcibly dispossess the plaintiffs about one and half year ago from the suit land and in view of such material evidence on record the findings “কোন তারিখের বিবাদীগণ বেদখলের হুমকি প্রদান করিয়াছে পি.ডব্লিউ-১ জমির আহমদ তাহার সাক্ষ্য সুনিদিষ্ট ভাবে বলিতে পারে নাই। based on no evidence and as such in not giving decree for declaration of title and permanent injunction erred in law and as such the impugned judgment and decree are liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate for the appellant also submits that the plaintiffs specifically made averments in the plaint that Ali Hossain and his sister Srimoti Achia Khatun executed the deed of sale on 26.10.1930 in favour of 2(two) brothers namely Abdul Motaleb and Ali Ahmed upon receipt of consideration money and handed over possession pursuant to deed and also handed over the deed to take step for admitting the same for registration but that sale deed could not be registered and the said deed kept in the custody of the predecessor of the plaintiff IL and PW-I produced the deed dated 26.10.1930 from their custody in Court, the learned Judge ought to have marked the same as Exhibit and should have passed a decree for declaration of title pursuant to the deed of sale itself as the plaintiffs are in possession but the learned Judge has not given the decree of declaration of title in spite of such evidence on record, thereby committed error of law in not decreeing the suit and the learned Joint District Judge has it committed illegally in coming to the finding- অপর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলার বাদীপক্ষ মামলাইট তামাদিতে বারিত মর্মে দাবী করিয়াছে। বাংলাদেশ স্বাধীন হওয়ার পর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলার বিবাদীগণ অপর ৩৩/০৭নং মামলার বাদীগণকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে বেদখল করিয়াছে। সুতরং তামাদি মেয়াদের মধ্যে অপর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলাটি দায়ের করা হয় নাই। সুতরাং অপর ৩৩/০৭ মামলাটি তামাদি বারিত মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহীত হইল 
 and dismissing the suit. The learned Advocate for the appellant then submits that the learned Joint District Judge illegally came to the finding “অপর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলার বাদীপক্ষ মামলাইট তামাদিতে বারিত মর্মে দাবী করিয়াছে। বাংলাদেশ স্বাধীন হওয়ার পর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলার বিবাদীগণ অপর ৩৩/০৭নং মামলার বাদীগণকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে বেদখল করিয়াছে। সুতরং তামাদি মেয়াদের মধ্যে অপর ৩৩/০৭ নং মামলাটি দায়ের করা হয় নাই। সুতরাং অপর ৩৩/০৭ মামলাটি তামাদি বারিত মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহীত হইল  and dismissed the suit on conjecture and surmises without proper scrutiny of the evidence on record. The learned Advocate for the appellant lastly submits that the learned Joint District Judge should have decreed the suit on the basis of his finding to the effect that the plaintiffs are in possession of the property on the basis of an unregistered deed for more than 70 years as contemplated under Section 53A of the Transfer of the Property Act i.e. to the rights under Section 53A of the Act and the judgment and decree are otherwise bad in law and as such are not maintainable in law and as such the impugned judgment and decree are not sustainable in law and the impugned judgment of the learned Joint District Judge suffered from legal perversity and legal infirmity and as such the same is liable to be set aside. 

7. Heard the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant perused the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court, perused the oral and documentary evidences as adduced by the PWs and DWs and also consider the submission as advanced by the learned Advocate advanced by the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant. 

8. We perused the deposition as adduced by PWs and DWs at the time of trial in support of their respective cases. Learned Advocate for the appellant in course of his submission draws our attention that the trial Court at the time of disposal of the suit failed to appreciate properly the legal aspect of the case and thereby the finding and decision arrived at by the trial Court are perverse and not in accordance with law. We find that the trial Court seriously erred in law in holding that the suit is not maintainable in the present form and also is not tenable in law. We find that the trial Court at the time of passing the impugned judgment and decree miserably failed to take into notice exhibit 2 i.e. A.S. Khatian No.399 and 1045, the certified copy of exhibit 3 and 3Ka and certified copy of B.S. Khatian No.1099 marked as exhibit 4 and rent receipt dated 12.3.1997 and 27.6.2005 which has been marked as exhibit 5 and 5Ka. The trial Court at the time of passing of the impugned judgment and decree did not at all take into consideration those exhibits and most illegally and erroneously dismissed the suit and the said erroneous observation and finding of the trial Court deserve interference under the appellate jurisdiction of this Court as the said erroneous finding of the trial Court cannot be sustainable in law and liable to be set aside. We also find that the trial Court at the time of disposal of the suit failed to consider the deposition of PW.1 and most illegally and arbitrarily passed the impugned judgment and decree which cannot be sustainable in law under any circumstances of the case.

9. We find the impugned judgment and 'appearing for the appellant decree of the trial Court suffers from serious miscarriage of justice as such non-consideration of oral and documentary evidences in passing the impugned judgment and decree is fatal which deserves our interference under the appellate jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court.  

10. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case we are of the view that the impugned judgment and decree dated 21.09.2008 passed in Other Suit No.32 of 2007 and 33 of 2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Chittagong deserves our interference. 

11. In the result, the appeal is hereby allowed with cost. 

12. The impugned judgment and decree dated 14.09.2008, 21.09.2008 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No.32 of 2007 heard analogously with Other Suit No.33 of 2007 are hereby set aside. Consequently both the suits are hereby decreed with cost against the defendant-response dents. 

13. Send down the lower Courts records along with a copy of this judgment to the concern Court immediately for information and necessary action.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. M. Enayetur Rahim, J:- Defendants have preferred this appeal being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 16.11.2005 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Thakurgaon in Money Suit No.01 of 2004 decreeing the suit. 

2. The present respondent as plaintiff instituted Money Suit No.] of 2003 in the 2' Court of Joint District Judge, Thakurgaon impleading the present appellants as defendants seeking the following reliefs: 

অতএব, বাদী প্রার্থনা করিতেছে যে, ক) ‘ক' তপশীল বর্ণিত “মেসার্স পীতালী ইলেক্ট্রনিক্স”নামীয় অংশীদারী ব্যবসা প্রতিষ্ঠানে বাদীর ১/২নং (অর্ধাৎশ) অংশ রহিয়াছে মর্মে যেযেণা পূর্বক অংশীদারী ব্যবসা প্রতিষ্ঠান “যেসার্স পীতালী
ইলেক্ট্রনিক্স” এর অংশীদার ভংগের ডিক্রী প্রদান করিতে; 

খ) ‘ক’তপশীল বর্ণিত “যেসার্স পীতালী ইলেক্ট্রনিক্স" নামীয় ব্যবসা প্রতিষ্ঠানে ১৯৯০-১৯৯১ইং সাল হইতে ১৯৯৮-১৯৯৯ সাল পর্যন্ত চুড়ান্ত হিসাব নিকাশ অন্তে বাদীর প্রাপ্য অর্ধাংশ টাকা পরিশোধিত টাকা বাদে  ৬,১৬,১৩৪/০০ টাকা আদায়ের জন্য ১নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রী দিতে;

গ) ‘ক’ তপশীল বর্ণিত “যেসার্স গীতালী ইলেক্ট্রনিক্স”নামীয় ব্যবসা প্রতিষ্ঠানে ১৯৯৯-২০০০ইং সাল হইতে ২০০৩ইং সালের জুন মাস পর্যন্ত হিসাব নিকাশ অন্তে বাদীর প্রাপ্য অধাৎশ টাকা বাবদ ১নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রী দিতে;

ঘ) তপশীল বর্ণিত যে'সার্স গীতালী ইলেক্ট্রনিক্স দোকানের ও গোডাউনের যাবতীয় অস্থাবর মালামাল সমূহের একটি তালিকা (ইনভেন্টরী) প্রস্তুত করিবার নিমিত্ত একজন এডভোকেট কমিশনার নিয়োগত্রুমে উক্ত অস্থাবর মালামালের
হিসাব বিবরণী ও মূল্যঘানের বিবরণী দাখিল করিবার নিমিত্ত যথাযথ আদেশ দিতে; 

ঙ) অত্র আদালত ব্যয়ে বাদীর অনুহুলে এবং বিবাদীর প্রতিকুলে ডিক্রী দিতে;

চ) আইন ও ইকুইটি মতে যাহা প্রতিকার পাইতে হকদার তাহাও ডিক্রী দিবার আদেশ দিতে;

	3. The plaintiff's case, in short is that the plaintiff and defendant No. 1having been friendly relationships for a long time at one stage they were agreed to run a partnership business. Accordingly, they had entered into a partnership agreement on 01.01.98 B.S. In the agreement dated 01.01.1998 B.S. it was stipulated that the plaintiff would have given Taka 80,001/- as the capital of the business and the shop premises of the defendants would be treated as their capital; the defendant No. 1 would manage, supervise their business and he would also be liable for other business related affairs like purchase and sell of the goods etc.; the bank account would be operated by the defendant No.1 and after ending of the every Bengali year the loss and profit of the business would be accounted and the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 would be liable for loss and profit in equal share; the parties were debarred to transfer their respective share to third party and if one of the party would not agree to remain as partner of the business, he would have given a 6(six) months’ notice on the other side but in no case within S years the parties could not be entitled to dissolve the business or demand his respective share or profit. Plaintiff gave Taka 80,001/- to the defendant No. 1 as the capital of the business and the defendant No. 1 after receiving the said money started business in the shop premises of the defendants, which was their paternal property. They started partnership business installing signboard under the name and style as M/s. Gitaly Electronics. The defendant No. 1 being a teacher of a Government Primary School, he had been carrying on the business by appointing employees since 01.01.1398 B.S. in the shop premises, while they were carrying on business of various electronics goods like Watch, Clock, Radio, Tape recorder and Casset, within a shod period their business had been developing day by day. The defendant No. 1 used to take money from the plaintiff beside the capital money for the business and the defendant No. 1 also repaid the same. The defendant No.1, from the profit of the business, used to pay the salary of the employees of the shop, electricity bill, municipality tax and other business related expenditures. The defendant No. 1 at his own will used to prepare the accounts and maintain the stock register of the goods of the shop and when the plaintiff asked him to show the accounts and stock register, the defendant No. 1 all the times avoided to show accounts and stock register on this or that plea and in this may the defendant No.1 had passed so many years. As per the terms of the agreement the plaintiff did not take any step against the said illegal activities of the defendant No.1 within 5(five) years. The plaintiff on so many occasions requested the defendant No. 1for accounts but the defendant No.1did not pay any heed to the plaintiffs such request. The defendant No. 1paid Taka 1,54,200/, as profit of the business to the plaintiff in different occasions in between the year 1990-1991 to 1998-1999 and through a cheque the defendant No.1 also gave Taka 80,000/- in the year 2001 and the defendant No. 1gave in total Taka 2,34,200/- to the plaintiff up to the year 2002 as business profit, which is much lesser than he was entitled. The plaintiff when finally asked the defendant No.1 to give him the accounts and demanded ‘টালী খাতা’ the account for day to day business, stock register and other business documents, then the defendant No.1 on 28.09.2001 supplied him an account containing 22 page without giving the full account, stock register and necessary documents regarding purchase and sell of goods. The said account was incomplete one and nothing was mentioned about total amount of purchase of goods and selling of goods, Eventually the plaintiff examined the said account, supplied by the defendant No.1, by a Chartered Accountant firm, at Dhaka and after auditing those it was found that after starting, their business up to 1998-1999 financial year the gross profit was Taka 17,00,608/- and the plaintiff was entitled to get it's 50% i.e. Taka 8,50,304/-and as the defendant No.1 paid Taka 2,34,200/-, the plaintiff is entitled to get the rest amount of profit of Taka 6,16,134/-. The defendant No.1 agreed to pay the said money. But ultimately he denied paying the same and in such circumstances plaintiff sent a legal notice to the defendant No.1 demanding his profit as he was entitled. In reply to the said notice the defendant No.1 disclosed that in the shop in question, his younger brother defendant No.2 had been doing business. The defendants were trying to grab the partnership business and in that situation it became necessary to dissolve the partnership business. Since the defendant No.1 did not pay any heed to the legal notice of the plaintiff, the plaintiff was compelled to institute the present suit.

4. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. In the written statement it was contended that under compelling circumstances the  defendants agreed to do a partnership business with the plaintiff; it was agreed between them that the defendant would have given their paternal shop premises for the business of electronic goods and the said shop premises would be treated as the capital of the defendants and the plaintiff accepted the said proposal; defendant No. 1receipt Taka 80,001/- from the plaintiff as his capital and they started business in the shop premises; one Satyajit Nag was the representative of the plaintiff; the defendant No. 1maintained the accounts, stock register and other business related documents and the plaintiff was impressed to see the such activities of him. Subsequently the defendants came to know that Satyajit Nag was the partner of the plaintiff and Taka 80,001.00 was given as capital money by both of them. The agreement was ended on 31.12,1402 B.S, that is in the year 1995-1996 and in between that period, gross profit of business was Taka 2,39,399/- out of which the plaintiff and the defendant would get taka 1.19,699/- each and the plaintiff already had received Taka 29,200/- in different occasion. Thereafter at the instance of the well-wisher of both the parties they agreed to continue the partnership business on verbal agreement. Subsequently misunderstanding arose between the plaintiff and Satyajit Nag and Satyajit Nag left the plaintiff and plaintiff's brother became the sells man of the shop. When the partnership business was going on, on the basis of verbal agreement the plaintiff in the middle of the year 2001 disclosed to the defendants that he would not continue the partnership business and he demanded his share of profit including the 50% goods of the shop. The defendants ultimately agreed to pay the dues to the plaintiff, as he was entitled to get and in presence of the representative of the plaintiff on 28.09.2001 an account was prepared from 19.07.1990 to September, 2001. As per the said account gross profit was Taka 9.08,036/- and total expenditure was Taka 4,42,9£15/- and deducting the other various expenditure the profit was Taka 4,15,33E- out of which the plaintiff was entitled to get Taka 2,07,665.50. Out of Taka 2,07,665.50 the plaintiff on different occasions received taka 1,04,589/- and the rest due amount of profit of taka 1,03,076/-. When the plaintiff demanded the said money, under a compelling circumstances the defendants executed a deed in favour of the plaintiff as “হাওলাত নামার অঙ্গিকারনামা” and thereafter on different occasion within 14 months they paid Taka 70,000/- to the plaintiff. After receiving the said amount suddenly the plaintiff stopped to take further amount and by a legal notice through his learned Advocate demanded more money, having no basis. The defendant also returned back the capital money amounting to taka 80,000/- given by the plaintiff. The plaintiff all the times putting his signature had received money and he never raised any objection regarding the day to day accounts, yearly accounts prepared by the defendants. The plaintiff had managed to obtain an audit report from a Chartered Accountant, which has got no legal basis and had been claiming illegal money from the defendants. The said audit report in fact is not prepared by the Chartered Accountant on the basis of the “টালী খাতা” stock register and other document of the business and on the basis of the said report the suit cannot be decreed as prayed by the plaintiff. The plaintiff making false claim for illegal gain instituted the suit and the same was liable to be dismissed with costs. 

5. The learned Joint District Judge considering the pleadings of the respective parties framed as many as 5(five) issues. The plaintiff to prove its claim examined 4(four) witnesses and also adduced documentary evidence, which were marked as exhibits 1-9. On the other hand the defendants also examined 3(three) witnesses in support of their case and also adduced documentary evidence which were marked as exhibits Ka-Gha series. 

6. The learned Joint District Judge after hearing of the suit by judgment and decree dated 16.11.2005 decreed the suit declaring the plaintiff's 50% share in the partnership business under the name and style M/s. Gitaly Electronics and also passed a decree dissolving the partnership. The learned Joint District Judge also decreed for a sum of Take 10,96,017/- in favour of the plaintiff as the profit of the business from the year 1990-1991 to 2002-2003 including the capital money given by the plaintiff. 

7. Against the said judgment and decree the defendants have preferred this appeal. 

8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan and Mr. Shishir Kanti Majumder appeared for the defendant appellants. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan in his submission referring section 69 sub-section 3(a) of the Partnership Act has conceded that the present suit for dissolution of partnership business is maintainable, though it is not a registered firm. He also submits that section 69 of the partnership Act prohibits suit by a-partner of an unregistered firm against another partner or against the firm itself but the exception is sub-section 3(a) of section 69 is to this general provision, providing for suit by a partner-of a firm for dissolution of a firm or for accounts of dissolved firm, but the learned Joint District Judge acted illegally in decreeing the suit violating the Provision of Order XX, rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that as per provision of the said law the court can pass a preliminary decree for dissolution of a partnership and thereafter direct for accounts but the learned Joint District Judge relying on the exhibit-2, the audit report, which was procured by the plaintiff privately, passed a decree for an amount of taka 10,96,017.00 and thereby erred in law in decreeing the suit without holding any account as per law and the decree is a nullity in the eye of the law and the same is liable to be set aside. To substantiate his contention he refers the case of Md. Abdul Jabber Sarkar-Vs- Md. Mabud Bux and another, reported in 7 PLR Dhaka, page-23. Mr. Shishir Kanti Majumder, learned Advocate for the appellant drew our attention to exhibit-2, the r audit report and exhibit-Kha, that is the accounts of the partnership business, maintained by the defendants and show us the discrepancies between the two documents particularly in determining the loss and profit of the business. 

9. On the other hand Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, and Mr. Abdus Saturn Mondal, learned Advocates appeared for the plaintiff respondent. Mr. Ali submits that in decreeing the suit dissolving the partnership firm the learned Joint District Judge did not commit any error of law. However, he concedes with the submission of Mr. Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate of the appellant, that the Court should have pass a preliminary decree for dissolution of partnership business as per Provision of Order XX rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereafter direct for accounts. 

10. We appreciate the submission and attitude of the learned Advocate of both the parties. 

11. In the instant case the partnership business on the basis of an unregistered document is admitted by both the parties. In view of the said admission, the plaintiff is entitled to get a preliminary decree for a declaration that he is a partner in the business in question and for dissolution of partnership business. 

12. Order XX, rule 15 of the Code of Civil procedure runs as follows: 

"Where a suit is for the dissolution of a partnership, or the taking of partnership accounts, the Court, before passing a final decree, may pass a preliminary decree declaring the proportionate shares of the parties, .fixing the, clay on which the partnership shall stand dissolved or he deemed to have been dissolved, and directing such accounts to be taken, and other acts to be done, as it thinks, fit." 

13. From a plain reading of the impugned judgment and decree it appears to us that the learned Joint District judge passed the same beyond the scope of Order XX, rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Said law clearly contemplates that before dissolution of a partnership or taking of partnership accounts, before passing a final decree court may pass a preliminary decree declaring the proportionate shares of the parties, fixing the date of which the partnership shall stand dissolve or be deemed to have been dissolved and directing such account to be taken and other acts to be done the Court thinks fit. But in passing the impugned judgment and decree the learned Joint District Judge without passing any preliminary decree and taking account straight way relying on a procured audit report by the plaintiff, exhibit-2, has determined the profit of the business and the share of the respective parties and decreed for an amount of taka 10,96,017/- in favour of the plaintiff. 
14. From exhibit-2, the audit report, it appears that P.W.2, Tofayel Ahmed, the Chartered Accountant made remark to the effect: 

“ব্যবসায়ের দৈনন্দিন ক্রয়-বিক্রয়ের সমর্থনে ব্যবহৃত টালী খাতা সমূহ (বৎসর অনুযায়ী) মজুত মানের 
বিবরণীর সমর্থন যোগ্য ক্যাশ মেমো, চালান, দলিল দস্তাবেজ ইত্যাদি নির্ধারণের জন্য উপস্থাপন করা হলে সংশোধিত লাভ/লোকসানের বিপরীতে নির্ধারিত প্রতিবেদন এর Supplement করা যেতে পারে ৷”

P.W.2, Tofayel Ahmed in his cross-examination admitted to the effect:

“১৯৯৫-৯৬ইং সনে মাল ক্রয় বাবদ দেখানো হয়েছে ৭, ৭৫,২১৬/০০ টাকা ৷ আর আমার প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখ
রয়েছে ৫,৯৫,৪১৬/0০' এবং ১৯৯৬-৯৭ইং ��নে পাতায় উল্লেখ আছে মাল ক্রয় বাবদ ৭,৩৩,২৬২/০০ টাকা ৷ আর আমার প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখ রয়েছে ৫,৯১,৬৩০/০০ টাকা এবং ১৯৯৭-৯৮ইং সনে খাতায় মাল ক্রয় বাবদ উল্লেখ আছে ৮,০২,৫৯৪/০০ টাকা আর আমার প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখ রয়েছে ৬,২০,8 8 ০/০০ টাকা এবং ১৯৯৮-৯৯ইং সনে পাতায় মাল ক্রয় বাবদ উল্লেখ আছে ৭,২৩,৫8১/০০ টাকা এবং আর আমার প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখ রয়েছে  ৫,০৭,৫৯8/০০ টাকা ৷ কোন ফার্মের “১”বৎসরের হিসাব নিকাশের ভিত্তিতে Gross Profit আসবে “৯” বৎসরের হিসাব নিকাশের Gross Profit একই রকম হবে না। পক্ষ কর্তৃক দাখিলী পাতায় ১৯৯০-৯১ইং সনের কোন পরিবহন খরচ লিখা হয় নাই ৷ ঐ পাতায় ১৯৯১-৯২ইং সনের এবং ১৯৯২-৯৩ইং সনের এবং ১৯৯৩-৯8ইং সনের এবং ১৯৯৩-৯8ইং সনের এবং ১৯৯8-৯৫ইং সনের এবং ১৯৯৫-৯৬ইং সনের এবং ১৯৯৬-৯৭ইং সনের এবং ১৯৯৭-৯৮ইং সনের এবং পরিবহন খরচ লিখা আছে ৷ আমি তা আমার অডিট রিপোর্ট ডিলিট করে দেখায়াছি ৷ ঐ টাকাটা আমি খরচ হিসাবে দেখায়াছি ৷ আমি ৯ বৎসরের হিসাব একত্রে করি নাই ৷ আমি বৎসর বৎসর হিসাব করেছি ৷ যদি আমার হিসাবের ৯ বৎসরের মাল বিক্রয়ের টাকা একত্রে যোগ করা হয় তাহলে তা ৭০,১৬,৬8৩/০০ টাকা হবে কিনা তা আমি সময় নিয়ে যোগ না করে এখন বলতে পারব না ৷ যদি ১৯৯৮-৯৯ইং সনের মজুদ মালের ২,৯৮,৭৫২/০০ টাকা উক্ত ৭০,১৬,৬৪৩/০০ টাকার সহিত যোগ করা হয় তা হলে তা ৭২,৩৫,৫৯৫/০০ টাকা হবে কিনা তা এখন আমি যোগ না করে বলতে পারব না। 

In view of the above evidence and 4 materials on record it is crystal clear that exhibit-2, the audit report is not a conclusive account of the business in question and same is also a biased, incomplete report and suffers from inconsistency and as such the learned Joint District Judge acted illegally in decreeing the suit for an amount of Taka 10,96,017.00 relying on the said procured audit report and same cannot be sustained. 

15. Although in Order xx rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure the language has been used as 'may pass a preliminary decree' but if we read the entire provision of above law as a whole and consider the scheme of the said law, it would be clear that passing a preliminary decree is mandatory before taking account. We have no hesitation to hold that the impugned judgment and decree is passed beyond the scope of order 20, Rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure and same is without jurisdiction and a nullity in the eye of law. 

16. In the case of Gulab Thai —Vs- Shibba Mal and another, reported in AIR 1937, All 674 it has been observed: 

"Whether the firm is dissolved by a decree of court or otherwise, the dissolution can never be complete unless the accounts of the firm are settled." 

In that case it has been further held that the right for accounts in a suit for dissolution of a firm is not an account of any provision of section 69 of the Partnership Act nor because the dissolution is not complete unless the accounts are settled, but because of the provision in Order xx rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure, Court may grant it. 

17. Once a suit for dissolution of a partnership is filed it will attract the operation of Order xx, rule 15 of the Code of Civil procedure under which the Court is quite competent to grant necessary relief as contemplated in that rule. Prayer for determination of shares and for accounts are not implicit in the prayer for dissolution, but under order xx, rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Court may grant it. 

18. In view of the above discussion we are also of the view that learned Joint District Judge failed to understand the purport and scope of order xx rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure and proceeded with the case in a wrong way. 

19. In the instant case partnership business is admitted and in view of the provision of section 69 and sub-section 3(a) of the Partnership Act the present suit for dissolution of partnership is maintainable as conceded by the learned Advocate of the defendant-appellants relying on the decision reported in 7 PLR Dacca, Page-23. On the other hand learned Advocate of the plaintiff respondent has also conceded that a proper accounting as per provision of Order XX rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure is required to be prepared. In view of the above position of the respective parties, it is not at all necessary to discuss the evidence of the respective parties afresh to determine whether there was any partnership business between the parties and to determine the accounts. 

20. Having discussed as above we are inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. We send the case back on remand to the trial Court to pass a preliminary decree on the basis of the evidence available on the record in the light of the provision of Order xx, rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure determining the date on which the partnership shall stand dissolve or deem to be dissolved and thereafter by appointing an accountant knowing person, preferably an agreed person by the parties, direct to prepare accounts and on the basis of such accounts final decree be passed. It is to be mentioned here that in the instant case profit of the parties are admittedly equal that is 50% 50%. 

21. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 16.11.2005 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Thakurgaon in Money Suit No.01 of 2004 is hereby set aside. The suit is sent back on remand to the trial court with the observation made in the body of this judgment. 

22. Send down the lower Court records at once.

End.
