full_judgment:
Mr. Sharif Uddin Chaklader, J:  This rule, at the instance of applicants-petitioners, 
directed against judgment and order No.14 dated 13.06.2011 passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, 4th  Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.12 of 2011 arising out of Artha Execution Case No.01 of 2011 arising out of judgment and decree dated 01.06.2010 passed in Artha Rin Suit No.149 of 2009 pending in the Artha Rin Adalat, 4th  Court, Dhaka by which an 
application under Order XXI Rule 58 and 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the 3rd  party petitioners was rejected. 

2. lamina Bank Limited filed Artha Rin Case No.300 of 2008 before the learned 
District Judge, Dhaka and subsequently renumbered as Artha Rin Case No.149 of 2009 when transferred to Artha Rin Adalat, 40 Court, Dhaka for realization of Tk. 18,23,59,000/- against defendant opposite party Nos.1 and 3-8. On contested hearing against defendant No.2, some of the defendants did not contest. Decree was passed on 25.05.2010 and Money Execution Case being Artha Zari Case No.01 of 2011 was filed on 01.06.2010. 

3. 30 party petitioners filed present Miscellaneous case on 14.04.2011 stating that the decree was passed against wrong person and 3' party petitioners is actual owner of the suit property and decree was passed fraudulently on the averments made in the plaint. The court fixed date after date in taking step for submitting schedule as per Section 32(2) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain which having not been filed or submitted the case was dismissed. 

4. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali with Mr. Sadananda Rana, learned Advocates, appearing for the applicants-petitioners, on reference to the case of Mollah Shahidul Islam Vs. Monsur Rahman, 57 DLR 164 = 21 BLD 171 submits that, fraud has been alleged having been pleaded and exposed, as security or assurance as contemplated under 32(2) of the Ain are not required to furnish or deposited. 

5. We have gone through the cited decision wherein it is held as:- 
"The only question which falls for our consideration is whether the petitioner is required to furnish any security as envisaged under Section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 even in the event of an application being filed under Order XXI, Rule 90 and 91 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 is in the following lerms :- 
“জারীর বিরুদ্ধে আপত্তি-(১) অর্থঋণ আদালতের ডিক্রি বা আদেশ হইতে উদ্ভূত জারি মামলায় কোন তৃতীয়পক্ষ দেওয়ানী কার্যবীধী আইনে বিধান মতে দাবি পেশ করিলে আদালত প্রাথমিক বিবেচনায় উক্ত দাবী সরাসরি খারিজ না করিলে ডিক্রিদার অনুর্ধ্ব ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে উহার বিরুদ্ধে লিখিত আপত্তি দায়ের করিয়া শুনানী দাবি করিতে পারিবেন।
(২)উপরিউক্ত মতে দাবি পেশ করিবার ক্ষেত্রে দরখাস্ত কারী ডিক্রিকৃত অর্থের ২৫% এর সমপরিমান জামানত দাখিল করিবে এবং অনুরুপ জামানাত দাখিল না করিলে দাবি অগ্রাহ্য হইবে।”

From the language in which the said section is couched it would appear that only the claim of the 3"1 party would attract the provision of sub-section (2) and under the provision of Civil Procedure Code that claim is only dealt with under Order XXI Rule 58 of the 
Ors Vs. Govt. of Bangladesh & Ors 23BLI(HCD) 2015 Code of Civil Procedure. The investigation of claim and only objection to that claim are dealt with by rule 58 to rule 62 and beyond that no third party's claim is conceivable under any provision of Order XXI. The provision of investigation of claims and objections has been clearly provided under the aforesaid rules under heading 'investigation of claims and objections' and the claim is preferred when the• property is under the attachment. The petitioner in the instant case although apparently made claim over the property auction sold, but in substance they have challenged the auction sale proceeding on the ground of fraud. So the kind of claim that has been preferred does not come within the ambit of rule 58 of Order XXI of the CPC. It is further indicated in sub-section ( I ) of Section 32 of the Ain, 2003 that the decree holder also may file objection within the period not exceeding 30 days and can claim hearing for disposal of the claim made by the 3"I party. Therefore, the contemplation of the legislature in Section 32(2) is the investigation of claims and objection as provided under Order XXI, Rule 58 not beyond the periphery of rule 58, and since the petitioner filed the petition under Order XXI Rule 90 and 91 for setting aside the sale on the ground of fraud they are not required furnish any security as provided under subsection 2 of Section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The teamed Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat appeared to have exercised his power and jurisdiction beyond the law." 

6. Since this judgment covers the case before our hand squirrelly, we are of the 
view that any type of security in any manner is not required. We find substance in the rule. 

7. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. 

8. The judgment complained is set aside. Learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Court No.4, Dhaka is directed to proceed with the case in accordance with law. We further directing the learned Judge to dispose of Miscellaneous Case No.12 of 2011 arising out of Artha Rin Case No.149 of 2009 within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this order without giving any unnecessary adjournment to any party. 

9. Communicate this order at once. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Ashraful Alam. Advocate -- for the Petitioner 
Mr. Shamsuddin Babul with Mr. Kanai Lal Shaha Advocates -- For the Opposite Parties

Versus

full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, J:-This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties no. 1 to 7 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 15.09.2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge. 2nd Court. Comilla in Miscellaneous Appeal no. 28 of 2001 affirming the judgment and order dated 30.04.2001 passed in Miscellaneous Case no. 01 of 2000 by the learned Additional Senior Assistant Judge (In Charge) rejecting the case as not maintainable under order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be set aside and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, are that, the opposite parties no. 1 to 7 as plaintiffs instituted partition Suit no. 186 of 1986 in the court of Munsif, 3rd court. Comilla which was subsequently renumbered as partition suit No. 82 of 1991 in the said suit the plaintiff impleaded Aheda Khatuun, the predecessor of the present petitioners, as defendant no. 18. After hearing the contesting parties the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Comilla, dismissed the suit. 

3. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 207 of 1992 in the Court of learned District Judge, Comilla. After contested hearing, the learned District Judge allowed the appeal and decreed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 4.5.1996 Against the said judgment and decree, the contesting defendants preferred revisional application being Civil Revision no. 3866 of 1998 before this division wherein the order of the learned District Judge has been affirmed. Thereafter the predecessor of these petitioners, Aheda Khatun, defendant no. 18 of the partition suit, filed Miscellaneous Case no. 1 of 2000 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Comilla under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that she is a co-sharer in the suit schedule land but no notice/ summons of the Partition Suit and Title Appeal was served upon her. In the said miscellaneous case the contesting opposite parties no.1-7 without submitting any written statement filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure contending inter-alia that the partition Suit no. 82 of 1991 being dismissed the plaintiff opposite parties as appellants preferred Title Appeal no. 207 of 1992 in the Court of District Judge, Comilla. After hearing the contesting parties, the learned District Judge allowed The appeal by setting aside the judgment passed by the learned senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Comilla and decreed the suit which was ultimately affirmed by the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. It has also been stated that the original decree being merged with the decree of the appellate court, the miscellaneous case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable as barred by law. The petitioner of The Miscellaneous case filed an application under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Both the applications were heard together and after hearing the parties the trial court rejected the application under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding that the judgment of the trial court and appellate court below has been merged with the judgment passed in Civil revision no. 3866 of 1998. The relevant portion is quoted herein under:
“ফলে দৃশতঃ নিম্ন ও নিষ্ম আপীল আদালতের রায মহামান্য হাই কোটের রায় দ্বারা Absorve হইয়া গিয়াছে। ফলে নিম্ন আদালতের রায়ে কোন অস্তিত্ব নাই। সে ক্ষেত্রে আপীল আদালতের রায়ের পর দেওয়ানী কার্যাবিধি ৯ আদেশ ১৩ নিয়ম প্রযোগে আপীল আদালতের  রায় ডিক্রি রদ রহিতের আিইনতঃ কোন সুযোগ নাই।
Against the order, the petitioners preferred Miscellaneous Appeal no. 28 of 2001 in the court of District Judge, Comilla which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Comilla, After hearing the parties, the learned Additional District Judge, Comilla disallowed the miscellaneous appeal and thereby affirmed the order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional court, Comilla. In the said backdrop, the present petitioners heirs of Abeda Khatun (defendant no. 18 of the partition suit) moved this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before this division and obtained the present Rule. 

4. Mr. Md. Ashraful Alain. the learned advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not a plaint and as such the Additional Joint District Judge committed an error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order holding that the miscellaneous case order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is barred by law under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his submission, the learned Advocate referred the case of Harunor Rashid Talukder Vs Md. Mahbubur Rahman Talukder and others, reported in 1 MI.R(AD) 286. 

5. Mr. Md. Shamusddin Babul along with Mr. Kanai Lai Shaha, the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party nos. land 2 in support of impugned Judgment submits that the opposite parties filed application under order 7 Rule 11 read with section 151 of Code of Civil procedure and the learned Additional District Judge passed the impugned Judgment and order invoking section 151 of the Code of Civil procedure which provides inherent power of the court and as such the appellate court below did not commit any error of law. 

6. Heard the learned advocates at length, perused the revisional application, lower court's record and the decision cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

7. On perusal of the record it appears that the defendant no. 18 of the partition suit filed Miscellaneous Case no.1 of 2000 under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil procedure stating that she is a Co-sharer of the suit schedule land but the plaintiff without serving any summon notice upon her filed an application in the suit praying for exemption from service of summon upon her and obtained an order beyond her knowledge, It has also been stated that she was not at all aware of the proceedings of the Partition Suit no. 186 of 1986 which was renumbered as Partition Suit no. 82 of 1991 and also the proceedings of Title Appeal no. 207 of 1992. It has been further stated that notice/summon of the Title Appeal no. 207 of 1992 was also not served upon her. 

8. The application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure being not a plaint, application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil procedure shall not apply. Therefore, The trial court has committed an error of law in entertaining the application filed by the plaintiffs under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The appellate court below also failed to notice this legal aspect of the case in affirming the order passed by the trial court rejecting the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The findings of the trial court as well as the lower appellate court that the decree of the trial court has been merged with the appellate court is factually wrong inasmuch as the suit was decreed by the appellate court. Even if, assuming but not conceding, the contention of the opposite parties accepted that the judgment of the appellate court below has311been affirmed by the revisional court and thus the suit was finally decreed that may be applicable in the case of the contesting defendants but so far the petitioner of the miscellaneous case is concerned, she having alleged that summons of the suit was suppressed and the decree was obtained fraudulently, she is not binding by the decree passed by the appellate court below is accepted, in that case, the defendant-petitioner shall be without may remedy and the plaintiffs shall be allowed to enjoy the benefit of the decree obtained beyond her knowledge and thereby she will be deprived of her fundamental and legal right to enjoy the property as an admitted co-share. 

9. It is settled Principle of law that a proceeding under section 151 of the Code of Civil procedure cannot be taken when there are other remedies available for securing the redress in the case of punjab Ali Pramanik and others Vs. Mohd. Mokarram Hossain reported in 29 DLR(Sc) 185 our apex Court held:
 "Where specific relief is available, inherent power of Courts under Section 151 of the Code cannot be invoked." 
Therefore, I find no other alternative but to interfere with the impugned order. However, I make it very clear that the decree passed by the appellate court below as affirmed by the revisional court shall be binding upon the contesting defendants as well as upon the plaintiffs and the application filed by the petitioner of the miscellaneous case in any way shall not affect the decree so far as it relates to the contesting-defendants and the plaintiffs. 

10. With the above observation the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

 11. The impugned order dated 15.9.2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge. Comilla affirming the order dated 30.4.2001 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Comilla is hereby set aside. 

12. The trial court is directed to entertain the application filed by the defendant no. 18 as petitioner under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and dispose of the same on merit in accordance with law after notifying the parties concerned. 

13. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. 

14. Send down the lower court's record at once.

End.

lawyer: Mr. Mirza Hossain Haider For the Petitioner. No one for the opposite parties.
parties:
Kalidas Dev ------ petitioners.
Versus
Babul Chandra Chakrabarty (Agradani) and others ------ opposite party.
full_judgment:
Mr. Muhammad Ansar Ali, J:- This Rule arises out of an application by defendant-petitioner under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.5.86 passed by the learned District Judge, Jamalpur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 121 of 1985 confirming the judgment and order dated 28.11.85 passed by the learned Munsif, First Court, Jamalpur rejecting an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Misc. Case No. 37 of 1985 for setting aside an ex parte decree dated 3.6.85 passed by the learned Munsif in Other Class Suit No. 32 of 1984.

2. Short facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are as follows:-

The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid Other Class Suit No. 32 of 1984 in the First Court Munsif, Jamalpur on 4.3.84 against one Priyabala Debi predecessor of the defendant-petitioner and 3 others for permanent injunction in respect of .13 acre of land of C. S. Plot No. 53 Mouza Kursha Kongarpara within Sadar P. S. and District Jamalpur and also there was a prayer for temporary injunction. The case of the plaintiff-opposite parties was that the predecessor of the present petitioner, Priyabala Debi was a stranger to the suit-land and she had purchase .08 acre of land with a C. I. sheet but from the co-sharer of the plaintiffs and thereafter filed a partition suit being Partition Suit No. 148 of 1970 in the Court of 1st Munsif, Jamalpur and she being a stranger was not entitled to any joint possession in the suit land with the plaintiffs but still she tried to go into the possession of the suit land forcibly. Hence the suit for permanent injunction.

3. The said defendant Priyabala Debi, predecessor of the present petitioner filed a written statement to contest the suit contending inter alia that she filed a partition suit being Partition Suit No. 148 of 1970 and got a preliminary decree which was subsequently made final on 18.6.74 and she got possession of her share amicably. But subsequently the plaintiff-opposite parties forcibly dispossessed her from some portion of her share; that during the pendency of the aforesaid suit, the defendant Priyabala Debi interstate and on her death the petitioner was made a party in the suit on 10.4.85 by way of substitution. Thereafter the suit proceeded and 15.5.85 was fixed for hearing but on the date upon the prayer of the defendant, 3.6.85 was fixed for pre-emptory hearing of the suit. The defendant-petitioner on the date fell seriously ill and could not appear in court and as a result the suit was taken up for ex parte hearing and ultimately decreed ex parte by the learned Munsif. The defendant petitioner thereafter having recovered from his illness filed an application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the ex parte decree and for restoration of the suit to its original file and number. The application was registered as Misc. Case No. 37 of 1985. The defendant-petitioner examined 3 witnesses including himself as P.W. 1 and the doctor who made her treatment as P. W. 3 in support of his case and the plaintiff opposite-parties jointly filed a written objection to contest the Misc. Case and examined one witness i. e. the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 as O. P. W. 1. The learned Munsiff after hearing the Misc. Case and on consideration of the materials on record dismissed the Misc. Case on contest by an order dated 28.11.85 on a finding that the defendant failed to prove his alleged illness on the date of hearing of the suit on 3.6.85. The defendant-petitioner being aggrieved by the said judgment from the learned Munsif filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 121 of 1985 before the learned District Judge, Jamalpur. After the hearing both the sides the learned District Judge was pleased to dismiss the same on contest and affirmed the judgment and order of the learned Munsif of similar finding by his judgment and order dated 26.5.86. Thereafter the defendant-petitioner moved the instant application in this court and obtained the present Rule. It may be mentioned that in spite of due service of notice of the rule upon the plaintiff-opposite parties there is no appearance on their behalf to oppose the Rule.

4. Mr. Mirza Hossain Haider, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioner submits that both the courts below have committed serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision and occasioning a failure of justice is not setting aside the ex parte decree in as much as the same was passed without complying with the mandatory provisions of law that means without being satisfied as to whether the legal requirements for passing the ex parte decree in the absence of the defendants were fulfilled or not. While elaborating his argument, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has drawn my attention to the provision of order 9 rules 6 as well as those of order 20 rules 4(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The relevant portion of order 9 rule 6 reads thus:

Rule 6: Where the plaintiff appears and the defendant does not appear when the suit is called on for hearing, then

(a) if it is proved that the summons was duly served the court may proceed ex parte;

(b)  ------

(c)  ------

(d)  ------

From the above it appears that in the absence of the defendant if summons is found to have been duly served upon him, the Court may proceed ex parte. It does not say that the court must necessarily pass an ex parte decree in absence of the defendants. Rather the Court may decree or dismiss the suit ex parte according to the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record. Order 20 rule 4 sub-rule (2) speaks of contents of a judgment and the same is as follows:-

"Judgments of other Courts shall contain a concise statement of the case, the points for determination, the decision thereon, and the reasons for such decision." Again rule (5) of the said order goes further to state the following:-

"5. In suits in which issues hart been framed, the Court shall state its finding or decision, with the reasons therefore, upon each separate issue."

5. Now, from a plain reading of the aforesaid provisions of law it appears that there are some legal requirements in passing a judgment whether ex parte or otherwise. In the instant case it appears that the lower appellate court has failed to examine the propriety of the impugned order dated 3.6.85 of the learned Munsif from the above angle and has only confined itself to the question of sufficient cause preventing the defendant-petitioner from appearing in the Court on the date fixed for hearing of the suit. Hence it is contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the learned District Judge has committed serious error of law in upholding the order of the learned Munsif and the ex parte decree and the same has cause a failure of justice. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has relied on a decision in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Israil Ali and others reported in 1981 B. S. C. R., vol.- V(AD), 222, wherein it has been laid down by their Lordships that.

"The trial Court again committed an error of procedure in not complying with the mandatory provisions. It has only been stated that P. W. 1 was examined. Exts. 1- 2(d), 2-2(b) and 3-3(1) marked and the plaintiffs case proved. This does not at all satisfy the legal requirements nor is it possible from reading the judgment, that the trial Court at all applied judicial mind; whether the plaintiffs witnesses and papers proved the plaintiffs case.... The findings recorded by the trial Court neither satisfied the legal requirements nor from such finding the alleged case of the plaintiffs was proved."

The learned Advocate has also relied on another decision in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Abdul Wadud and others reported in 25 D. L. R. (SC), 90, wherein it has been laid down as follows :

The plaint is no evidence for the proof of the case of the plaintiff. The absence of the defendant who asked for adjournment but refused on reasons assigned thereof cannot give occasion for the plaintiff to obtain ex parte decree without producing the relevant documents on the basis of which relief is sought for. The Court is bound to apply its mind with reference to the pleadings and satisfy itself as to what should be the proper proof for passing a decree on the basis of the averments made in the plaint."

5. In the instant case, the learned Munsif refused the defendants prayer for adjournment of the hearing and passed the following ex parte judgment and decree on 3.6.85 :-

“বাদীপক্ষ পাঁচ ব্যক্তি নামীয় একখানা হাজিরা দাখিলা করিয়া কোর্টে উপস্থিত আছেন। ১ নং বিবাদীপক্ষ সময়ের প্রার্থনায় একখানা দরখাস্ত দাখিল করেন। শুনিলাম প্রার্থনা সন্তোষজনক নয় বিধায় অগ্রাহ্য করা গেল। পক্ষদ্বয়কে এক্ষণই প্রস্তুত হওয়ার জন্য নির্দেশ দেওয়া গেল। পরবর্তীতে ১ নং বিবাদীপক্ষ আর কোন প্রতিকার পাইবেন না। বার বার ডাকাডাকি করিয়া ও বিবাদী পক্ষকে কোর্টে হাজির পাওয়া গেলনা বিধায় অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি একতরফাভাবে শুনানির জন্য হাতে লওয়া হইল। শপথ গ্রহনান্তে বাদীপক্ষের ১ নং স্বাক্ষী বাবুল চক্রবর্তীর জবানবন্দি লিপিবদ্ধ করা হইল এবং ভিন্ন ফর্দ্দ যাহা নথিতে সামিল করা হইল। এবং বাদী পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ কৌসুলীর বক্তব্য শ্রবণ করা হইল। রেকর্ড পর্যালোচনা করিলাম। বাদীগণ তাহাদের দাবী প্রমাণ করিতে পারিয়াছে। কোর্ট ফী যথার্থ।  অতএব আদেশ হইল যে,

অত্র মোকদ্দমা বিনা খরচায় একতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রি হইল। ১ (ক) নং বিবাদী যাহাতে নাঃ ভূমিতে জোরপূর্বক প্রবেশ করিয়া বাদীগণের শান্তিপূর্ণ দখলীয় স্বত্বে ব্যাঘাত সৃষ্টি করিতে না পারে সেই মর্মে চিরস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞা দেওয়া গেল।”

It is contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that from a reading of the impugned ex parte judgment, it appears that the learned Munsif only recorded the deposition of the plaintiff as P. W. 1 and without proof of any document filed by the plaintiff and or marking the same as exhibits in support of the plaintiffs case and without complying with the provisions of Order 20 rule 4 sub-rule 2 and Rule 5 that means without applying his judicial mind to the facts and Circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, has arbitrarily passed the impugned ex parte judgment and decree and granted the relief for permanent injunction in favour of the plaintiff against the contesting defendant-petitioner. I myself have carefully read the impugned ex parte judgment and decree and I find that the learned Munsif has not uttered a single word in respect of possession of the parties in the suit-land though it is a suit for permanent injunction wherein question of possession is of vital importance and also about the documents which have been only filed in Court by the plaintiffs in support of his case but not legally proved and marked as exhibits in the suit. Thus it is clear that the minimum legal requirements in passing the ex parte judgment and decree have not been complied with and thus there has been gross violation of the mandatory provisions of law which has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice. The learned District Judge has totally failed to notice this vital defect in the impugned ex parte judgment and decree and illegally upheld the same without proper application of his judicial mind to the material aspect of the case. However in view of the above provisions of law and the decisions referred to above, I find much force in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and I am inclined to hold that the ex parte decree has been passed illegally and without compliance of the mandatory provisions of law and hence the impugned orders of the courts below suffer from serious legal infirmities which have caused a failure of justice and hence need be interfered with by this court in the interest of justice. Now, as regards the finding as to the sufficient cause by which the defendant-petitioner has been allegedly prevented from appearing in the trial court on the day fixed for hearing of the suit, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the same has not been based on proper consideration of the material on record and the learned Munsif has given undue weight to some minor discrepancies in the deposition of the witnesses instead of considering the materials and the vital parts of the evidence on record particularly with regard to the illness of the defendant petitioners on 3.6.85 and further the evidence of both the sides has not been judged by the Court below by equal standard and as a result has been a complete miscarriage of justice.

6. It is also contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the appellate Court equally committed illegality in upholding the finding of the trial Court on the question of sufficient cause without considering the evidence in its true and proper perspective and as such the said finding is nothing but a perverse one which has occasioned a failure of justice.

<u>7. I have heard the learned Advocate on the above question of sufficient cause and I think the submission of the learned Advocate merits consideration but as I have already found that the impugned ex parte decree cannot be sustained in law in view of fact that the same was passed ex parte without fulfillment of compliance with its basic legal requirements, rather in violation of the mandatory provisions of law. I do not like to made any final observation of my own on the said question. Now in view of my earlier finding as to the propriety of the ex parte decree, the impugned orders of the courts below along with the ex parte decree in question are liable to be set aside in the interest of justice.</u>

8. For the reasons stated above, the Rule is therefore made absolute. The impugned orders of the courts below along with the ex parte decree are set aside. The suit being O. C. suit No. 32 of 1984 is restored to its file and number for hearing and disposal in accordance with law in the light of the observations made above with notice to both the parties on condition that the defendant petitioner must pay a sum of Taka 500/00 as costs to the plaintiffs before the suit is taken up for hearing.

9. Let a copy of this judgment be transmitted to the courts below immediately.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. M. A. Muntakim with Mr. Abdullah Al Baki Mr. Mohammad Nazmul Hassan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner 
Mr. Ariful Islam, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No.2
parties:
Ashraf Uddin Ahmed (Chunnu) ----- Petitioner
VERSUS
Jamuna Bank and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Mahmudul Hoque, J:- This Rule nisi was issued under Article 102 of the
Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh at the instance of the petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why Order No.29 dated 24.07.2012 passed by the respondent No.1 in Artha Execution Case No.166 of 2010 arising out of Artha Rin Case No.404 of 2008 rejecting the application filed under Order 21, Rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 for permission of selling the mortgage property of schedule Nov.1 and 2 through private negotiation on the condition of depositing the sale proceeds to the concerned court and order No.30 dated 08.08.2012 disposing of the execution case finally (Annexure-DI ) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper, 

2. Facts leading to issuance of Rule, in brief, are that the respondent No.2 bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No.404 of 2008 on 14.07.2008 against the petitioner and others in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka for realization of Taka 4,29,33,201/- by selling the mortgaged property. 

3. The petitioner as defendant No.3 filed written statements on 31.08.2000 denying all material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that the petitioner did not execute any personal guarantee for the loan granted to the Proforma-respondent Nos.3-6 and he is not liable for the loan and had not defaulted in payment of the amount due to the bank but the respondent No.1 court without applying his judicial mind and material facts decreed the suit against the petitioner vide judgment and decree dated 24.02.2010. 

4. Thereafter, the respondent hank filed Artha Execution Case No.166 of 2010 for execution of the decree on 30.05.2010 against the petitioner and others. In the said execution case the petitioner filed an application under Section 49(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 praying for installment of the decreetal amount of money. The court upon hearing allowed the application on 09.01.2012 affording an opportunity to pay the decreetal money by 4 installments. The petitioner tried his level best to pay the installments but failed as he could not arrange the amount. Thereafter, on 28.05.2012 the court cancelled the installment facility as the petitioner failed to pay l' installment by 09.05.2012 and fixed on 05.06.2012 for taking steps on behalf of the decree holder. On 24.07.2012 the petitioner filed an application under Order 21 Rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. 2003 praying for permission of selling the mortgaged property under schedule Nos. l and 2 through private negotiation on the condition of depositing the sale proceeds to the court. but the court without taking the facts into consideration rejected the same vide Order No.29 dated 24.07.2012 and fixed on 08.08.2012 for taking steps. On the date fixed, the decree holder filed an application under Section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM praying for issuance of a certificate in favour of the decree holder bank. The court upon hearing allowed the application and disposed of the execution case finally vide its order No.30 dated 08.08.2012. At this stage the petitioner moved this court by filing this application under Article 102 of the Constitution against the Order No.29 dated 24.07.2012 and order No.30 dated 08.08.2012 and obtained the present Rule and stay.

5. Mr. M. A. Muntakim, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that admittedly the mortgaged properties were placed on auction but no bidder was found and, in the circumstances, the court ought to have allowed the application filed by the petitioner allowing himself to sell the property by private negotiation and to deposit the sale proceeds to the court by exercising its inherent power under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adatat Ain as well as under the provision of Order 21, Rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure for ends of justice but in not doing so, the court committed illegality and acted malafide. He further submits that since the respondent No.2 bank initiated the suit against this petitioner claiming the petitioner as garantor for the loan, in such situation the decree holder as well as the court ought to have proceeded with the properties owned by the principle borrower first under Section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and only thereafter with the guarantor's properties in the event of any shortfall. But in the present case, no such steps had been taken by the respondent No.2 bank as well as the respondent No.1 court and as such the order passed by the respondent No.1 court rejecting the application filed by the petitioner under Section 57 of the AM and Order 21, Rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure is illegal and without lawful authority. He further submits that the executing court can exercise its inherent power for securing ends of justice but in the instant case the court most arbitrarily rejected the application without complying with the provisions of law and as such the impugned orders are illegal and passed without lawful authority. 

6. None of the respondents has filed any affidavit-in-opposition. Mr. Ariful Islam the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2, bank, opposing the Rule submits that the court in passing the impugned order rejecting the application of the petitioner under Order 21, Rule 83 and Section 57- of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain committed no illegality rather passed the order in accordance with law. He further submits that since the mortgaged property could not be sold in auction for want of a bidder, the court had no alternative other than to proceed with the provision in Section 33 of the AM. It is also argued that nothing in sub-rule (3) of Rule 83 of Order 21 shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or charge on such property. In support of his submissions, Mr. Islam read out the sub-rule (3) of Rule 83 of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure and referred to judgment passed by the Appellate Division in the case of Kazi Abul Hossain —vs- Standard Chartered Bank and others in CPLA No.1 868 of 2002, as well as to the cases of Kaveribai Ammal by agent S.L. Narayana Rao —vs- Mehta and son, reported 1924 Madras-234 and Koralal —vs- Punjab National Bank Limited reported in AIR 1921 Lahore-384. 

7. We have heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the application, impugned Orders and other papers appended thereto. 

8. Upon a perusal of the impugned order it is found that the respondent No.1 court while passing the order rejecting the petitioner's application under Order 21, Rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adatat AM assigned the reasons for the same and also observed that the petitioner as judgment debtor did not take any step for selling the property or raising the amount of the decree arranging buyer when auction notice was published in the newspaper and also observed that the filing of the application represents but it is merely a dilatory tactic of the judgment debtor. 

9. We have gone through the decision in Kaveribai Animal by agent S.L. Narayana Rao -vs- Mehta and son reported in 1924 Madras 234 wherein it is held that an application to extend the time fixed by the mortgage decree for the purpose of allowing the amount of the decree to be raised by mortgage or by private sale of such property cannot be granted in view of the provision of Order 21, Rule 83 and the same view has also been expressed in the case of Kora Lal -vs- Punjab National Bank Limited reported in AIR 1921 Lahore 384 wherein it is also held that the provisions of Rule 83 do not apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or charge on, such property. The reason for this being that -the case of a mortgage decree the right of sale does not depend upon attachment in execution but is conferred by the decree itself and that where the decree contains a specific provision as to the sale of the property the court has no discretion in the matter. 
10. Besides, another decision in the case of Agrani Bank Vs. Anwarul Bashir Khan passed in Civil Appeal Nos.) 05-108 of 2008 is also quoted below which wholly supports this view: 
"The expressions 'the amount of the decree may be raised used in Sub-rule  ( I ) means the total decreetal amount and not an amount which could not satisfy the decree, and no court can grant such permission unless the entire debt can be realized by private alienation. This provision should be read subject to the provision of Sub-rule (3) which is a non-obstante clause, which provides "Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property 'directed to be sold in execution of decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or charge on, such property." 

So, Sub-rule (I) does not apply to cases in which property is directed to be sold in execution of a decree on a mortgage. This is because: the decree holder or the creditor's right of sale rests on the decree. If the judgment debtor affected the alienation with the consent of the decree holder, the implication of such sale would be otherwise. This is because by giving consent to the private sale the decree holder does not become a holder of the decree for payment of money which is an essential condition for the applicability of Section 73 of the Code. Therefore, there is no doubt that in case of a decree for foreclosure be it the High Court Division, or any other superior Court, it has no power to issue certificate to alienate the mortgaged property for enabling the judgment debtor to raise money for payment of the total decreetal amount by private sale without the consent of the decree holder. 

11. In view of above observation and in the light of the decisions referred above, we find no manner of application of the provisions of Order 21, Rule 83 of the Code of Civil Procedure or Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain in the present case because the court reserves no right to issue such certificate under Sub-rule (2) of Rule 83 to sell the property by private negotiation which has been put in auction under Section 33(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain for sale in auction of the mortgage decree. Resultantly, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

12. In the result, the Rule is discharged, without any order as to cost. The stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated. 
13. Communicate the judgment to the court concerned at once. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Kazi Rehan Nabi, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner. 
Mr. Mohammad Abdullah, Advocate ------ For the Opposite parties.
parties:
Agrani Bank ------ Petitioner.
Versus
Mrs. Lutfunnahar Begum and others ------ Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal, J:- This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.531 of 2004 arising out of Artha Rin Adalat Case No.388 of 2003 should not be set-aside. 

2. The relevant facts in short are that the-petitioner-Bank as plaintiff instituted a suit being Artha Rin Suit No.388 of 2003 against the defendant-opposite party No.1, Mrs. Lutfunnahar and another for realisation of its outstanding dues with 'interest amounting to Tk. 25,87,984/- as stood on 31.3.2003 on the averments that the loan amounting to Tk.2,00,000/- was disbursed as per terms and conditions of loan sanction letter but the defendant-opposite parties inspite of repeated letters to re-pay the loan issued by the plaintiff-bank did not turn to repay the loan. Hence, the suit. 

3. After exhausting all the formalities available under the law the suit was decreed ex-parte vide ex-parte order and decree dated 4.10.2003 (decree singed on 13.10.2003) and subsequently, the final decree was drawn up on 01.01.2004. Ultimately, the decree-holder-Bank in order to realise its outstanding dues by selling the mortgaged property put the decree into execution by filing Artha Jari Case No.61 of 2004 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Dhaka. 

4. During the pendency of the said Artha Jail Case No.61 of 2004 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st  Court, Dhaka the judgment-debtors filed an application under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for dismissing the Artha Jari Case. 

5. The Artha Rin Adalat upon hearing the parties rejected the application by its Order No. 16 dated 17.10.2004 holding that the provision of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 is not applicable in the case inasmuch as in this case the suit was decreed ex-parte vide ex-parte order and decree dated 4.10.2003 (decree singed on 13.10.2003) and the final decree was drawn up on 01.01.2004, that is, long before the provision of section 47(3) came into force. 

6. Against the said order No. 16 dated 17.10.2004 the defendant-opposite parties filed Civil Revision No.531 of 2004 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka. Ultimately, the said revision was transmitted to the Court of Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka for disposal. 

7. The learned Additional District Judge upon hearing the revisional application by his judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 allowed the revision and set-aside the ex-parte order and decree dated 04.102003 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Rin Suit No.388 of 2003. 

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 the decree-holder bank moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.  

9. Mr. Kazi Behan Nabi, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the learned Additional District Judge under misconception of law and facts most illegally without adverting the material finding of the Artha Rin Adalat, that is, the provision of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is not applicable in the case most illegally passed the impugned judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 setting aside the ex-party order and decree dated 4.10.2003. He next submits that the learned Additional District Judge ought to have been arrived at a finding that the revisional application was misconceived, ill-advised and not maintainable inasmuch as the judgment debtors preferred the same against the ex-parte judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat without depositing 10% of the decreetal amount as per express provision of sub-section 3 to section 19 of the Ain, 2003. 
10. Referring to the provisions of section 47(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 Mr. Rehan Nabi, submits that the learned Additional District Judge failed to appreciate the simple question of law as the provisions of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 is not applicable in the present case inasmuch as the Artha Rin Suit No.388 of 2003 was decreed on 4.10.2003 ( decree singed on 13.10.2003) and the final decree was drawn up on 01.01.2004 that is long before the provision of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 came into force on 5th May, 2004. Mr. Rehan, finally submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case the impugned judgment and order is not only illegal also perverse being contrary to law as well as without jurisdiction and as such the same is liable to be set-aside.  

11. On the other hand, Mr. Mohammad Abdullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties supports the impugned judgment and order passed by the Additional District Judge, 7th  Court, Dhaka which was, according to him just, correct and proper. He submits that the suit was decreed ex-parte against the judgment-debtor-opposite parties for an amount of Tk.25,00,000/- but there is nothing on record to show that the claim of the plaintiff-Bank is based on any documentary evidence whatsoever. He further submits that as per provision of section 60(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 all suit pending under the old Artha Rin AM namely Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 stood transferred before the Artha Rin Adalat established under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and in such legal position the Bank cannot claim more than 200% of the principal amount as per provision of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 and thus, the learned Additional District Judge committed no illegality in setting aside the ex-party judgment and decree dated 4.10.2003 (decree singed on 13.10.2003).

12. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the Revisional application, supplementary affidavit dated 17.8.2010 along with other connected papers including the impugned judgment and order as filed therewith. To appreciate the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides from a correct angle, we want to decide first as to the question of maintainability of the instant revisional application. 

13. In deciding this point, we feel it necessary to quote hereunder the provisions of section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

Section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 reads as follows:  ১৯। একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কিত বিধান ৷-
১ ৷ মামলার শুনানীর জন্য ধার্য কোন তারিখে বিবাদী আদালতে অনুপস্থিত থাকিলে, কিৎবা মামলা শুনানীর জন্য গৃহীত হইবার পর ডাকিয়া বিবাদীকে উপস্থিত পাওয়া না গেলে, আদালত মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে নিস্পত্তি করিবে। 

২ ৷ কোন মামলা একতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রী হইলে, বিবাদী উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রীর তারিখের অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী রদের জন্য দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন ৷

৩ ৷ উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান অনুযায়ী দরখাস্ত দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে বিবাদীকে উক্ত দরখাস্ত দাখিলের তারিখের পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১ ০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা বাদীর সেই পরিমাণের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরূপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে, অথবা জামানত স্বরূপ ব্যাৎক ড্রাফট, পে-অর্ডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোপ্য বিনিমেয় দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসাবে আদালতে জমাদান করিতে হইবে।

8।উপ-ধারা(৩)এর বিধানমতে ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা জমাদানের সংগে সংগে দরখাস্তটি মঞ্জুর হইবে, একতরফা ডিক্রী রদ হইবে এবং মূল মামলা উহার পূর্বের নম্বর ও নথিতে পুনরুজ্জীবিত হইবে এবং আদালত ঐ মর্মে একটি আদেশ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবে, এবং অতঃপর মামলাটি যে পর্যায়ে এক তরফা নিষ্পত্তি হইয়াছিল, ঐ পর্যায়ের অব্যবহিত পূর্ববর্তী পর্যায় হইতে পরিচালিত হইবে৷ 

From a reading of the above quoted provisions of section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003, it transpires that Artha Rin Adalat AM imposes two preconditions on filing an application against the ex-parte decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. One of such preconditions is that 10% of the decreetal amount as security must be deposited and then the application must be filed within 30 days from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree. It is found in this case the present opposite parties preferred the t revisional application against the ex-parte judgment and decree before the learned District Judge, Dhaka without depositing any amount in compliance with the provision of section 19 of the Ain, 2003. Since the defendant judgment debtors had not deposited 10% of the decreetal amount for preferring the application or revision against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat, in the eye of law the application/ revision was incompetent and not maintainable. 

14. Now, let us see how far the Artha Rin Adalat was justified in rejecting the application under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003. The Artha Rin Adalat rejected the application under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 by its Order No.16 dated 17.10.2004 stating as follows: 

“অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ৪৭(৩)ধারায় বলা হইয়াছে এই ধারার বিধানটি এই আইন বলবৎ হইবার ১(এক) বৎসর পর কার্যকর হইবে৷ আলোচ্য ক্ষেত্রে দেখা যায় অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ১লা যে, ২০০৩ হইতে কার্যকর হইয়াছে এবং 8৭ ধারাটি ১লা মে, ২০০8 হইতে কার্যকর হইয়াছে৷ ফলে দেখা যায় বর্নিত 8৭ ধারার কার্যকরী হওয়ার বহুপূর্বে অর্থ্যাৎ ৪/১০/২০০৩ ইং তারিখে অত্র মোকদ্দমা একতরফা ডিক্রীর আদেশ হওয়ায় বিবাদীর ৪৭ ধারার দরখাস্তটি বিধি সম্মত নহে৷ এমতাবস্হায় বিবাদীপক্ষের বিগত ১৫/৯/২০০8 ইং তারিখের দরখাস্তটি সরাসরি নাকোচ করা হইল৷” 

15. On a perusal of the said order together with the provisions of section 47 of the AM, 2003, it appears that sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 47 of the AM, 2003 has put an embargo on a filing suit claiming interest more than 200% of the loan granted and sub-section (3) of section 47 of the Ain, 2003 has made this embargo affective from one year after coming of this Ain, 2003 into force, that is, from 1st May, 2004. Our, view is therefore, that the Artha Rin Adalat rightly on assigning sound reason rejected the application under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 by its order No.16 dated 17.10.2004. 

16. On an analysis of the impugned judgment and order dated 5.01.2006, we are surprise to see that the learned Additional District Judge without adverting the 'sole finding of the Artha Rin Adalat that the provision of section 47(3) of the Ain, 2003 is not applicable in this case abruptly set-aside the ex-party order and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. We do not think that the learned Additional District Judge sitting under revisional jurisdiction made a correct approach to the simple problem. 

17. Furthermore, there is another aspect of the case to which we think the attention of 
the learned Additional District Judge ought to have been drawn that is the proposition of law is by now well settled in so many cases including in the case of Sultana Jute Mills Ltd. and others Vs. Agrani Bank and others repotted in 46 DLR(AD)174, in the case of Hosne Ara Begum & another Vs. Islami Bank Bangladesh and others reported in 5 MLR(AD) 290, in the case of Md. Harun-Or-Rashid Vs. Pubali Bank Ltd. and others reported in 27 BLD(AD) 326 that no revision lies against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, we find there is a good deal of substance in the contentions raised by Mr. Rehan Nabi, that the learned Additional District Judge under misconception of law and facts most illegally set-aside the ex-parte judgment and decree and the same is liable to be set-aside.
18. On query from the Court Mr. Abdullah, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties could not refer to any principle which has been allegedly violated by the Artha Rin Adalat or to any fact which has either been ignored or wrongly relied upon. Mr. Abdullah, however, repeatedly submitted that the Artha Rin Adalat mechanically decreed the suit ex-parte without considering the aspect that the present opposite parties paid Tk. 1,72,000/- out of total Tk. 2,00,000/- principal amount. 

19. This argument in defending the impugned judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 is fallacious as well as misconceived. 

20. In any view of the matter, having regard to the fact as aforesaid, we are inclined to hold that the learned Additional District Judge seriously erred in law in passing the impugned order without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 5.01.2006 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.531 of 2004 arising out of Artha Rin Adalat Case No.388 of 2003 is set-aside. 

22. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. 

23. Since the matter has been dragging over of period of 7 years the Artha Rin Adalat concerned is directed to proceed with the execution case expeditiously. 

24. Communicate the order at once. 

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 1.12.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 7 of 2007)
full_judgment:
B. K. Das J.:- This Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 1st December, 2008 of a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in making the rule issued in Civil Revision No. 07 of 2007 absolute. 

2. The petitioner No. 1 herein as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 74 of 1994 for declaration of title and for further declaration that registered kabala being No.6996 dated 02.07.1991 executed by tile defendant nos. 1 and 2 in favour of defendant No. 3 was collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiff' and also for recovery of khas possession by evicting the defendants therefrom. The suit was decreed on compromise with defendant No. 1 and 2 and ex-pare against the rest by judgment and decree dated 02.09.2002. Then, the defendant Nos. 4 to 6 made an application under order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2006 for restoration of the suit to its original file and number after set-ting aside the experte decree. 

3. The plaintiff, meanwhile, put the decree in execution being Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2006. The defendant Nos. 4 to 6 on 1.3.09.2006 made as application for stay of further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case. By an order dated 08.10.2006 the Executing Court rejected the application on the view that as there was no suit pending, such application was not maintainable. 

4. Being aggrieved, the defendant Nos. 4 to 6 made an application under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil procedure for revision of such order of the Executing Court but by an order dated 8.10.2006 revision application was rejected in affirming the order of the Executing Court. 

5. Being aggrieved thereby the respondent as petitioner moved the High Court Division in revision being Civil Revision No. 7 of 2007 and a learned Single Judge upon hearing the parties by judgment and order dated 1st December, 2008 made the rule absolute and further proceedings of the execution case in question was stayed till disposal of Miscellaneous case No. 23 of 2006. 

6. The decree-holder-petitioner being dissatisfied with the said order of the High Court Division filed the instant petition. 

7. We have heard the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan and considered the impugned judgment and all other materials on record Mr. Bhuiyan for the petitioner submits that the revisional court found that the plaintiff-petitioner having got the decree On compromise on 2.9.2002 (decree singed on 9.9.2009 is legally entitled to get the benefit thereof and that the Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2006 was filed by defendant Nos. 4 to 6, after about three and half years under Order 9 Rule 13 and that the learned Senior Assistant Judge, upon overall consideration rejected the application for stay of further proceedings of the execution case and the lower appellate court affirmed the same upon finding also that it was not at all proper to stay further proceedings of the execution case after such a long time on the plea of non service of summons raised by the defendant Nos. 4 to 6 and the High Court Division without adverting to the reasons given by the lower appellate court reversed the concurrent decision and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the lower appellate court having affirmed the decision of the learned Senior Assistant Judge given on the application under order 21 Rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure by giving cogent reasons, the High Court Division committed an error of law in reversing the concurrent decision and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. 

8. We find merit in the submissions of the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner. Leave is accordingly granted. 

9. The petitioner is directed to deposit security of Taka.1,000/- within 1 (one) month. 

10. The petitioner is permitted to prepare the paper book out of court in accordance with rules. 

End.
