full_judgment:
LATIFUR RAHMAN, J.: This appeal by leave by the Auction Purchaser-appellant is directed against the judgment and order dated 24.6.90 of the. High Court Division; Dhaka passed in Civil Revision No. 438 of 1990 discharging the Rule, after affirming the order dated 27.1.90 passed in Money Execution Case No. 78 off 1984 of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong. 

2. Respondent No. 3 as plaintiff institute Money Suit No. 161 of 1969 .in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong against respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and three others as defendants for recovery of Tk. 4,73,001. 35 with subsequent costs and interests alleging, inter alia, that the defendants in 1961 opened letter of credit with the plaintiff bank for importing machineries for setting up a Glass Factory at Nasirabad, Chittagong; that the Machineries were imported but the defendants neither established the factory nor paid back the amount to the plaintiff and hence the suit. 

3. Respondent No. 1, Company filed written statement duly verified by its Managing Director, respondent No. 2, but ulitmately did not contest the suit. The said suit on transfer to the Court of 3rd Subordinate Judge, Chittagong was renumbered as Money suit No. 36 of 1971 and was decreed ex-parte on 27.7.72. The said decree was put into execution in Money Execution Case No. 34 of 1982 of the 3rd Court of subordinate Judge, Chittagong. But after the abolition of the said Court the case was renumbered as Money Execution Case No. 78 of (11.1984 of the 2nd Court of subordinate Judge, Chittagong. Some of the imported machineries as described in schedule 1 of the plaint were stored and kept in the godown under the care and control of respondent No. 3-bank and in such circumstances respondent No. 3 filed an application on 18.11.82 under Order 21 Rule 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the executing Court of attachment and sale of the said machineries and the executing court allowed the said application by its order dated 3.2.83. Thereafter a notice was published in the daily Azadi on 19.9.88 of public auction of the said movables of the judgment-debtors on 5.11.88., Public auction of the said movables was accordingly held on 5.11.88 and the highest bid of the appellant for Tk. 2,52,500.00 was accepted and the appellant deposited the entire sale price of Tk. 2,52,500.00 in court by challan as per order of the Court. 

4. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application in the aforesaid Money Execution Case No. 78 of 1984 not to deliver the auction sold movables to the appellant till their filing a case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Civil Procedure Code for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 27.7.72. Thereafter respondent Nos. 1 and 2 file another application on 11.12.88 under Section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code for cancellation of the auction sale and for return of the machineries to them on payment of Tk. 5 (live) lacs. The executing court disposed of the said two applications observing that the said application could be considered if the judgment-debtors deposit in court the entire decrial dues with interest and costs amounting to Tk. 6,19,578/29 within 22.12.88. On the application of the respondents time was subsequently extended upto 11.1.89 for depositing the decrial dues. 

5. On 31.12.88 respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 130 of 1988 for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 27.7.72. Respondents also filed an application in the said Miscellaneous case for stay of further proceedings of Money Execution Case No. 78 of 1984 and 2.1.89 was fixed for hearing and disposal. A similar application for stay was also filed in the Money Execution Case no. 78 of 1984 on 1.1.89 which was rejected by the executing court by its order No. 83 dated 28.1.89. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 again on 9.2.89 filed another application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the executing court for staying further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of the aforesaid Misc. Case No. 130 of 1988, but the learned Judge rejected the application by his Order No. 86 dated 13.2.89 and the execution case was ordered to be proceed with. Respondents thereafter filed successive petitions for time allowing them to bring stay order from the High Court Division and they having failed to bring the stay order, the executing court ordered to deliver the auction sold goods to the appellants whose bid was earlier accepted and who pad and deposited the price by challan on 15.11.88 as per order of the Court; but the auction sold goods were not delivered to the appellant 

6. Respondents Nos. 1 and 2 thereafter filed another application on 17.5.89 for time to bring stay order but the same was rejected. The said respondents then filed another application under Section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code for time for seven days to bring stay order but the same was also rejected on 18.5.89 and directions were issued to deliver the auction sold goods to the appellant but the same were not delivered. 

7. On 21.5.89 respondent Nos. 1 and 2 moved a revisiOnal application before the High Court Division, Chittagong but ulitimately withdrew the same as not pressed. The said respondents also filed two applications before the executing court on 21.5.89 one for seven days-time to bring stay order and the other for 15 days-time to deposit the decrial dues but both the applications were rejected. 
8. In the meantime the appellant sold the aforesaid auction purchased goods to one Parimal Bikash Sen at a total consideration of Tk.4.75 lacs by an agreement of sale with a stipulation that if the goods were not delivered to him he would get compensation of Tk. 1.00 lac which was also brought to the notice of the executing Court. 

9. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2, however, on 22.6.89 ultimately deposited the decretal dues much out of time and the executing court by Order No. 127 dated 27.1.90 was pleased to pass order for release of the auction sold goods in favour of the Judgment -debtor-respondents and allowed the auction-purchaser appellant only compensation @ 10%. This order was challenged before the High Court Division in revision, being Civil Revision No. 438 of 1990 and the Rule was discharged. 

10. the learned Judges of the High Court-Division though found that the sale of goods in question became absolute under Order 21, Rule 77 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Court has still the jurisdiction to set aside the sale under Section 151 of the code of civil procedure. The learned Judges after referring to a number of decisions, particularly the case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 109, held that the executing court rightly exercised its inherent power after considering the hardship of all concerned. 

11. leave was granted to consider whether the sale having become absolute under Order 21, Rule 77(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned Judges misdirected themselves in releasing the auction sold goods in favour of the judgment-debtor-respondents; whether to correct and true interpretation of Order 21, Rule 78 of the Code, could the learned Judges release the goods in favour of the judgment-debtor when, the sale is not a nullity and whether in vice of specific provisions of Rules 77 and 78 of Order  21 of the Code for Public auction of moveable property and remedy provided thereunder, section 151 of the Code is available in the instant case to set aside the sale. Leave was also granted to consider whether the High Court Division was wrong in assessing the compensation @ 10% in the face of the provision of Order 21, Rule 78 of the Code when the auction purchaser entered into an agreement for sale of the auction purchased moveable property with a 3rd party providing for compensation at Tk. 1 (one) lac. 
12. From the materials on record it appears that in the instant case the auction sale was held on 5.11.88 and on that day the Nazir of the Court submitted the proceeding before the executing court noting the amounts quoted by different tenderers and the executing court accepted the quotation of the auction purchaser-appellant being the highest bidder by an endorsement made in the body of the auction sheet by an order in the order sheet on 10.11.88 it was formally accepted and the auction purchaser was allowed time till 15.11.88 to deposit the entire bid money which was accordingly deposited on 15.11.88. 

Order 21, Rule 77, Sub-Rules 1 and 2 read as follows-

"77.-(1) Where moveable property is sold by public auction the price of each lot shall be paid at the time of sale or as soon after as the officer or Other person holding the sale directs and in default of payment the property shall forthwith be re-sold. 

(2), On payment of the purchase-money, the officer of other person holding the sale shall grant a receipt the same, and the sale shall become absolute." 

Thus, it appears that the appellant deposited the amount another the auction sale on 15.11.88 as per the order of the Court and after accepting the appellant. The auction sale of the tenant was formally accepted by the Court by order dated 10.11.88 giving time to the auction appellant to deposit the entire bid by 15.11.88 and the same was duly. As per Sub-Rule 2 of Rule 77 of the Code on payment of the purchase more by the sale became absolute and the same cannot be set aside in the manner as has been done by the executing court and affirmed by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. Further, a reference to Order 21, Rule 78 of the Code shows that for any irregularity in publishing or conducting the sale of moveable property the sale shall not be vitiated but a person sustaining any injury by such irregularity at the hand of any other person may institute a suit for compensation or for recovery of specific property and for compensation in default of such recovery. In the present case there being no allegation that the sale was a nullity, the same cannot be set aside as Rule 78 of Order 21 of the Code clearly speaks that for mere irregularity no sale shall be vitiated. Hence the learned Judges of the High Court Division without appreciating the true and correct import of Rules 77 an 78 of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure set aside the auction sale. The case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 109, is a case relating to auction sale of immoveable property wherein this Division after considering the case of both the parties in order to save the immoveable property of the appellant, an amount of Tk. 75,000/00 was directed to be paid to respondent No. 2 (highest bidder) as compensation as he was an innocent sufferer for the latches of the appellant. Thus, the case reported in 41 D.L.R. which relates to a immoveable property has no application in a sale of moveable property. Sale of immovable property is guided under Order 21, Rule 82 to 103 of the Code. Particularly Sale of immoveable property will become absolute and certificate will be issued under Rule 94 of Order 21 of the Code. The Court exercised its discretion when the sale had not become absolute but in the present case the executing court has exercised a discretion after the sale become absolute and the learned Judges of the High Court Division on a wrong reliance on the case reported in 41 DLR (AD) 109 upheld the exercise of that discretion. 

13. It may be mentioned here that specific provisions having been provided and ;r the Code of Civil Procedure for sale of moveable property by auction sale as contemplated in Order 21, Rules 77, 78 and 79, the learned Judges of the High Court division misdirected themselves in taking recourse to Section 151 of the Code of. Civil Procedure for setting aside the auction sale. The learned Judges also wrongly assessed compensation @ 10% when from the materials on record it appears that the auction purchaser-appellant entered into a contract with on Primal Bikash Sen to sell the moveable properties where in it was provided that upon the auction-purchaser's failure to deliver the auction purchased goods, the appellant would pay a compensation of Tk. 1 (one) lac to Parimal Bikash sen. It appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division illegally affirmed the order of the Subordinate Judge wherein he set aside the sale by exercising the inherent power of the Court under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thus the learned Judges did not act legally in affirming the order of the executing court. The impugned judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. Consequently, the appeal is allowed with costs.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 275 of 1995
lawyer: For petitioner: Mr. M. A. Matin, Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record. For respondent No. 1 : Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, Advocate-on-Record. Respondent No. 2 : Not represented.
parties:
Sonali Bank ------ Petitioner
Versus
Sultana Razia Nahar and another ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J. : The petitioner-Bank obtained a decree for Tk. 2,97,123.51 with interest and cost against respondent No. 2 a private limited company. During the pendency of the suit respondent No.1, wife of the Managing Director of the respondent-Company, filed an application under order 38 Rule 8 and order 21 Rule 58 giving rise to Miscellaneous case No. 1 of 1.984,  challenging an attachment before Judgment of the property which respondent No. 1, the wife, claimed to be her own. By judgment and order dated 4-9-84 the trial court, namely, the Artha Rin Adalat and the 3rd Court of subordinate judge, Khulna dismissed the Miscellaneous Case as not maintainable in the present form as also on the ground that the petitioner of the said application was entitled to no relief. Respondent No. 1 did not move any higher forum against the said order dated 4-9-34. 

2. After the suit was decreed against respondent-Company No. 2 the decree was put into execution and the same property was again attached. Respondent No. 1 then filed Miscellaneous case No. 39 of 1990 under Order 21 Rule 58 C. P. C. Claiming the attached property to be her own and not liable to be sold in execution of the decree. The decree-holder-petitioner-Bank filed a written objection stating that it is false that respondent No. 1 Purchased the attached property from one Azizur Rahman by a kabala dated 5-8-74. The petitioner claimed that the attached property was purchased her husband, the Managing Director, with his own money and in his own interest and in the benami of respondent No. 1. 

3. By a judgment and order dated 19-11-90 the Artha Rin Adalat dismissed the Miscellaneous case. Respondent No. 1 preferred F. M. A. No. 18 of 1991 in the High Court Division against the said judgment and order of the Artha Rin Adalat and by judgment and order dated 16-1-95 a Division Bench of the High Court Division allowed the appeal, set aside the impugned judgment and order of the Executing Court and accepting the Claim of respondent No. 1 over the attached property released it from attachment. 

4. The petitioner-Bank has preferred this petition for leave to appeal from the aforesaid judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

5. Mr. M. A. Matin, learned Advocate for decree-holder-petitioner-Bank submits that respondent No. 1 having not preferred any appeal in compliance with section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Act, the appeal was incompetent. We find no substance in this contention. Respondent No. 1 filed an appeal under section 7 and its registration as an F. M. A. does not make any difference. The High Court Division also found that the appeal was presented within time and was not barred by limitation. 

6. Mr. M. A. Matin next submits that under section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Act only a judgment passed before the judgment in the suit itself is capable of being appealed against. Once the judgment in the main suit is passed, any other subsequent judgment, including any judgment passed by the Artha Rin Adalat as an Executing Court cannot be the subject matter of an appeal in terms of the language of section 7 of the said Act. 

7. This submission has also no legs to stand. Section 7 provides that any person aggrieved by any judgment and decree of an Artha Rin Adalat may prefei an appeal to the High Court Division within 30 days of the passing of the judgment of decree. Section 7 does not say that the judgment appealed against is limited to a judgment in the main suit itself. Any judgment, other than a mere order, which decides an issue both before and after the main judgment in the suit itself, even in the Executing court, can be the subject matter of appeal under section 7. 

8. Mr. M. A. Matin next submits that the petition of respondent No. 1. under Order 21 Rule 58 C. P. C. in Miscellaneous case No. 38 of 1990 was not maintainable as the circumstances of the case do not attract the provisions of order 21 Rule 58 C. P. C. 
	
9. Again we find no substance in the contention. The maintainability of the second application under order 21 Rule 58 C. P. C. was challenged on the ground that it was barred by res judicata, an earlier application having been dismissed by the Artha Rin Adalat. The High Court Division rightly held that the principle of res judicata is not applicable in such proceeding. 

10. Mr. M. A. Matin submits with regard to the merit of the claim that respondent No. 1 failed to produce her title deed of the attached property either before the Executing Court or before the High Court Division and in such circumstances she failed to discharge her initial onus that the attached property belongs to her.

11. This submission too is misconceived, because the petitioner-Bank did not deny that the attached property stands in the name of respondent No. 1. it was the petitioner's case that she held the attached property in the benami of her husband, the Managing Director of the judgment-debtor-Company. The onus was on the petitioner-Bank to prove the benami character of the attached property and the High Court Division rightly held that to establish a benami transaction the petitioner-Bank must institute a separate proceeding and the said relief is not available to the Bank in an execution proceeding. 

12. We find no ground for interference. 

13. The petition is dismissed. 

End.

lawyer:
No one: For the Petitioner
No one: For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Harendra Nath Mandal ------ Petitioner
Versus
Chitta Ranjan Haider and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J: This rule is directed against the order dated 17.6.1984 passed by the learned Munsif, Nazirpur in the District of Pirojpur, in Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1984 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure restoring Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1984 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit for partition on declaration of title in the suit land in the 2nd Court of Munsif at Pirojpur in which opposite party No.1 was defendant No. 13. Defendant opposite party No.2 contested the suit by filing written• statement while defendant Nos. 2, 15 and 20, though filed written statements, did not eventually contest the suit and some other defendants prayed for separate saliams. The suit was ultimately decreed on 30.1.1982. Thereafter opposite party No. 1 filed Title Appeal No. 39 of 1982 before the District Judge, Bakerganj against the aforesaid judgment and, decree but eventually the said appeal was dis-missed on 9.6.1983.
3. Opposite party No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 1982 before the 2nd Court of Munsif at Pirojpur for setting aside the decree passed on 30.1.82 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the said Miscellaneous Case was subsequently re-numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1984. The said Miscellaneous Case was eventually fixed for peremptory hearing on 29.5.1984 but as the petitioner was absent on that dale and took no step in the matter the case was dismissed for default. Thereafter opposite party No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1984 in the said Court under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1984 alleging inter alia that he was attacked with diarrhea is a result of which he could not appear before the Court on the fateful day on 29.5.1984 which lead to the dismissed of the case for default. In due course of time 15.7.1984 was fixed for peremptory hearing of Misc. Case No. 71 of 1984 but on the application of opposite party No. 1 the date of a hearing was shifted back to 17.6.1984 and on that date the learned Munsif allowed the said Miscellaneous case and set aside the order dated 29.5.1984 by which Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1984 was dis-missed and restored the case to its file and number. It is against this order allowing Miscellaneous Case No.71 of 1984 that the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present rule.

 4. No one appears to support the rule. 

5. No one also appears to oppose the rule. 

6. I have perused the impugned order dated 17.6.84 by which the learned Munsif allowed Miscellaneous Case No. 71 Of 1984 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure without assigning any reason whatsoever. It also appears from the impugned order that although the case was fixed for hearing on 17.6.1984, it was shifted back to 17.6.1984 on the prayer of opposite party No. 1 and on that very dale Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1984 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Civil Procedure was allowed in the name of interest of justice. 

7. An application under order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be allowed only when the petitioner satisfies the Court that there was sufficient cause for non-appearance of the petitioner when the case was called on for hearing. From the impugned order it is evident that the learned Munsif completely ignored the clear mandate of Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure in passing the impugned order, leaving the field of fact and straying to fiction. 

8. It is well-settled that the inherent power of the Court under section 151 C.P.C. can be resorted to in the interest of justice only when there is no specific provision In the Code of Civil Procedure to meet a particular situation and that too for preventing an abuse of the process of the Court or an apparent injustice. But in our case under review, the petitioner sought relief under the provision or Order 9 rule 4 C.P.C., where relief could be given to him if he was able to successfully meet the requirements of law in joined by the said Order. In the face of specific provisions of law under Order 9 rule 4 C.P.C. requiring necessary proof for the satisfaction of the Court to set aside the dis-missal of suit/case for default of the plaintiff or the petitioner, an applicant can succeed in his case only on the merit of his own case and not an any other extraneous considerations. When there is a specific provision of law for giving relief to an aggrieved party but the requirements of law are not met, the Court has no power to dole out gratuitions relief in the name of "interest of justice" or "ends of justice". The Court must not use these expressions lightly and capriciously as it would tend to defeat justice but use the same according to sound judicial principles for ensuring real justice. We may derive instant support of this view in the case of Mst. Khairunnesa Vs. Zabaida Nahar @ Jharns and others reported in 17 B.L.D. (AD), 51. 

9. In this case admittedly the petitioner of Misc. Case No. 71 of 1984 did not examine any witness in support of his case. Except his uncorroborated statements incorporated in his application under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure there is absolutely nothing on record to prove that he was pre-vented by any sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the case was called a for hearing and this lead to the dis-missal of his case for default. In the absence of any evidence before him providing necessary satisfaction that the petitioner was really prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court on the fateful day, the learned trial Court clearly erred in law in allowing Miscellaneous Case no. 71 of 1984 completely ignoring the mandatory provisions of Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The impugned order thus evidently suffers from legal infirmity which can-not be sustained. 

10. In the result, the rule succeeds and it is made absolute without any order as to costs.

11. The impugned order dated 17.6.84 passed by the learned Munsif. Nazirpur is set aside and Miscellaneous Case No.7I of 1984 is sent back on remand to the trial Court for decision according to law. The learned Musif" (now Assistant Judge), Nazirpur is directed to dispose of Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1984 within a period of 3 (three) months positively from the dale of the receipt of this order, after giving opportunities to the parties to represent their respective cases but without granting adjournments except on compelling reasons. 

12. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. 

13. Communicate this order to the learned Munsil (new Assistant Judge) Nazirpur at once. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 2180 of 2008.
lawyer:
For the Petitioners : Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Abu Siddique, Advocateon-Record. 
For Respondent : Mr. Shah Md. Monir Sharif, Nos. 1 -4 Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate on-Record. 
For Respondent Nos.5-8 : Not Represented.
parties:
Janata Bank Ltd. ------ Petitioner 
-Versus-
Gulneara Begum and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman, J: This leave petition arises out of the judgment and order dated 12.08.2008 passed in Writ Petition No.6136 of 2007 by the High Court Division making the Rule absolute. 

2. The writ petitioner filed challenging the order No.4 dated 02.10.2003 and the order dated 06.06.2007 passed in Execution Case No.58 of 2004 by the Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla. 

3. The facts relevant for the purpose of this application are that the petitioner bank filed Money Suit No.8 of 1984 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Comilla, against borrower, Sirajul Haque-the predecessor of these writ petitioners and others, for realisation of outstanding loan money and the said suit was renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No.295 of 1990 on transfer to the Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla, after promulgation of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and the suit was decreed exparte for Tk.40,871.56/- by the judgment and decree dated 23.04.1.991 and for satisfaction of the said decree the petitioner bank filed Execution Case No.37 of 1993 in the year 1993 and there-after filed two other Execution cases, third one being Execution Case No.73 of 2000 which was dismissed for default on 06.08.2002 and thereafter the 4th Execution Case was filed being Execution Case No.220 of 2003 on 25.08.2003, which has been renumbered as Execution Case No.58 of 2004. The last Execution Case was filed after promulgation of the Artha. Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and thereby the last Execution Case is to be proceeded with under the Provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 in view of Section 60(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain , 2003. As per Section 28 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 an Execution Case is required to be filed within one year from the date of disposal of the earlier Execution Case but within 6 years from the date of the decree. The judgment debtor filed an application challenging the initiation and continuation of the proceeding of the Execution Case No.58 of 2004 on the ground that the Execution Case has been filed after the period of limitation as provided under Provision of Section 28(3) and (4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 inasmuch as the Execution Case was filed in the year 1993 and thereby the 6 years allowed under Section 28(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has expired. The petitioner bank resisted the application submitting that the suit was decreed in the year 1991 and at the relevant time, under .Section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure an Execution Case can be filed within 12 years and that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 having been promulgated long after 6 years from the date of judgment and decree passed in the suit in the year 1991 the provision of limitation provided in Section-28 of the Ain, 2003 can not be applied in the instant case and that the provisions of Section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable in the instant case. The Executing Court accordingly admitted the Execution Case and being aggrieved there-against the judgment-debtor-respondent filed the writ petition challenging the issue of limitation and the High Court Division accepted the case of the judgment-debtor and made the Rule absolute. declaring the impugned order without lawful authority and of no legal effect observing that:-
"The learned Advocate for respondent-bank has argued that after coming of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 into operation the execution cases filed earlier did not require to be taken into consideration at all the limitation for filing of the present execution case started running afresh from the date of promulgation of this new Ain of 2003. But we are unable to accept this argument of the learned Advocate for the respondent bank. The decree in question was passed long before in the year 1991 and thereafter 3 execution cases were filed one after another and all of those execution cases were dismissed for default for the laches/negligence of the decree-holder bank. This fact cannot be ignored or brushed asider, Since at the time of coming of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 into force this decree in question was alive (as the 12 years time from the date of decree as mentioned in section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure was yet to expire) this decree was executable under this new Ain of 2003 but on fulfillment of all the conditions laid down in section 28 of this new Ain as quoted above. 
The learned advocate for the respondent-bank has argued also that the executing court concerned, consideration the facts and circumstances, condoned the delay in filing this execution case by the impugned order No.4 dated 02.10.2003 and as such the question of limitation cannot be reopened now in this writ petition. But we do not accept this contention also of the learned advocate for the respondent bank. The Artha Rin Adalat Ain is a special law. Section 28 of this Ain has specified the period of limitation for filing the execution cases under this Ain. Sub-section 2, 3 and 4 of Section 28 have provided also that the execution cases filed beyond the time limited prescribed by this Section 28 will be barred by limitation and will be rejected by the Adalat summarily. So, there was no scope for condoning the delay in filing this execution case and as such the impugned order No.4 dated 02.10.2003 condoning the delay in filing this execution case was illegal. So, from the above discussion it is evident that the execution case in question being filed beyond the time limit prescribed by Sub section (3) (4) of Section 28 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is barred by limitation and as such the auction sale of the mortgaged property of these petitioners in that execution case also is illegal." 

4. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner bank submitted in the light of the observations made by the High Court Division quoted herein above. It appears that the instant Execution Case arises out the judgment and decree passed on 23.04.1991 and that the I' execution case was registered as Execution Case No.37 of 1993. and thereafter two others Execution Cases being Execution Case Nos.12 of 1997 and 73 of 2000 were filed and in course of time those was dismissed and thereafter on 25.08.2003 the last Execution Case being Artha Rin Decree Case No.220 of 2003 was filed which has been renumbered as Artha Decree Case No.58 of 2004 filed in the Court of Artha Rin Malat, Comilla. Section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that where an application for execution of a decree is required to be filed, fresh application presented after expiration of 12 years is not maintainable. In the instant case it appears that the last Execution Case was filed beyond 12 years from the date of the decree in that the decree was passed on 23.04.1991 and the last Artha Decree 'Case No.220 of 2003 was filed on 25.08.2003, which thus show that the case has been filed after more than 12 years and 4 months from the date of the decree. Thus it is hopelessly time barred. It also appears that the last Execution Case has been filed after the promulgation of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and as per Section 60 of the said Act any pending proceeding is to be proceeded with under the Provision of new Act and Section 28 of the said Act provides the limitation for execution case under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and the maximum period of limitation of 6 years provided such execution case filed within one year from the disposal of the previous execution case filed under the said Act. In the instant case the provision of Section 28 cannot be applied inasmuch as the limitation of 6 years expired prior to promulgation of new Act, 2003. Be that as it may since the execution case has been filled after more than 12 years Section-48 of Code Civil Procedure is of no help. The leave petition do not merit consideration being barred by limitation. 

5. The petition is accordingly dismissed. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition For Leave to Appeal No. 1413 of 2005.
lawyer:
For the Petitioners: Mr. T: H. Khan, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Abu Siddique, Advocate-on-Record. 
For Respondent : Not Represented.
parties:
Ali Hossain, and others ------ Petitioners 
-Versus-
The Chairman, First Court of Settlement and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdul Matin, J.- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.08.2005 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.2645 of 2001 discharging the Rule challenging the judgment and order dated 11.03.2001 passed by the 1st Court of Settlement, Segunbagicha, Dhaka in Case No. 97 of 1987 (KhaS), Lalmatia, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. 

2. The petitioner filed the Writ Petition No.2645 of 2001 before the High Court Division challenging inclusion of the building at 3/9, Block-F, Lalmatia, Mohammadpur, Dhaka in Bangladesh Gazette 'Kha' dated 23.09.1986 published under Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance 54/85 at page No.9764(20) serial No.5 as well as judgment and order dated 11.03.2001 passed by the 1st Court' of Settlement, Segunbagicha, Dhaka in Case No.97 of 1987. 
3. The facts, in short, are that the aforesaid plot of land upon which the disputed building situated was originally allotted to SK. Mowla Box and Zobeda Begum by an allotment order dated 30.03.1967 by the then Government of East Pakistan and subsequently a lease deed dated 27.06.1967 was registered between the Government of East Pakistan on the one hand and SK. Mowla Box and Zobeda Begum on the other. That after allotment order and registration of lease deed the original owners Sk. Mowla Box and his wife Zobeda Begum took delivery of possession of the aforesaid Building and began to own, possess and live therein by paying Government clues and the cost of the plot of land without any interruption from any quarter. 

4. After Liberation War the original owner Sk. Mowla Box and Zobeda Begum were in need of raising case money for their business and for paying installments of the cost of the house and accordingly they concluded a bainanama with Sk. Shafazuddin Ahamed on 15.10.1973 for the sale of the suit property and handed over delivery of possession to Sk. Shafazuddin on the same day that is on 15.10.1973. Thereafter, a clearance certificate for the payment of the full cost of the suit property was issued by the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement on 13.03.1975 and that it was stipulated in the bainanama that the vendor Mowla Box and his wife Zobeda Begum will execute and register the sale deed within one year after completion of the formalities by themselves and when the vendor failed to do so the purchaser Sk. Shafazuddin Ahmed was constrained to file a suit being Title Suit No.22 of 1975 for specific performance of contract in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Court, Dhaka. 

5. The Government as defendant appeared on 15.01.1975 in the aforesaid suit and prayed for time by a petition for filing written statement but at last the G.P. did not contest the case because he could not procure the relevant connected papers and para-wise statements from the Ministry concerned and hence the suit was decreed ex-parte on 23.12.1977. After an. ex-parte decree a sale deed being No.40563 dated 21.11.1978 was executed and registered through court in favour of Sk. Shafazuddin, the purchaser. After ex-parte decree and registration of the aforesaid sale deed the Government preferred a Miscellaneous Case being No.159 of 1986 but .subsequently the said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed for default on 21.01.1989. Against the said order the Government did not take any step before the higher court. 

6. After decree and registration of the sale deed through court while the purchaser Shafazuddin has been owning, possessing and living in the aforesaid building, his name was recorded during R.S. operation and that while the purchaser has been owning, possessing and living in the aforesaid building without any interruption from any quarter he applied to the Assistant Commissioner of the House and Settlement of the Ministry of Works, Segunbagicha, Dhaka for mutating his name in place of the earlier owners and in reply the Assistant Commissioner by his letter dated 05.07.1982 asked the purchaser Shafazuddin Ahammed to submit the lease deed, purchase deed, plaint and decree of the court. Thereafter Shafazuddin submitted the aforesaid documents in writing to the Assistant Commissioner. 

7. On 24.03.1982 the Housing and Settlement Officer of the Ministry of Works, Segunbagicha, Dhaka published a show cause notice to the allottee of Lalmatia Housing Estate about the 'construction of their respective allotted plot and the purchaser Shafazuddin gave a reply in writing on 20.08.1982 to that show cause notice and Shafazuddin Ahmed completed the construction of building within two years.- In the aforesaid circumstances while Shafazuddin Ahamed had been owning, possessing and living in the aforesaid building the section officer Moksud Ahammed by his Memo No.9/124 dated 20.01.1986 asked him to show his documents in support of his occupation and in reply he submitted his documents in writing explaining, inter-alia, that he purchased the building from its original owners Sk. Mowla Box and his wife Zobeda Begum and since then he is in possession of the aforesaid building and he has also applied earlier to the Assistant Commissioner of the Housing and Settlement of the Ministry of Works for mutating his name along with all the documents. 

 8. The building in question was enlisted in the Bangladesh Gazette dated 23.09.1986 as per provision of the Ordinance 54/85 whereupon the petitioner filed a petition in the First Court of Settlement for release of the building under Section 7 of the Ordinance 54/85. The aforesaid petition was registered as Case No.97 of 1987 in the First Court of Settlement. The Court of Settlement without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record illegally rejected the aforesaid case on 11.03.2001. Thereafter the petitioner filed writ petition as aforesaid and the High Court Division passed the impugned order discharging the Rule issued earlier and hence this petition. 
9. Heard the learned Counsel and perused the petition and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other papers on record. 

10. Then learned Counsel for the petitioners submit that the High Court Division treated the letter issued by the Section Officer (vide Annexure-`K' to the writ petition) as statutory notice under section 5(1) (b) of the ordinance No.54 of 1985 but this finding is not correct as it is not in inconformity with the form 11 referred to in Rule 3 of the Rules for the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Taking over Possession) Rules, 1972 framed under the provision of Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and disposal) Order, 1972, the letter so issued is no notice in the eye of law and as such the findings of the High Court Division in respect of mandatory statutory notice is without lawful authority and are liable to be set aside. 

11. The learned Counsel has referred to the cases of Bangladesh Vs. Kazi Ashrafuddin Ahmed reported in 23 BLD(AD) 2003 Page-49 and Bangladesh Vs. Amela Khatoon others reported in 53 DLR(AD) 2001 Page-55. 

12. The learned Counsel further submits that when a bainanama is proved in a competent court of law in a case in which the Government was a party and the case is decreed in favour of the petitioner and the Government filed Miscellaneous Case No.159 of 1986 against the decree which was dismissed for default and the Government did not go to the higher court, the court of settlement has no jurisdiction to require the bainanama to be proved before them as the decree is binding upon them. 

13. It appears that the High Court Division considered Section 4 of the Ordinance No.54 of 1985 and 5(1) (b) of the Ordinance and held: 
"According to the said provision a notice in any from is required to be issued under P.0.16 of 1972 on or before the 31s` day of March, 1986 in case enlisting a property as abandoned property under "Kha" list which will be published under Section 5(1) (b) of the Ordinance 54 of 1985." 

The notice as in exhibit-K is dated 20.01.1986 long before 31.03.1986 and has been rightly held to be a valid notice in respect of a property which is an abandoned property as per provision of P.0.16 of 1972. The question whether or not the vendor of the petitioner was holding processing and managing the property in question on 28 February of 1972 is the pertinent question which has not been answered by the petitioner whose title allegedly accrued on the basis of a hainapatra dated 15.10.1973. The subsequent suit for specific performance of contract and the decree in the suit is of no avail to the petitioner inasmuch as the very status of the land and building in question as abandoned property was not decided in the suit. 

14. The petitioner could not prove the possession of his vendor on 28 February, 1972 and therefore the Court of Settlement rightly rejected the settlement case and the High Court Division correctly discharged the Rule. 

15. In the facts and circumstances of this case the decisions reported in 23 BLD(AD) 49 or 53 DLR(AD) 55 have no manner application in the instant case. The proposition of law has been settled by this court in the case of Government of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Jalil and others reported in 48 DLR(AD)10 where it has been laid down that the onus, is squarely on the claimant of the building to prove that the building is not an abandoned property. The Government has no obligation either to deny the facts alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property merely because the same is disputed by the claimant. 

16. This Court also decided the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution and held that the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution can interfere with the findings of a tribunal of fact only if it can be shown that the tribunal had acted without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material evidence/facts causing prejudice to the complaining party or that it had acted malafide or in violation of any principle of natural justice. 

17. We find no merit in this petition which is accordingly dismissed. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Goutam Kumar Roy: For the petitioner
No one appears: For Opposite parties
parties:
Sushil Chandra Das ------ Petitioner
Versus
Niranjan Paul and others ------ Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha J.: In this Rule the order dated 20.7.1997 passed by the senior Assistant. Judge, Shariatpur Sadar (Chakandi) in Title Suit No. 21 of 1994 has been called in question. By this impugned order the learned senior Assistant Judge allowed the application of opposite party No. 1 under order 1 Rule 10 of the code of civil procedure and impleaded him as a defendant in the suit which was finally disposed of by a regular judgment dated 28.11.1996 (decree drawn up on 13.1 1.1996). 

2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that the petitioner as plain-till instituted a suit for specific performance of contract in respect of 183/4 decimals of land in the court of the Assistant Judge, Shariatpur sadar (Chikandi) being Title Suit No. 21 of 1994, alleging, inter alia that the suit land measuring 183/4 decimals along with other lands recorded in S.A. Plot No. 161. 162 and 163 under S.A. Khatian Nos. 47. 82 and 120 of Mouza No. 80 Dhanuka, P.S. palong belonged to Nilkrishna pal and others. While being the rightful owner in possession of the suit property Nilkrishna intended to sell his share to the plaintiff and eventually on 27.6.91entered into an agreement to sell the land to him at a consideration of Tk. 10.000/- only and in pursuance of the said agreement Nilkrishna Pal duly executed a bainapatra in favour of plaintiff on receipt of Tk. 9,500/- as earnest money in part performance of the contract. It was stipulated between in parties that Nilkrishna Pal would soon execute and register a sale deed in favour of the plain-tiff on receipt of the balance of the consideration money. It was contended that. the petitioner in due course offered the balance of the consideration money to Nilkrishna Pal who consumed time on some plea or the other and eventually refused to execute and register the promised kabala on 3rd Paush. 1400 B.S and hence the Suit.

3. It appears the said was ultimately decreed Ex-parte on 26.4.1994. Thereafter, the Government of Bangladesh filed Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1994 before the senior Assistant Judge, Shariatpur Sadar (Chikandi) under order 9 Rule 13 of the code of civil procedure for setting alise the above mentioned Ex-parte decree and for restoration of the suit to its original file and number. Eventually the said Miscellaneous case under order 9 Rule 13 of the code of civil procedure was allowed and the Ex-parte decree dated 27.4.199 set aside. Thereafter, the suit was again decreed on contest by judgment dated 28.11.1996 passed by the senior Assistant Judge. Shariatpur Sadar (Chikandi) and the decree was duly drawn up on 13.11.1996 in pursuance of the aforesaid judgment dated 28.11.1996. It appears that on 11.3.1997 i.e. two and a half months after drawing of the final decree the present opposite party No. 1 Niranjan Pal filed an application under order 1 Rule 10 of the code of civil procedure praying for adding him as a defendant in the suit alleging inter alia that the alleged contract for sale in favour of the plaintiff is a false and fabricated One. It was further con-tended that defendant No. 1 i.e. Nilkrishna Pal had died before the alleged contract. It was also alleged that he is a reversioner of Nilkrishna Pal and he has interest in the suit property and as such he is required to be impleaded in the suit. 

4. The learned senior Assistant judge by the impugned order dated 27.7.1997 allowed the application of opposite party No. 1 under order 1 Rule 10 of the code of civil procedure and made him a defendant in the suit and ordered for amendment of the plaint accordingly. It is against this order the present petitioner moved this court and obtained. 

5. Mr. Goutam Kumar Roy, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that after the suit was finally disposed of and decreed on contest on 28.11.1996 and the decree was drawn up on 1,3. 11.1996 the learned Assistant. Judge became focus officio so far as Title Suit No. 21 of 1994 is concerned and as such he had no power to reopen and review the case and to implead opposite party No. 1 as a defendant in a suit which was admittedly no more alive and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

6. Mr. Roy has placed before me the impugned order and the application of opposite party No. 1 under order 1 Rule 10 of the code of civil procedure as contained in Annexure 'C' to the petition. It appears that the Title Suit No. 21 of 1994 was finally disposed of by judgment dated 28.11.1996 and the learned Assistant judge duly signed the decree on 13.11.1996 thereby formally putting a seal of finality on the suit and the learned Assistant. Judge evidently because functions officer in respect of Title Suit No. 21 of 1994. It is almost preposterous to conceive how the learned Assistant judge in the face of the contested decree dated 28.11.96 could revive a dead case. Which was no longer pending be tore him and over which he had no authority at all, just on the application of a third party. It is evident that after the passing the decree in Title Suit No. 21 of 1994 on 23.11.96 in the absence of any appeal by the aggrieved party before the superior court, Title Suit No. 21 of 1994 became a deed case for all times to come and as such there was no scope to add opposite party No. 1 or anybody else as a defendant in the suit which was no longer alive. If opposite party No. 1 both aggrieved by the decree passed in Title Suit No. 21 of 1994 he might have some other relief available to him but he had no right to be added as a defendant in the suit which has already been finally disposed of by a regular judgment dated 28.11.96. The application of opposite party No. 1 under order I Rule 10 of the code of civil procedure in the facts and circumstances of the case must be held to be a totally misconceived and futile exercise. It is unfortunate that the learned Assistant. Judge totally failed to apply his judicial mind in the facts and circumstances of the case and the settled law bearing on the subject and fell in a serious error of law in passing the impugned order in a most causal and irresponsible manner thereby setting at naught a contested decree in respect of which he was totally fuscous officio. The impugned order clearly suffers from patent legal infirmity and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

7. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and the law bearing on the subject. I find sufficient substance in the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and the same are accordingly sustained. 

8. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned order dated 20.7.1997 passed by the senior Assistant judge, Shariatpur Sadar (Chakindi) in Title Suit No. 21 of 1994 is set aside and the application of opposite party No. 1 under Order 1 Rule 10 of the code of civil procedure filed on 11.3.1997 before the senior Assistant Judge, sadar (Chikindi) stands rejected.

9. The order of stay earlier granted by this court stands vacated. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq, J: By this application the defendant-petitioner of Civil Revision Case seeks for an order dispensing with the direction recorded by this court to file the decree of the Family Court. 

2. The defendant petitioner invoked this court's Civil Revisional Jurisdiction on laying a petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the decisions recorded by the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Bishes Adalat and the Family Appellate Judge in Family Court Appeal No. 56 of 1997 reversing those recorded by the Family Court and Assistant Judge; Fourth Court, Dhaka in Family Suit No. 8 of 1995 dismissing the suit. 

3. In the Civil Revision Petition Rule was sought to be issued calling upon the plaintiff opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 14.11.1999 passed by Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Damon Bishes Adalat, Dhaka in Family Court Appeal No. 56 of 1999 setting aside the judgment and order dated 30.7.1997 passed by the Family Court and Fourth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Family Suit No. 8 of 1995 would not be set aside. Rule was issued accordingly, on 21.11.1999. 

4. In the Civil Revision Petition, decree of the courts below had not been filed and the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner undertook to file the certified copies of the decrees of the courts below within two (2) weeks. Accordingly, at the time of issuance of Rule the plaintiff petitioner was directed to file the decrees of the courts below within two (2) weeks from date in the section. In default, the rule was to stand discharged. 

5. On 7.12.1999 the plaintiff petitioner had only filed the decree recorded by the Family Appellate Court in Family Appeal No. 56 of 1997 in the section vide Entry No. 47928 dated 5.12.1999. But the decree of the Family Court in Family Suit No. 8 of 1995 had not been filed within the time fixed by this court. 

6. Thereafter, an application for dispensing with the direction to file the decree of the Family Court was registered on 6.12.1999 and affidavit had been also shown on that date i.e. on 6.12.1999 which was after the expiry of the period fixed by the court. On 5.12.1999 the period of two (2) weeks expired. The said application was presented before the court on 3.1.2000 and the same appeared in the list on 4.1.2000, and on that date at the instance of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner the matter was adjourned for two weeks. 

7. The application appeared in the list on 18.1.2000. 

8. In the application registered on 6.12.1999 it had been stated that the petitioner applied for the certified copies of both the decrees and got the decree of the appellate court and on query came to know that the decree of the trial court had not been drawn up and being asked the concerned Sheristadar informed that decrees are not drawn up for the cases of the minors and as of the decree of the trial court. The petitioner thus this is, prayed for disposing with the direction to file the decree of the Family Court. 
9. Section 16(1) of the Family Court Ordinance, 1985 enjoins that a Family Court shall pass a decree in such form and manner and shall enter its particulars in such register of decrees prescribed. 

10. Rule 5 of the Family Court Rules, 1985 mandates that in every suit under the Ordinance on passing the judgment, a decree shall be drawn up in form C and shall be signed by the presiding Judge, and the decree shall bear the seal of the Family Court. 

11. Sub-section 1 of section 17 of the Ordinance enshrines that subject to the provisions of sub-section 2, an appeal shall lie from a judgment, decree or order of Family Court to the Court of District Judge. Sub-section 5 of section 17 states that .a certified copy of the judgment, decree or order of the court from which the appeal is preferred shall be attached with the appeal.

 12. The formal expression of a decision of a Civil Court is an order. The word 'Order' occurring in sub-sections 1 and 5 of section 17 may be said to include any "decision" rendered by a court on a question between the parties of a proceeding before the court. The "Decision" may be of both interlocutory and final. The decision rendered by the Family Court is final decision/judgment setting the controversy and determining the rights of the parties in the suit on consideration of the facts, issues and legal aspect and the same is not an interlocutory order. 

13. From the above it has, thus, been manifestly clear that a decree will be drawn up by the Family Court after the pronouncement of the judgment. 

14. On 21.11.1999 at the time of issuance of Rule this court directed the plaintiff-petitioner to file decrees of both the courts below within two (2) weeks from date in the section with the default clause that Rule would stand discharged in the event of non-compliance of the order. The order is quoted hereunder: 
"The plaintiff-petitioner is directed to file the decrees of both the courts below within 2 (two) weeks from date in the section, in default, the Rule shall stand discharged." 

15. The words used in the order is "shall stand discharged" and not "will be discharged". There is a distinction between the words "shall stand discharged" and "will be discharged". In the former, the order reaches to its finality and the order of discharge will have automatic operation leaving no scope for recording any further order and the court retains no jurisdiction to deal with the matter further. In the latter the order does not become final in case of default and the discharge is not automatic and further order will be required for discharge. 

16. On 4.1.2000 the matter was adjourned for two (2) weeks on the basis of a prayer made by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner. There was no scope for recording any further order on the matter after recording the positive order dated 21.11.1999 that the rule would stand discharged in default of filing the decree of courts below within two (2) weeks from date. This order dated 4:1.2000 appears to have been passed under misapprehension and the said order is hereby re-called. 

17. On conspectus, I am of this positive view that this court after recording the order dated 21.11.1999 got no scope for passing any order dispensing with the order directing the plaintiff petitioner to file the decree of the trial court in the section. This application, thus, stands rejected and the rule issued on 21.11.1999, also, stands discharged for default.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J: This rule is directed against the order dated 23.7.98 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka allowing Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1997 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure setting aside the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No, 46 of 1997 of Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka. 

2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that Abdul Khaleque Munshi, the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners, as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title in the suit property and for a declaration that the proceedings before the concerned Revenue Officer are illegal and without jurisdiction in the 4th Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 383 of 1983, contending inter alia that the suit property appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 107 in C.S. Plot 565 comprising an area of 80.68 acres in mouza Tejkunipara within P.S. Keraniganj, now Gulshan, Dhaka originally belonged to Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate the S. khattari urordingly pareas in the name of Kumai Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. As the laid was a marshy land under deep water it was recorded in the C.S. khatian as 'Beel Bhumr. Abdul Khaleque Munshi being the neighboring owner of some other land started filling earth at his own cost during the years 1927-1936 as a result of which land became fit for cultivation and he grew boro paddy therein. It has been stated that the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate having found Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamders in possession of the suit land demanded rent from Abdul Khaleque Munshi and he agreed to pay rent whereupon between 1936-1947, the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate settled 52.17 acres of land by different pattan names on different dates and prepared C.S. B khatian in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamdars and realised rent from them by entering their names in the Tenants' Register No. II, showing the area of land settled and the rate of jama and other charges but Abdul Khaleque Munshi refused to pay rent to the Bhawal. Raj Court of Wards Estate as owner of 28.51 acres of land on the ground that he had been possessing the same on the basis of adverse possession by making it fit for cultivation at his own cost and exertions. As Torab and others illegally cut and took away boro paddy grown by him, Abdul Khaleque Munshi filed a criminal case against those trespassers under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The learned SDO and the appellate Court found the said Abdul Khaleque Munshi in possession of 80.68 acres of land and restrained the trespassers by way of injunction from entering into the case land. Thereafter Torab Ali and 91 others filed a suit for declaration of title against Abdul Khaleque Munshi in the 1st Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 89 of 1962. In the said suit the learned Subordinate Judge found Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin as borgaders under the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin filed Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 in the Court of the District Judge, Dhaka and the learned Additional District Judge, who heard the said appeal, allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment of the trial court on the finding that Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin have right title, interest and possession in the land of CS Plot No. 565. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, Abdul Khaleque Munshi, son of Abdul Hakim, Torab Ali and 90 others filed Second Appeal No. 685 of 1970 before the High Court Division but the said appeal was also dismissed and the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 were affirmed. Against the aforesaid judgment of the High Court Division, Abdul Khaleque Munshi , Son of Abdul Hakim and 91 others, who were the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962, filed CPLA No 84 of 1974 before the Appellate Division but were unsuccessful. Eventually 14.16 acres of land out of the aforesaid 80.68 acres of land in CS Plot No. 565 was acquired by the Rajuk in Land Acquisition Case No. 55 of 1958-59 and compensation was assessed in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamder Amiruddin. As the compensation assessed by the Collector was inadequate, plaintiffs Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin filed Arbitration Case No. 248 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka who ultimately assessed compensation at Tk. 347760/00 in place of Tk. 46368/00 as assessed by the Collector. Against the aforesaid judgment and order the Government filed 2nd Appeal No. 169 of 1970, which was subsequently converted into Civil Revision No. 807 of 1993 before the High Court Division, to reduce the amount of compensation. The Government thus recognized and accepted the title of the plaintiff Abdul Khaleque Munshi in the suit land. In the meantime, RS operation in respect of the land of 80.68 acres along with other lands started. In the Bujarat stage of RS operation plaintiff Abdul Khaleque Munshi got the land of 80.68 acres recorded in his name and in the name of his benamder and transferees but at the attestation stage the Government and other persons, including the principal defendants, filed a dispute case claiming title in 80.68 acres of land. Most of the defendants are either the heirs and heiresses or transferees of the 92 plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962 in the 1st. Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. It was alleged that not only the defendants have got no legal claim or title in the suit land but also their claim is barred by the principle of resjudicata in view of the decision in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 89 of 1962 and Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964. It has been further alleged that the settlement officer of the basis of some false and fabricated documents and in deference to the decision of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962, Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 and Second Appeal No. 685 of 1970 and CPLA No. 84 of 1974, recognised the claim of the defendants and illegally passed order for recording the names of the defendants in the RS khatian in respect of 80.68 acres of land, including 17.3067 acres in the name of transposed plaintiff Nos. 2-12 as shown in schedule 'B' and .4164 acres of land in the name of pro-forma defendant No. 128 as shown in schedule 'C' to the plaint. The land measuring 1.4750 acres out of 52.17 acres has not been recorded the name of pro-forma defendant Nos. 129 and 130, and it has been wrongly shown as vest-ed property. It has been further alleged that no land having vested in the Government, it cannot claim any title thereto. The defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land measuring 80.68 acres and the claim of the defendants and the orders of the settlement officials during the RS operation recording the suit land in the names of the defendants are wrong and hence the suit for declaration of title in the suit land. 

3. Abdul Gafur and Hafizuddin appeared in the suit by filing power on 19.4.84 in Title Suit No. 383 of 1983 before ale of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and prayed for time for filing written statement. Thereafter the suit was transferred to the 1st Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for expeditious disposal of the suit and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 83 of 1985. The said  Abdul Gafur and Hafizuddin, being defendant Nos. 20-25, sought for adjournments for filing written statement in the suit but ultimately they did not file any written statement within a period of 10 years. Ultimately their application for adjournment for filing written statement was rejected by the Court on 14.8.94. Thereafter the Chairman and the Manager of the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for being added as a defendant in the suit and the said prayer was allowed by order dated 11.3.97 whereby the Chairman and the Manager of the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate were made defendant Nos. 131-132. These defendants subsequently filed written statement in the suit denying all material allegations of the plaint and contended inter alia that the suit property belonged to Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate. The suit was ultimately transferred from the 1st. Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka to the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka by order dated 27.3.97 and the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 46 of 1997. In course of time 3.4.97 was fixed for peremptory hearing of the suit and it was eventually decreed on 19.5.97 on contest against defendants Nos. 131 and 132 and ex parte against the rest, excluding the present petitioners. 

4. Thereafter defendant Nos. 20-25 filed an application before the subordinate Judge and commercial court No. 1, Dhaka under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 5.11.94 whereupon Misc. Case No. 10 of 1997 was started. The learned District Judge, Dhaka thereafter transferred the said Misc. Case No. 10 of 1992 to the Subordinate (Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka where it was renumbered as Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997. 

5. The plaintiff resisted the aforesaid Misc. Case by filing written objection denying all its material allegations and contended inter alia that the defendants were never pre-vented by sufficient cause from appearing before the court when the case was called on for hearing. It was further contended that the story of illness of the learned Advocate for the petitioners and of the petitioner No. 1 himself is false and fabricated and as such they are not entitled to any relief in the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

6. At the trial the petitioners of Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 examined 3 witnesses, including their engaged Advocate ABM Muzaffar Hossain and the contesting opposite parties also examined 3 witnesses in support of their respective cases. 


7. The learned Subordinate Judge by his impugned order dated 23.7.98 allowed Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 on contest with a cost of Tk. 15000/00 to the plaintiffs as compensatory cost. 

8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned order dated 23.7.98 allowing Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the petitioners moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

9. Mr. Md. Shafiqul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that in view of the fact that the petitioners of Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 failed to prove that they were prevented by sufficient cause within the meaning of Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure from appearing before the court when the ex parte decree was passed, the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in allowing Misc. Case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on illegal and irrelevant considerations and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that payment of compensatory cost amounting to Tk. 15000/- cannot be a justification for allowing the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such the learned Subordinate Judge was manifestly wrong in not dismissing the case as the petitioners failed to prove that they were prevented by sufficient cause within the meaning of Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

10. Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for opposite party Nos. 1-4, on the other hand, submits that the learned Subordinate Judge on careful consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record on being satisfied about prevention of the petitioners by sufficient cause exercised his judicial discretion in allowing Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 with a cost of Tk. 15000/00 to the plaintiffs and as such the impugned order does not suffer from any illegality or legal infirmity occasioning failure of justice so as to justify interference by this court exercising revisional power under section 115(I) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

11. Mr. Md. Shafiqul Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that although a different view from the one taken by the learned trial court can be taken on the question of sufficient cause, a court of revision will not be justified in reversing the decision of the trial court without finding the order of the trial court illegal and occasioning failure of justice and consequently the impugned order calls for no interference by this court. 

12. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that in view of the fact that Title Suit No. 83 of 1985 was transferred from the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge to the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka on 23.7.98, which was an off date, beyond the knowledge of the petitioners and their engaged Advocate, they had no scope to know about the development of the proceedings of the suit before the court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka, where it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 46 of 1997 and this non-notified transfer must be considered as a sufficient cause preventing the petitioners from appearing before the court when the impugned ex parte order was passed and in that view of the matter the impugned order was rightly set aside by the learned Subordinate Judge on cogent ground and it suffers from no illegality to call for interference in revision. Mr. Ahmed further submits that in view of the fact that a compensatory cost of Tk. 15000/- has been allowed to the plaintiffs towards mitigating their financial losses by exercising sound judicial discretion by the learned trial Court and proper justice has been meted out to the parties, the impugned order has not occasioned failure of justice that may call for interference by this court. 

13. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has placed before us the impugned order as well as an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and written objection filed thereto. The learned Advocate has placed before us the material evidence adduced by the con-tending parties in Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge on detailed discussion of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record found, as of fact, that the petitioners were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the court when the impugned ex parte decree was passed against them. As a safeguard against any prejudice to the plaintiffs the learned Subordinate Judge allowed compensatory cost of Tk. 15000/00 to the plaintiffs as a solatium. This does not in any way come in conflict with the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the petitioners were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the impugned decree was passed. 

14. In support of his submissions Nil-. Ahmed has placed before us the case of MA. Wahab and another Vs. Abul Kalam and another, reported in 44 DLR (Al)), 13 wherein it has been held that if an order of the Court affecting one of the pillars of the suit is meant for communication to all parties concerned, it must be communicated before further progress of the suit. In our case under review, it is clearly found that Title Suit No. 383 of 1983 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka on an off date beyond the knowledge of the petitioners and the fact of such transfer was never-brought to the knowledge of either the petitioners or their engaged Advocate so as to give them the opportunity to pursue their cause before the transferee Court. Transfer of a suit from one court to another Court is a very important matter affecting one of the pillars of the suit and that cannot, in all. fairness, be done on an off date keeping the interested par-ties in the dark about it and that too without bringing it to the notice of the engaged Advocates of the parties at any point of time. This transfer of the suit has indeed prejudiced the petitioners seriously and this along should be construed as a sufficient cause within the meaning of Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure preventing the opposite party petitioners from appearing before the court when the ex parte decree was passed. In support of his contention Mr. Ahmed has placed before me the case of Muhammad Ramjan Sawdagar Vs. AHM Fazlul Huq, reported in 15 DLR, 99 in which a Division Bench of this Court took the view that if an order is passed on an off date, in a case not appearing in the cause list or on a date not fixed for the case, it is incumbent upon° the Court to see that the order is communicated to the engaged Advocate of the concerned parties and when this is not done, the subsequent proceedings must be set aside. Rule 466(2) of the High Court Civil Rules and Order provides that orders directing anything to be done by parties or their pleaders shall be signed by the parties or their Advocates. If further provides that if on an off date an order is passed, endeavors must be made to get it signed by the concerned Advocates before the matter proceeds further. We get instant support to our view in the case of Jahurannessa Vs. Safed Ali Bepari and others, reported in 36 DLR. 253. 

15. In the facts and circumstances of the case, it must be held that the entire exercise by way of transfer of the case to the 1st Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, was made illegally beyond the knowledge and comprehension of the petitioners, opening the gate to the ex parte decree causing serious prejudice to them. The transfer of the case on an off date beyond the knowledge of the petitioners, in the facts and circumstances of the case, smacks of malafides on the part of the plaintiffs to steal a walk over against the petitioners and the question of malafide appears in the fact of the record. 

16. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has not been able to point out any illegality or legal infirmity in the impugned judgment and order in misreading and non-reading of the material evidence or misconstruction of any important document affecting ultimate decision in the case. 

17. In the facts of the case, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge committed no error of law in passing the impugned order and the same has not occasioned failure of justice. We do not, therefore, find any substance in the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. Accordingly, this revision case is found without substance and it must fail. 

18. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost and the impugned order dated 23.7.98 passed by the learned 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka allowing Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is affirmed. 

19. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. 

20. Communicate the order to the learned Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka at once for his information and necessary action.

End.
