full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Tafazzul Islam, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite. party Nos. 1-6 to show cause as to why the order dated 29.10.98 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 41 of 1997 dismissing the application filed by defendant No. 3 petitioners, praying for rejection of the plaint should not be set aside. 

2. The facts relevant for the disposal of the case are that the opposite party Nos. 1-6, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 218 of 1994 in the 3rd Court' of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, which being transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, and Subordinate Judge, Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No. 41 of 1997, seeking declaration that the plaintiffs have got their right, title and interest in the suit land, the suit land was not under requisition in L. A. Case No. 138 of 1961-62 and notification No. 3/94-95 datP4 29.2.94 published in the Daily Inquilab inviting tender for earth filling in the suit land is illegal, malafide and without any jurisdiction. 

3. Thereafter the plaintiffs filed as application under Order 39 Rule-1 and 2 read with Section-151 C.P.C. praying for restraining the defendant No. 3 from filling earth in the suit land. The defendant No. 3 by filing written objection opposed the aforesaid prayer of temporary injunction, the learned Subordinate Judge, after hearing the parties by order dated 18.4.96 allowed the prayer for temporary injunction and restrained The defendant No. 3 from changing the nature and character of the suit land. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 18.4.96, the defendant No. 3 preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1.996 before the High Court Division and also obtained connected Civil Rule No. 163 (FM) of 1996 and after hearing the appeal and the connected Rule, by judgment and order dated 10.3.97 Mr. Justice Golam Rabbani of the High Court Division dismissed the appeal and discharged the connected Rule affirming the judgment and order dated 18.4.96 while Mr. Justice Joynul Abedin, differing with the said judgment delivered by Mr. Justice Gholam Rabbani, allowed the appeal and-disposed of the connected Rule by setting aside the judgment and order dated 18.4.96. Since there was difference of opinion among the learned judges regarding the issue as to whether the suit is barred by the principle of resjudicata in view of the judgment and order dated 12.11.93 passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992, the learned Chief Justice sent the records of the aforesaid appeal to Mr. Justice Kazi Ebadul Hoque, a Judge of the High Court Division, who by his judgment and order dated 19.6.97 agreed with the view expressed by Mr. Justice Md. Joynul Abedin to the effect that in view of the decision of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992 the suit is barred by the principle of resjudicata and accordingly allowed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1996 and the impugned order dated 15.4.96 was set aside and the connected Rule was also disposed of accordingly. Thereafter the defendant No, 3, on 9.8.98, filed an application for rejection of the plaint of Title Suit No. 41 of 1997 on the ground that the suit is barred by the principles of resjudicata in view of the decision of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992, which was also affirmed by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court by judgment dated 27.3.94 passed in Civil Petition for leave Nos. 117 to 119 of 1994, and also the above judgments and orders dated 10.3.97 and 19.6.97 respectively passed by the Special Bench of the High Court Division. The plaintiffs filed written objection to the said application contending inter alia that the application for rejection of the plaint is misconceived and that the question of resjudicata, being mixed question of law and fact in the pre-sent suit, can only be decided on the basis of evidence in the suit itself. 

4. The learned Subordinate Judge aft'?" hearing of the parties, by the impugned order dated 29.10.98 rejected the said application holding that the question of resjudicata may be considered at the time of hearing of the suit along with other issues involved in the suit. 

5. Mr. M. Safiullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in the present suit the plaintiff/petitioner sought for declaration amongst others for their right title and interest of the suit land which was ) requisitioned in L.A. Case No. 138/61-62 and by the judgment dated 22.11.93 passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992, the Rule was discharged holding that the suit was still under requisition and RAJUK was entitled to deal with the suit land as appeared expedient to it, under the provisions of Section 93A of Town Improvement Act and that the suit land, which was requisition in L.A. Case No. 138/61-62 was never de-requisitioned the Appellate Division also affirmed the above judgment. Further, the Special Bench of the High Court Division in F. M. A. No. 81 of 1996 and in connected Civil Rule No. 163/(F.M.) 96 clearly held that the reliefs sought by the plaintiffs/opposite parties declaration that the plaintiffs have right title and interest the suit land and the suit land was not under requisition L.A. case No. 138, 1961-62 are barred by principles of resjudicata and so there is nothing more to be decided by the trial court and accordingly the plaint was liable to be rejected and the learned Subordinate Judge acted illegally not rejecting the plaint. 

6. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate"' for the opposite party, on the other hand, submits that it is only after evidence are led at the trial of the suit, it can be decided as to whether the suit is maintainable or not, there being no cause. of action and the suit being barred by law and the plaintiff, having not stated in the plaint that the suit was barred by principles of - resjudicata, the question as to whether the suit is maintainable or barred by principles of resjudicata in a question of law which can will decided by the trial court in terms of Order-14 Rule-2 read with Section-4 C.P.C. and accordingly the learned Subordinate Judge did not commit any illegality. 

7. We have gone through the contents of the revisional application, the annexure annexed therein and also other papers. It appears that being aggrieved by the order of temporary injunction passed in Title Suit No. 218 of 1994 on 18.4.96 the petitioner preferred first Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1996 also obtained connected Civil Rule No. 163 (F.M.) 96 and therefore the Special Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing the parties, allowed the appeal holding that since in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1994, which was affirmed by the Appellate Division, the High Court Division held that this very suit property was requisition in L.A. Case No. 138/1961-62 and was under derequisitioned and the Special Bench of the High Court Division by judgments and orders dated 10.3.97 and 19.6.97 passed in F.M.A. No 81 of 96, the present suit filed the plaintiffs/opposite party No. 4 is barred by principles of resjudicata. In the aforesaid circumstances the defendants/petitioners on 9.8.98 filed an application under Order-7 Rule-] 1 C.P.C. praying for rejection of the plaint and by the impugned order, the learned Subordinate Judge rejected the said application on the ground that the question of resjudicata may be decided at the trial of suit along with Other issues. It further appears that against the aforesaid orders dated. 10.3.97 and at 19.6.97 passed in F.M.A. No. 81 of 1996, the plaintiffs/opposite parties preferred Civil Appeal No. 1133 of 1997 before the Appellate Division which is pending for hearing. Accordingly the question is whether the observation made by the Special Bench of the High Court Division in the aforesaid F.M.A. No. 81 of 1996 to the effect that the suit filed by the plaintiffs/opposite pal. lies is barred by principles of resjudicata took final shape and became binding and so in the aforesaid circumstances the learned Subordinate Judge was right in whether actually that the issue of resjudicata, which is an issue of law, has to be decided by the trial court at the time of the trial along with other issues? 

8. It is settled principle of law that in an application under Order-7 Rule-11 C.P.C. the defendant has to show the court that taking all the statements made in the plaint as it is, the suit is barred by any law but in the present case, there is nothing to show from the averments as made in the plaint, the suit appears to be barred by law. However if the observations as made by the Special Bench of the High Court Division to the effect that the suit is barred by principles of resjudicata reached its finality, then however the petitioners could argue that the aforesaid view should be read along with the plaint but since a civil appeal has been filed against the above orders on dated 10.3.97 and 19.6.97 of the Special Bench passed in F.M.A. No. 81 of 1996 and the same is pending for hearing in the Appellate Division, at the (the) aforesaid view of the Special Bench of the High Court Division can-not be read along with the plaint of the present suit. However when the suit may be taken up for hearing defendants will be at liberty to raise this issue of resjudicata relying on the judgments passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992 along with observations made in F.M.A. No. 81 of 1996 and under the provision of Order 14 Rule 2 C.P.C. the learned Subordinate Judge may be postponing other issues of fact, hear this issue of law regarding maintainability of the suit on the principles of resjudicata. Accordingly, we are on the view that the learned Subordinate Judge did not commit any error occasioning failure of justice so as to call for any interference by this Court exercising revisional power under Section-115(1) C.P.C. 

9. In the result, the Rule, is discharged without any order as to costs and the impugned order dated 29.10.98 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, and Dhaka and Subordinate Judge in Title Suit No. 41 of 1997 is affirmed. 

10. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

	End.

full_judgment:
MD. TOFAZZUL ISLAM. J :- This Rule at the instance of the defendant petitioners, is directed against the judgment and order dated 28.7.1991 passed by the Assistant Judge, Noakhali Sadar Upazila Additional Court, Noakhali in civil suit No. 733 of 1978 rejecting the prayers of the defendant petitioners for amendment of the written statement. It appears that in this Revisional application the petitioners also challenged some other orders as contained in the aforesaid judgment and order dated 28.7.1991, but one Rule was issued only in respect of refusal of the learned Assistant Judge allowing the prayer for amendment of the written statement. 

2. The plaintiff opposite parties instituted the aforesaid civil suit No. 733 of 1978 seeking declaration of the title to the lands described in the schedule of the plaint of the said suit contending inter alia that they got the suit lands from proforma defendants opposite party Nos. 9 and 10, who are the successors of the original owner of the suit land, by settlement and were paying the rent to the land-lords regularly. But however during the last Diara-Jarip the suit land was recorded in the names of defendants opposite parties Nos. 6 and 7 through mistake and the said defendant opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 illegally sold out suit land to the defendant petitioners Nos. 3 and 4 and the defendants opposite party No. 8 through forged documents and the plaintiffs opposite parties have all along been possession of the suit land. In the aforesaid suit the plaintiffs opposite parties also sought for declaration that the said forged deeds by where the defendants opposite party No. 6 and 7 sold the land to the defendant No. 3, 4 and defendant opposite party No. 8 are inoperative and void. 

3. The defendants petitioners contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material allegations as made in the plaint and contending interalia that one Musleh Uddin purchased a portion of the suit land from the defendant opposite party No. 7 who got the suit land By way of inheritance and also is a recorded tenant and the defendant petitioners purchased that portion of the suit land from the aforesaid Muslehuddin and then the suit land was Mutated in their names through Mutation case No. 115 of 1979-80 and Mutation case No. 7 of 1979-80 and that they are in possession of the suit land with right title interest and they are cultivating the suit land after paying rent regularly. In the aforesaid written statement the petitioner in paragraph 13 stated as follows:- রাজেন্দ্র দাস উক্ত ভূমিতে মালিক দখলকার থাকা অবস্থায় গনু মিয়াকে বন্দোবস্ত দিয়া দখল অর্পনে নিঃসত্ববান হইয়া যান। গনু মিয়া উক্ত ভূমিতে বন্দোবস্ত সুত্রে মালিক ও ভোগ দখলাদার থাকাবস্থায় আমেনা কন্যা ওয়ারিশ বর্তমান রাখিয়া পররোক গমন করেন। আমেনা খাতুন উক্ত ভূমিতে ওয়ারিশ সুত্রে মালিক ও সভোগ দখলদার থাকাবস্থায় নুরের একমাত্র পুত্র ওয়ারিশ রাখিয়া পরলোক গমন করেন। 

 4. In their application for amendment dated 28.7.91 the defendant petitioner prayed for following amendment :- 
বর্ণণার ত্রয়োদশ দফায় বর্ণনায় 6ষ্ঠ পৃষ্টায় লিপি থাকা অবস্থায় শব্দের পূর্বে ‘‘১৩৫৯ বাং সনের ১লা বৈশাখ হেইতে হুকুম নামা সুত্রে বার্ষিক ২০ আনা জমায় ৪.৮৬ ডিং ভূমি আবদুল আজিজকে এবং’’ ব্যাকাংশ লিপি হইবে। এবং তৎপর ঐ পৃষ্টার 7ম লাইনে লিপি থাকা উক্ত শব্দ কর্তন ক্রমে তদস্থলে ‘‘তাহার অংশের হিস্যে।।. আনা অংশের।।. শব্��� লিপি হইবে। 

5. The learned Assistant Judge however by the impugned order rejected the aforesaid prayer for amendment on the ground that since the defendant petitioners filed the additional written statement, his application for amendment of the said written statement can not be allowed. 

6. From the supplementary Affidavits filed on behalf of the defendant-petitioners it appears that during the pendency of the aforesaid civil suit No. 735 of 1978, in terms of the prayer of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1, the court bellow, vide order No. 79 dated 23.8.1990, amended the plaint adding the name of the plaintiff Nos. 2 to 4 in the plaint and vide order No. 95 dated 13.5.1991 the plaint was again amended adding the name of the plaintiff opposite party No. 5 in the plaint. 

7. Mr. Moshfiquddin Bokhtear, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned Assistant Judge acted illegally in refusing the prayer for amendment of the written statement merely on the ground that since this defendants filed Additional written statement, the prayer for amended of the written statement can not be allowed. The learned Advocate further submits since vide order dated 23.8.1990 and 13.5.1991 the learned Assistant Judge, in terms of the prayer of the plaintiff, amended the plaint, the filing of additional written statement by The defendant petitioners was nesseciated and by the said. additional written statement the defendant petitioners merely added some statement which was nesseciated in view of the amendment 9-14 plaint. On the other hand by the application praying for amendment of the written statement the defendant petitioners merely sought to correct the some mistake which was made the original written statement and. so the filing of the additional statement have no connection what so ever with the filling the application for amendment of the written statement. 

8. Mr. Mel. Ibrahim Khalil, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties however submits that the defendant petitioner filed the aforesaid application for amendment of written statement only with the purpose of delaying the disposal of the suit which was filed in the year 1978. 

9. I have gone through the records. It appears from the order that though the suit was filed in the year 1978, the plaintiff themselves prayed for amendment as late as in the year 1990-1991 and the learned court below allowed the prayer of the plaintiff for amendment of the plaint and thereby the plaintiff Nos. 2 to 5 were added as plaintiff and view of the above amendment, the filling of additional written statement  by the defendant petitioner was nesseciated. Since the plaintiff themselves filed the application for amendment after 12/13 years after filling of the suit, how the plaintiff now an take the stand that the defendant lied the aforesaid application dated 
28.7.1991 2 for amendment of the written Statement-in order to delay the deposition of Suit. From the original statement are made by the defendant made in paragraph 13 of the written statement and the corrections sought to made by the defendant in their application dated 28.7.1991 praying for amendment of the written statement contents of which have been quoted above, it appears that the afar said amendment of the written Statement as sought by the defendant petitioners will not change nature and character of the present suit and further the proposed amendment may also be necessary for the purpose of determining real question in controversy between the parties.

10. In the result the 'Rule is made absolute and the impugned order dated 28.7.1991 passed by the Assistant Judge. Noakhali .Sadar Upazila Additional Court, Noakhali in civil suit No, 733 of 1976 is set aside, there will be no. order as to cost. The court below is directed to dispose of the case as early as possible. 

End.

full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J: This Rule is directed against the order dated 2 .6.93 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Muradnagar, Comilla in Title Suit No. 44 of 1990 (Partition) rejecting the petitioners application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for impleading them as plaintiffs in the suit.

2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that opposite party Nos. 1 & 2 as plaintiffs instituted on 24.7.90 a suit in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge Muradnagar being Title Suit No. 44 of 1990, praying for partition of the suit property by metes and bounds on declaration of title in 30 decimals of land out of 68 decimals of land in suit plot No. 162, previously under Madan No. 12 and Khatian No. 137 of Mouza Nagarpur under Muradnagar Police Station, on the basis of a deed of gift and by way of inheritance. The said suit was eventually decreed ex-parte on 30.5.91. Thereafter defendant No. 4 Ansar Ali (who is opposite party No. 3 before this Court) filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 6.6.92, following which Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1992 was started and the learned Assistant Judge by his impugned order dated 29.10.92 eventually allowed the said case and set aside the ex-parte decree dated 6.6.92 and restoring the suit to its original file and number. Thereafter the petitioner purchased 11 decimals of the suit land from defendant Nos. 1 by 2 separate sale deeds dated 18.7.1991 and duly got into possession in the suit property. Thereafter the present petitioners got their names mutated in respect of the suit property and they have been owning and possessing it on payment of rent in their names to the appropriate authority.

3. As the suit progressed the present petitioners on 26.6.93 filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for adding them as co-plaintiffs alleging inter alia that the plaintiff appears to have entered into an unholy alliance with the defendants as a result of which he is not showing any interest in the proceedings of the suit. It was further alleged that since their vital interests are involved in the suit they are necessary parties thereto, otherwise their interests would suffer. The said application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure has been annexed to the petition and has been marked as Annexure "A" thereto.

4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge by his impugned order dated 21.6.1993 rejected the petitioner's application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding inter alia that since the petitioners purchased only a portion of the suit property during the pendency of the suit and they are claiming through the plaintiffs the are not necessary parties in the present suit. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 21.6.93, the petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

5. Mr. M. Faruque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge erred in law in refusing the petitioners' prayer under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure on erroneous view of law in the face of the allegations of fraud and collusion between the plaintiff and the defendants materially affecting their vital interests and the same has occasioned failure of justice.

6. None appears to oppose the Rule.

<u>7. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has placed before me the application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure alleging that of late the plaintiff has entered into an unholy alliance with the defendants and he is showing scant interest in prosecuting the suit with due diligence adversely affecting the vital interests of the petitioners and as such the petitioners' should be impleaded as co-plaintiffs in the suit. There is no denial of the assertions made in this application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In view of the fact that the petitioners have purchased a substantial portion of the suit property from the plaintiff by a registered sale deed and they are allegedly in possession thereof, it is evidence the their vital interests are involved in the suit and as such their presence in the suit appears to be just and proper in the interest of justice. Mr. Faruque Ahmed submits that the interests of the petitioners may be well-served if they are made defendants in the suit so that they may have there fill say in respect of their interests therein. Since the petitioners were not at the scene when the suit was filed and they became interested in the result of the suit subsequently, they cannot be made co-plaintiffs over the head of the unwilling plaintiff although they may have vital interests in the suit property and they are likely to suffer injury if the suit is decided in their absence opening up the doors for multiplicity of litigations. Order 1 Rule 10 (2) C.P.C. also leans support to the view that all necessary and proper parties should be impleaded in a single suit/case at any stage of the proceeding for avoiding multiplicity of litigations involving unnecessary harassments to the contending parties. The petitioners, are then found necessary parties in the suit and consequently the impugned and order suffers from and legal infirmity.</u>

8. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, I am constrained to hold that the learned Senior Assistant Judge, erred in law in rejecting the petitioners application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure in a mechanical way. In the facts of the case, the ends of justice will be sufficiently met if the Petitioners are impleaded as defendants in the suit as prayed for by the petitioners.

9. In the result, the Rule succeeds and is accordingly made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order is hereby set aside and petitioners applications dated 21.6.93 under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is accordingly allowed and they are impleaded as defendants in the suit. The learned Senior Assistant Judge is directed to proceed with the suit according to law after making necessary amendments in the plaint.

10. Since this is an old case the learned Assistant Judge is directed to dispose of the suit as expeditiously as possible, preferably within six months from the date of receipt of this order.

11. Communicate this order of this Court to the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Muradnagar at once. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

End.

Mahfuzur Rahman, J.: This Rule under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against an order passed by Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka on 30.11.97 in Partition Suit No. 176 of 1995 staying all further proceeding of Execution Case No. 16 of 1995 pending in the court of the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka till the disposal of the suit. 

2. The short facts relevant are that the petitioners being plaintiff instituted SCC Suit No. 8 of 1994 before the SCC Judge and Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for eviction of the tenant opposite party No. I from the shop room No. 2 in the ground floor of holding No. 20 Islampur Road within P.S. Kotwali, Dhaka on the ground of default in payment of monthly rent claiming opposite party No. 1 to be their monthly tenant. The petitioners also filed SCC Suit No. 9 of 1994 in the same court for eviction of the opposite party No. 1 from shop room No. 9 in the 1st floor of the same holding. The opposite party No. 1 did not enter appearance in SCC Suit No. 9 of 1994 and the same was decreed ex-parte on 25.9.94. 

3. Thereafter the opposite party No. 1 filed an application for restoration of the suit after setting aside the ex-parte decree in Miscellaneous Case No. 66 of 1994 which was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 28.10.96 and then the petitioner started Execution Case No. 16 of 1995. 

4. The opposite party No. 1 filed written statement in S.C.C. Suit No. 8 of 1994 admit-ting that he was a tenant under the petitioners but he purchased the portion of the suit premises from Mrs. Akhtar Banu, another co-sharer of the suit premises by registered sale deed dated 3.8.85 and the suit was decreed against him Opposite party No. I filed revisional application against the aforesaid judgment and order under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act -before the High Court Division which was numbered as civil Order No. 659/96 and the Rule was discharged on 7.3.96 in limine. The opposite party No. 1 moved the Appellate Division by filing Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 276/96 which was rejected by their Lordships judgment and order dated 7.7.96 holding that: it is established that a person is a tenant he cannot be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to resist a suit for eviction by his landlord as a subsequent purchaser from a co-sharer without surrendering his possession to his landlord. As, in the instant case, it is found that the petitioner was a tenant under the respondents to whom he paid rents upto December, 1900, he is debarred ,from setting up a claim of title in himself to resist the decree for eviction." During the pendency of the aforesaid SCC Suit No. 8.94 the opposite party filed a Partition Suit No. 175/95 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge at Dhaka impleading the petitioners as defendants and opposite party No. 2 claiming partition of the alleged purchased shop of the aforesaid holding No. 20, Islampur Road, Dhaka.

5. On the application by opposite party No. 1 in Partition Suit No. 176/95 under Order 21 Rule 29 of the Code the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 24.7.96 stayed further proceedings of SCC Suit No. 8/94 pending in the court of the Assistant Judge 3rd Court, Dhaka. The petitioners also on 11.8.96 filed an application for setting aside the stay order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge in Partition Suit No. 176/95 and the opposite party No. 1 filed another application on 27.11.96 under Order 21 Rule 29 of the Code before the learned Subordinate Judge in the same suit for stay of the proceedings of SCC Suit No. 9/94 and the Execution Case No. 16/95 pending before the Assistant Judge. 3rd Court, Dhaka both the applications filed by the petitioners dated 11.8.96 and the application filed by opposite party No. 1 dated 27.11.96 were heard by the learned Subordinate Judge who by his order dated 30.11.96 allowed the petition dated 27.11.96 filed by the opposite party No. 1 praying for stay of further proceeding of Execution Case No. 16/95 and dismissed the petition dated 11.6.96 filed by the petitioners for setting aside the order dated 24.7.96 staying the further proceeding of SCC Suit No. 8/94. 

6. As against that the petitioners moved this court and obtained this Rule. 

7. Mr. Mahmudul Islam the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that in view of the established legal position as enunciated by the Appellate Division in the case of Md. Atiqullah Vs. Mrs. Shanawara Begum and others, reported in 16. B.L.D. (AD) 260, the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law resulting in his decision occasioning serious failure of justice in passing the impugned order. He further submits that in the aforesaid case the Appellate Division clearly held that a tenant cannot be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to resist a suit for eviction by his landlord surrendering his possession to his landlord, the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in his decision resulting in an error of law occasioning serious failure of justice. He lastly contends that both the suits are not in the same court and order 21 Rule 29 of the Code has got no manner of application in this case when the proceedings was stayed are not pending in the same court. 

8. None appears to oppose the Rule. 9. We have perused the application and the relevant law. Admittedly both the SCC Suits are in the court of the Assistant Judge, 3rd court, Dhaka and another in the court of Subordinate Judge. 3rd court, Dhaka who passed the impugned order. Order 21 Rule 29 provides as follows:-
"9. Where a suit is pending in any court against the holder of a decree of such court, on the part of the person against whom the decree was passed, the court may, on such terms as to security or otherwise, as it thinks fit, stay execution of the decree until the pending suit has been decided" Admittedly both the suits are not in the same court and the impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is absolutely Illegal and has got no manner of application in this case. In the decision referred by Mr. Islam reported in 16 BLD (AD) 260 their Lordships have also referred: 
"The consistent view of the Appellate Division is that once it is found that a person is a tenant he cannot be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to resist a suit for eviction by his landlord as a sub-sequent purchaser from a co-sharer without surrendering his possession to his landlord. In the instant case, the petitioner was found as a tenant under the respondents to whom he had paid rent and as such he is debarred from setting up a claim of title in himself to resist the decree for eviction." 

10. In view of the discussions and the decision referred above we are of the view that the impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge cannot be sustained in law and is liable to be set aside. 

11. In the result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd court, Dhaka on 30.11.97 staying the Execution Case No. 16/95 of the court of the Assistant Judge, 3rd court, Dhaka is hereby set aside. 

12. The stay granted earlier by this court is hereby vacated. 

13. Communicate the order to the court below at once. 

	End.

full_judgment:
Md. Nurul Islam, J: This rule is issued upon the opposite party No. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 4-1-96 passed by the District Judge, Rajshahi in Miscellaneous Execution Case No. 1 of 1983 should not be set aside. 

2. The petitioner filed a Miscellaneous Case No.67 of 1975 under Section 27 of the presidents order No. 7 of 1973 against the present petitioner for recovery of Tk. 33,728.32. The opposite party No. 1 look loan of Tk. 15,000/- and Tk. 10,000/- at the rate of interest 7% and 8 percent per annum respectively from the petitioner on the terms incorporation the Mortgaged deed, registered on 2-6-66 and 2-1-74 for construction of a residential building vide loan case No. Raj-417. The opposite party No. 2 was grantor for repayment of loan under the terms of letter of guarantee executed by him on 1-1-74. According to terms of the Mortgage deed the opposite party No. 1 was to pay the borrowed amount with interesting monthly installment of Tk. 138.37 and Tk. 90.07 for a period of 15 years. The opposite party failed to pay the monthly installment of 25 months and did not pay the same to the petitioner. Tk. 33,728.32 with interest Miscellaneous Case for recovery of Tk. 33,728.32 with interest upto 30-6-78 allowed the Misc. Case on admission and gave 132 monthly installments for realisation of the aforesaid money. The petitioner challenged the order before this court in first Misc, Appeal No. 400 of 1979 and a Division Bench of this court by order dated 31-5-82 allowed the appeal and set aside the order dated 30-6-78 with direction to the respondent No. 1 to pay the inure outstanding at a time forthwith and in default mortgage property is liable to be sold under Article No. 27 of P. 0. No. 7 of 1973. Thereafter the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Execution Case No. 1 of 1983 to the District Judge, Rajshahi for execution of the decree for principal and interest therein. The opposite party Judgment debtor after depositing the decretal amount Tk. 33,728.32 filed a petition before the learned District Judge, Rajshahi for disposal of the execution case on full satisfaction. The learned District Judge by his order dated 4-1-86 disposed of the execution case on full satisfaction. Being aggrieved at and dis-satisfied with the aforesaid order the petitioner preferred. this application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil procedure and obtained 
the present rule. 


3. Mr. Shahid Alam, the learned Advocate for petitioner, submit that the High Court Division in it order directed the respondent to pay the entire outstanding at a time that means entire borrower money plus interest till realisation. He further submitted that the learned District 
Judge mis-understood the High Court's order by stator High Court order to pay amount due in the Misc. Case and not the subsequent interest. He again submitted that the learned District Judge Allowed , the Misc. Case on Admission that means he allowed all the prayers of the petitioner as stated in the plaint which includes the prayer for interest upto realisation of borrowed money. It is admitted that the opposite party No. 1 borrowed Tk. 15,000/- and 10,000/- from petitioner at the rate of Interest 7% and 8 percent respectively and opposite party No. 2 was the grantor for repayment of said loan. It is further admitted that the petitioner filed a case for realisation of Tk. 33,728.32. The learned District Judge by his order dated 30-6-78 allowed the Misc. Case and the said order runs as follows: 
[That the Misc. Case is allowed on admission. The amount of Tk. 33,728.32 as claim in the petition will be realised in 132 monthly installments. Its installment of Tic. 255/- each the last one for the balance starting from July/78 payable by 7th of each month. In default of any installment the balance remaining unpaid will he realised by sate of the mortgage properties of sufficient portion thereof.] Subsequent installment be refunded. The learned District Judge did not mention specifically about the prayer for interest of the petitioner. The aforesaid order is 
challenged before this court and a Division Bench of this court in its judgment dated 31-5-82 observed that the learned District Judge had no jurisdiction in awarding installments 132 in numbers for recovery of outstanding amounts. The court set aside the order of the learned District Judge with direction that the Respondent is liable to pay entire outstanding at a time forthwith. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that entire outstanding means principal amount and interest thereof. 

4. In the original Misc. Case No. 67 of 1975 the outstanding amount claimed for is Tk. 33,728.32. The learned District Judge by his order dated 30.6.78 Stated that the Specific amount claimed by the petitioner will be realised. About the prayer for interest in the plaint the learned 
District Judge is silent in his order that means that he did not allow the said prayer. Similarly the entire outstanding to be paid at a time as ordered by this court is the amount decreed by the District Judge by his order dated 4-1-86. In the appeal before this court no prayer was made by the petitioner for the interest till realisation of the principal amount. In this respect, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, Mr. Mansur Habib, submitted that the outstanding amount 
means decretal amount given in the decree of the Misc. Case No. 67 of 1972. He further submitted that since there was no specific order for interest of the decretal amount to realisation of the sum the opposite party may get benefit of same according to Section 34(2) of the Code of Civil procedure decree is silent with respect to the payment of further interest on such aggregate sum as aforesaid from the date of payment of the further interest on such aggregate sum as aforesaid from the date of payment of the decree to the date of payment or other earlier date, the court shall be deemed to have refused such 'interest, and a separate suit there-fore shall not lie. 'In a case reported in 37 D. L. R. (Ad)-1 (M/S.M.M. Ispahani Vs. Sonali Bank) their lordships hold.' In principal, what appears from Section 34 C.P.C. itself is that the court is not bound by what is provided in the contract itself, the matter of awarding interest being completely within its discretion,' In the instant case the trial court as well as the appellate court assailant about interest of the amount claimed by it will be deemed to have been refused provided that which is not done inadvertently or due to mistake. When interest is not awarded in the decree it can not be executed. As per order of the High Court the execution case was filed by the opposite party for realisation of the entire decretal amount that is outstanding amount. The learned District Judge by his order dated 4-1-86 rightly disposed of the execution case No. 1 of 83 on full satisfaction. In the above facts and circumstances I find no illegality in the aforesaid order of the learned District Judge. So I find no substance in the submission made by the Advocate for the petitioner. 

5. In the result, the rule is discharged without cost. Sent down the lower courts record immediately. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mohammad Gholam Rabbani, J: This Rule has arisen out of the following circumstances: Petitioner before us Mir Amanullah got a money decree of Tk. 80000/- in Money Suit No. 6 of 1986 from the Court of Subordinate Judge, Munshiganj, against defendants National Cold Storage Ltd. and its Managing Director Tofazzel Hossain Chowdhury. The decree was passed on 13.8.88. Then the .decree was put into execution in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1989 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Munshiganj. The Execution case is pending. In the decree plaintiff was awarded interest at the rate of 16% on the decretal amount from the date of the decree till realisation on 6.4.95 the judgment-debtor deposited an amount of Tk. 61.500/-. It appears from the certified copy of the order-sheet of the execution case annexed to the order-sheet of the execution case annexed to the revisional application the Execution court who is also 1st Court of Subordinate Judge passed certain orders allowing the application of the judgment-debtors to pay the decreetal amount in instalments and also to remit the interest as decreed. Ultimately, the decree-holder filed an application for review of the said orders but the application for review was rejected on 19.11.95 and hence this Rule. 

2. Mr. Md. Shamsul Huda the learned Advocate for the decree-holder, submits that all the aforesaid orders passed by the Executing Court acted 'illegally in refusing to review those on the application filed by the decree-holder. It is well-settled law that the executing court in required by law to execute the decree as it stands and it cannot go beyond the decree in any way. 

3. No one appears to oppose the Rule. 

 4. We, therefore, hold that the afore-said orders passed by the learned Subordinate Judge while executing the money decree in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1989 are wholly illegal and with-out jurisdiction. 

5. The Rule is made absolute. Orders passed on 20.10.94, 22.7.95, 30.8.95 and 19.11.95 by the learned Subordinate Judge in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1989 are set aside.

 It is ordered that according to the decree under execution the decree-holder is entitled to get interest at the rate of 16% on Tk. 61,500/- from 13.8.88 to 5.4.95 and also is entitled to get Tk. 18,500/- with interest at the rate of 16% thereon from 13.10.88 till realisation. The decree shall now be executed for the amount as ordered.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq, J: Feeling aggrieved by an order dated 12.7.1999 recorded by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 refusing to record an order of injunction in an application under Section 131 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Decree-Holder plaintiff-petitioner approached this Court in a Civil Revision petition under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for quashing the said order whereupon Rule was issued. 

2. The portrayal of the essential facts forming the background of the Civil Revision petition may conveniently be stated and noticed.  

3. The petitioners as plaintiffs laid a suit being Small Causes Court Suit No, 1 of 1992 in the Third Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka impleading Ansar Ali, the husband of the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 and father of the opposite party Nos. 3 to 7 for a decree of ejectment from the suit property. The suit was, thereafter, converted as Title Suit and renumbered as Title Suit No. 201 of 1994. The defendant Ansar Ali presented written statement traversing the allegations contained in the plaint.

4. The defendant Ansar Ali died during the pendency of the suit leaving behind the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as wives and opposite party Nos. 3 to 7 as sons and daughters and they were substituted as defendants in the suit. The defendants adopted the written statement presented by their predecessor Ansar Ali. 

5. The suit was decreed on contest against the defendants opposite parties. 

6. The plaintiff-petitioner as Decree Holder put the decree in execution by laying execution case being Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1999. 

7. Nasima Azad, the heir daughter of deceased defendant Ansar Ali, opposite party No. 7 laid a case being Miscellaneous Case No. 82 of 1996 under Rule 13 of Order 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit to its file and number on setting aside the decree. The said Miscellaneous case was withdrawn following a compromise entered between the Decree-Holder-plaintiff-petitioner and Nasima Azad. The Judgment-Debtor defendant opposite party Bashirunnessa, there-2 after on 15.2.1999 presented an application-under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration or the suit on setting aside the ex-party decree. The said application had been registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 1999. 

8. Learned Assistant Judge on the basis of an application from the Judgment Debtor-opposite party Basirunnessa stayed the proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1999 till disposal of the Miscellaneous Case No, 15 of 1999. The Decree Holder Plaintiff-petitioners, thereafter, presented an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for expunging the proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 1999 and order of stay recorded in Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1999. The said petition having been rejected by the learned Assistant Judge, the Decree-Holder-plaintiff-petitioner side invoked this Court's Civil Revisional Jurisdiction on laying a petition under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Rule was issued on the said application. The Civil Revision petition has been renumbered as Civil Revision No' 2498 of 1999. The Judgment Debtor-opposite parties being armed with the order of stay started raising kancha and semi-pucca structures and made preparation for making permanent construction on the suit property to induct some subtenants creating serious complication with regard to possession. The Decree-Holder-plaintiff-petitioners, there-after, presented an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for an order of injunction restraining the Judgment-Debtor-opposite parties from making pucca, semi-pucca, kancha or any other construction on the decreetal property and inducting any person thereupon till disposal of the case. 

9. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, by the order dated 12.7.99 kept the application on the record taking the view that the proceeding of the suit having been stood stayed, the application did not merit any consideration. The said order is the subject matter of challenge in the Civil Revision Petition. 

10. Mr. Md. Sirajul Islam Khan, along with Mr. Md. Ramzan Ali, the learned Advocates appeared for the petitioners of Rule. The opposite party No. 1 is represented by Mr. Mashuque Hossain Ahmed, with Mr. Md. Shah Alam Sarker, the learned Advocate.

11. The grounds pressed into service in the Civil Revision Petition are catalogued hereunder: 
(i) The lawer court acted illegally in not exercising its inherent power in issuing the order of injunction as sought by the Decree-Holder-plaintiff -petitioners. 
(ii) Ends of justice demanded an immediate an order of injunction as sought by the Decree-Holder-plaintiff -petitioners and the lower court failed to consider that the petitioners had no alternative remedy avail-able to them in the fact and circumstances of the case. 
(iii) The Decree-Holder-plaintiffs-petitioners are entitled under the fact and circumstances of the case—the protection of the learned court through issuance of an order of injunction as prayed by them. 

12. In the wake of grounds so pressed the question that survives for determination is whether in the fact, circumstances and also in the safe dispensation of justice, the Decree-Holder-plaintiffs-petitioners demand an issuance of injunction in their favour. 

13. In approaching the said question the inherent power of the Court and principles of law in issuance and non-issuance of injunction are to be seen and considered. 

14. Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not formulate any new doc-trine but only a legislative recognition of the well known principle that every court has inherent power to act exdebitio justiate and to do that the real justice for the administration of which it exists. Inherent power has not been conferred on the Court but it is a power inherent in the Court by virtue of its duty to do justice between the parties. Under Section 151 of the Code the Court acts debitio justiate according to equity, justice and good conscious of a court. 

15. The words as may be necessary for the ends of justice" appearing Section 151 
of the Code gives inherent power to High Court Division also to interfere with the order of the Subordinate Court and to record any order to secure the ends of justice. Courts including this Court are possessed of inherent power as may be necessary to do complete justice between the parties according to a situation which may arise in the course of a proceeding and the said power is fairly wide enough to meet any circumstances in the said dispensation of justice. 

16. An injunction is a writ framed according to the circumstances of the case commanding an act which the court records as essential to justice or restraining an act which it esteems contrary to equity and good conscience. In other words, an injunction is an equitable relief, a strong arm of equity. It is to be issued in aid of justice and not to aid injustice. Temporary injunction is mere provisional in its nature and its sole object is to preserve the subject  matter in controversy without determining the rights of the parties and to prevent the  doing of an act whereby the subject matter of the right in the suit property or controversy may be in danger. (Emphasis put) 

17. In the case in hand admittedly the,, Decree-Holder-plaintiff-petitioners got decree, no matter whether ex parte or contested in a suit for ejectment and put decree into execution in an execution case. The Judgment Debtor-defendant-opposite party side on the basis of Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 1999 under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, obtained an order of stay of the proceeding of Title Execution Case. It is the positive assertion of the Decree-Holder-plaintiff-petitioners that the Judgment Debtors-defendant opposite-party side on the strength of order of stay started kancha, semi-pucca structures and also permanent construction on 11the suit property and by way of an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Decree-Holder-plaintiff -petitioners prayed before the court for exercising Court's inherent jurisdiction in recording an order of injunction restraining the Judgment Debtors defendant opposite party side from making any kancha, semi-pucca or permanent structure and construction. The decree so obtained by the plaintiffs Decree-Holders-petitioners stands good so long the same is not set aside in Miscellaneous case laid by the Judgment Debtors defendant-opposite party side. Taking the advantage of an order of stay of the proceedings of the Title 
Execution case the Judgment Debtors defendant opposite party side cannot be allowed to make semi-pucca, kancha structure and permanent construction by changing the nature and character of the suit property causing loss and damage to the Decree-Holder-plaintiffs-petitioners. In 
the fitness of the facts and circumstances the learned Assistant Judge was required to record an order of injunction restraining the Judgment Debtors defendant opposite party side from raising structure and making construction kancha, semi-pucca or pucca on the suit property. The learned 
Assistant Judge, thus, appears to have committed a substantial error in not issuing an order of injunction as prayed by the Decree-Holder-plaintiff -petitioners. 

18. It is well settled that the principal  object behind all legal formalities is to safeguard the paramount interest of Justice  and mere technicalities unless offering an  insurmountable hurdle should not be  allowed to defeat the ends of justice  (Emphasis laid). To save the paramount interest of justice the learned Assistant Judge was duty bound to record an order of 
injunction over looking the technicality that proceeding of the Title Execution case stood stayed. It is always to be borne in mind that—law and procedure primarily holds banner of Justice. (Emphasis put). 

19. The power to be exercised under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is  
supervisory which may be also exercised  suo motu. The High Court Division is  clothed with supplementary power and  Superintendence and control over the  Judgment and Orders and action of the  Courts subordinate to the High Court Division and the power of Revision is  
intended to be exercised with a view to sub-serve and not to defeat the ends of Justice.  
(Emphasis laid). 

20. In the fact and circumstances of the case, to secure Justice, in exercise of the power under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure I am inclined to issue an order of injunction. The Judgment Debtor defendant opposite parties are here-by restrained by an order of injunction from raising any structure, kancha, semi- pucca or pucca or making permanent construction on the suit property till disposal of Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 1999. 

21. Resultantly, the Rule arising out of Civil Revision petition is made absolute. 

22. The order of status-quo granted by this Court at the time of issuance of Rule stands modified and order of injunction is granted in the manner stated above. 

23. No. costs. 

End.

Ashkor Ali ------ opposite Party.
full_judgment:
M. Bazlur Rahman Talukder, J: This revisional application under Section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure arises against the judgment and order dated 30.5.1995 passed by Mr.Md. Zafrol Hasan, Senior Assistant Judge, Keraniganj, in Title Suit No .131 of .1994 refusing the stay of Title Suit No. 131 of 1994 under Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure till disposal of Title Suit No. 151 of 1994 of the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. 

2. Short facts involved in the case are that on 24.7.94 opposite party No. 1 Askar Ali, as the sole plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 151 of 1994 in the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against a large number of defendants, III in number, impleading the petitioners as defendants Nos. 61-67 for a declaration that the plaintiff is the sole owner of 2.90 acres of land of schedule property including Plot. No. 759 bearing an area of .35 acres in Mouza Modhyer Char and Plot No. 132 embracing an area of .69 acres of Mouza Napiadi and that .the, S.A. records were wrongly published. 3. Subsequently on 16.10.94 the said Askor Ali opposite party- No. 1 in this revisional application together with his son Din Mohammad, opposite party No. 2 jointly brought a suit being Title Suit No. 131 of 1994 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Keraniganj, Dhaka for permanent injunction againg.1 the present petitioners as defendants so as to prevent the said defendants from of eating any obstacles in the possession of the plaintiffs in Plot No. 759 of Modhyer Char and Plot No. 132 of Napiadi Mouza alleging title and possession therein. 

4. While both the suits were in progress on 25.5.95 the defendant petitioners filed an application before the learned Assistant Judge Keraniganj under Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for stay of the subsequent suit being Title Suit No. 131 of 1994 of the said Court, pending the hearing of the previous suit being Title suit .No. 151 of 1994 of the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on the ground that the matter in issue in the two suits is directly and substantially the name for the reason that the disputed question of the plaintiffs Title in the suit land including .Plot No. 759 of Mousa Moclhyer Char and Plot. No. i 132 of Mouza Napiadi is involved in -both the- suits together with the question of possession.  

5. The learned Assistant Judge by his order dated 30.5.1995 rejected the petition of the defendant petitioners holding that the material issue in the two suits in not directly and substantially the same the nature and character of the two cases being different, the cases of action of the two suits were also different and as such section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not-applicable 'and with the above observations, the learned Assistant Judge rejected the petition of the defendants under Section 10 of the Code Of Civil procedure. 

6. Defendant petitioners being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned Judgment and order No. 15 dated 30.5.1.995 passed by the learned Assistant Judge Keraniganj in Title Suit No. 131 .of 1994 has preferred the present revisional application.  

7. Mr. S. R Karmaker and Mr. L. Gomes the learned Advocates appeared for the petitioners and Mr. Fariduddin Md. Reza the learned Advocate appeared for the opposite parties No. 1-2. Mr. Karmaker appears with Mr. L. Gomes for the petitioners has submitted that the learned Court below committed a substantial error of law failing to evaluate that Section 10 of the code of Civil Procedure contains no reference whatsoever to the subject matter or the cause of action of the case. 

8. Mr. Karmaker has further submitted that the learned Court below committed a substantial error of law in failing to evaluate that the final decision being reached in the Previous Suit such decision may operate as reajudicate in the subsequent suit. Mr. Karmaker, has further submitted that it is not the requirement of law that the matter on the issue involved in the two suits should be totally identical, but they must be substantially same. Mr. Karmaker further submitted that if the subsequent suit Title suit No. 131of 1994) in not stayed it would result in unnecessary trial of the suit and litigation expenses of both the parties and there my be possibility of confliction - judgments in the two proceedings. Mr. Karmaker has further submitted that the Court below fell into an error of law in not perceiving that the subject matter in issue in subsequent suit is also materially, directly and substantially in issue in the previously instituted suit between the parties and as such the learned Assistant Judge ought to have taken notices that he has jurisdiction to entertain an application tinder Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

9. Mr.Karmaker has further submitted that Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is to prevent conflicting judgments in respect of matters directly and substantially involved  bill the suits so that the parties e not prejudiced to the detriment of their interest and that the learned assistant. Judge has not considered the vital aspect of the matter resulting thereby failure of justice in his decision. 

10. Mr. Karmaker lastly submitted that the Court has inherent power to stay the suit even where section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not strictly apply for ends of justice. 

11. Mr karmaker has submitted by referring to plaints of the aforesaid two suits i.e Title Suit. No. 151 of 1994 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and the Title Suit No. 131 of 1994 pending in the Court of the Assistant Judge Keraniganj, Dhaka, that the two suit: Plots being Dag No. 759 of Khatian No. C. 5.160, of Mouza Modhyer Char and Dag No. 132 of C. S. Khatian No. 67 of Napiadi Mouza are the 'same suit plots in both the suits. 

12. Mr. Karmaker by referring to 45 DLR (HCD) Page 374 'has submitted that the subject matter in issue is material and not the claim of parties. He has further submitted that the learned assistant Judge/Munsif also committed an error of law to say that the nature and character of the two suits are different. 

13. Mr. Karmaker then referred to AIR 1972 (Cal) Page 128 and has submitted that complete identity of either the subject matter of the parties is not required in an application under. Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

14. Mr. Karmaker then referred to AIR 1973 (Pat) Page 196 and has submitted that for determining whether the matter directly and substantially in issue in former suit as well as in subsequent suit is the same of the test to be applied is whether adjudication of the matter directly and subsequently arising in the former suit ill decide materially the subsequent suit but will also operate as resjudicate in the subsequent suit between the same parties and not whether the cause of action or reliefs claim and/or one of the issues arising in both the suits are the same. 

15. Mr. Karmaker, also referred to a decision of .PLD 1968 (HCD) Page 557 and has argued that Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure has an application where the matter in issue in the subsequent suit is also directly and substantially in issue in the previously instituted suit pending in the same or any other Court having jurisdiction to grant relief claimed in that suit and parties in both the suits are litigating in the same common title. Mr. Karmaker also submitted that multiplicity of proceedings might arise if subsequent, suit in question is not stayed and he will be highly prejudiced thereby.  

16. Mr. Karmaker, also referred to 61 'Page 559 and submitted that for an application of Section 10" of the Code of. Civil Procedure complete identity of either the subject matter or the parties is not required and in the facts and circumstances of the case the learned Court below ought to have allowed the application granting stay in Title suit No. 131 of 1994.

17. On The other Mr. Fariduddin Md. Reza appearing for the opposite party Nos. and 2 has submitted that in the facts and circumstances the learned Senior Assistant Judge .Keraniganj. Dhaka has rightly rejected the application of the defendant petitioners saying that. the two suits in question i.e Title Suit No. 151 of 1994 pending in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and Title Suit No.- 131 of 1994 pending in the Court of .Senior Assistant Judge. Dhaka are not of same nature and character and the cause of action in the two suits are different. 

18. Mr. Reza has referred to AIR 1954 .(Panj) Page (113 and has submitted that for an application under Section. 10 of the Cade of Civil Procedure the same matter should be directly and substantially an issue in both the suit and if it is in part, that. will no do. 

19. Mr. Reza then referred to AIR 1947 (Lahore) Page 28. and has submitted that in order to attract the application of section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, their must be a complete identity of the entire subject matter of the two suits .and it is necessary that over matter in dispute should be directly and substantially in issue in the two suits are the same. 

20. Mr. Reza then referred to AIR 1947 (Born) Page 64 and has  submitted that for an application under  Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedures all matters is issues in Second suit must be matters in issue in the previous suit. 

21. Mr. Reza has referred to PLD 1961 (Dhaka) Page 344 and has submitted that in order to attract the operation of the principle embodied in Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is necessary that the entire subject matter of the two suits should he the same. 

22. Mr. Reza then submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the Seaton 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not applicable and the Court below the rightly rejected the application of defendants petitioner and the Rule issued by the High Court Division should be discharged. 

23. I have heard both the Sides at length and it is found that though the entire subject matter of the two suits are not the case at least two suits plots are the same i.e. the two suits plots being Plot Nos. 759 in C.S. Khatian NO. 160 of Mouza Modhyer Char P.S. Keraniganj, Dhaka and Plot No. 132. of C. S. Khatiari No. 67 of Mouza Napiadi P.S. Kerahiganj, Dhaka are the same suit plots in both the suits -i.e. Title suit No. 151.of 1994 of the learned 4th Court of Subordinate Judge. Dhaka and Title No. 131 of 1994 of the Assistant Judge Keraniganj, Dhaka and the Prolcagation of the two suits in their own ways could not be prudent. I find that there is considerable force in the agreement of Mr. Karmaker the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioners that the final decision being reached in the previous  suit would apprate  as reajadicata in the subsequent suit and earlier suit will have bearing in the subsequent suit over the same subject matter (at least for two suit plot and there are chances that defendant petitioners might be prejudiced in determining of their 'claims and I. feat, that the Court has inherent power to stay the suit, I find that the subject matter in issue (at least for two suit plots) as aforesaid in  the above two Suits for the same, in material and not the claim of  the parties, 

24. On careful circumstation of the Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure it Same to an that the subject matter (at least two suit plots mentioned above) in issue in the previously instituted and in the subsequent suit is material consideration for the Court in an application under Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure are the relevant issue in the said two suits. 

25. In the facts. and circumstances of the case, 1 find that at least two Suit plots in the above two suits are the same and in two Court's proceeding are pending and to avoid conflict of judgments and to avoid possibility of multiplicity of proceedings, the subsequent suit should be stayed. 

26. During the pendency of this revisional application the opposite Parties field and application for permanent injunction Under Order 29, Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and. Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for temporary injunction alleging that the suit land including Plot No. 759 of Mouza Modhver Char and Plot No. 132 of Mouza Napiadi are involved in both the suits and that the defendant petitioners are required to be restrained by way of temporary injunction from entering into the suits land On the other side, the defendant petitioners claim that they are in exclusive possession of the suit land (by swearing an affidavit) this question of possession by both the parties is a case of claim and counter claim. 

27. Anyhow, the parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of the possession in the disputed lands. 

28. In view of the above discussions I set aside the impugned judgment and order and allow the application field by the defendant-petitioners under Section 10 of Code of Civil Procedure and direct the trial of the subsequent suit i.e. Title Suit No. 131 .of 1994 pending in the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge Keraniganj. Dhaka be stayed till disposal of the earlier suit that is Title suit. No. 151 of 1994 pending in the Court of 4th subordinate Judge, Dhaka. 

29. In the result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. 

End.
