full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J: This rule is directed against the order dated 13.8.82 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 67 of 1985.

2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of this rule are that opposite party Nos. 2-3 as plaintiffs filed title Suit No. 102 of 1962 before the Sub-Ordinate Judge; 1st Court Dhaka against the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners and others praying for a specific saham in the suit property according to their shares.

3. The suit was contested by defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam, the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners, defendant No. 7 and defendant Nos. 14-16 by filing written statements denying the material allegations of the plaint contending inter alia that the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit property and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge by his impugned judgment dated 10.7.65 was pleased to decree the suit in preliminary form. Thereafter opposite party No. 1, who was defendant No. 7 in the suit, filed on 20.7.67 an application praying for appointment of an Advocate Commissioner for effective partition of the suit property in terms of the preliminary decree and the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge by his order dated 16.8.67 was pleased to allow the said prayer and directed the decree holder to deposit the requisite commission fees. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge was eventually pleased to accept the Advocate Commissioner's Report on 3.5.84, although the judgment-debtors raised objection against the said report. The preliminary decree was subsequently made final on 3.5.84.

5. On 6.8.1986 the petitioners filed an application for staying all further proceedings of Execution Case No. 67 of 1985 alleging inter alia that the predecessor-in-interest defendant. No. 5 Abdus Salam had died on 3.3.84 i.e. about two months before passing of the final decree on 3.5.1984 and as such the said final decree is a nullity in the eye of law and consequently the petitioners prayed for setting aside the final decree as being passed against a dead man in defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam and prayed for staying all further proceeding of the Execution Case in question. The learned Sub-Ordinate Judge by the impugned order dated 18.8.86 rejected the petitioners prayer holding that although defendant No. 5 died on 3.3.84 and the final decree was passed on 3.5.84 the decree in question cannot be treated as a nullity in view of the provision of Order 22 rule 4(4) of the Code of Civil procedure.

6. Mr. Abdul Hamid Chowdhury, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge seriously erred in law in passing the impugned order on an erroneous view of law regarding the provision of Order 22 rule 4(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, Order 22 rule 4(4) C.P.C. reads as follows:-

"(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (3), the plaintiff shall not be required to substitute and shall he exempt from the necessity of substituting the legal representatives of any such defendant who has failed to file a written statement or who having filed it has failed to appear and contest the suit at the hearing and judgment may in such a case he pronounced against the deceased defendant notwithstanding the death of such defendant and shall have the same force and effect as if it had been pronounced before the death took place".

<u>7. There is no dispute to the fact that deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam filed written statement in the suit and contested the suit- by adducing evidence and he was allotted a saham for 1.31 acres of land. There is also no dispute to the fact that deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam, one of the judgment-debtors, died on 3.3.84 before the passing of the final decree on 3.5.84. It is thus manifestly evident that the final decree was passed against deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam without bringing his legal representatives on record by way of necessary substitution. It is true, the rights of the contending parties in a suit for partition are determined in the preliminary decree and the final decree is just a follow-up of the preliminary decree in effecting partition of the suit properties by metes and bounds keeping in view the existing possession of the parties as far as practicable. The final decree is, in fact, a continuation of the preliminary decree in course of which the parties are put to actual physical possession of the suit properties according to sahams allotted to them. So, if the final decree is completed in the absence of a party who was allotted a specific saham it is likely that his vital interest to go unrepresented and he is adversely affected thereby. Since in the instant case, a definite saham measuring 1.31 acres of land was allotted to deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam he had, and after his death his legal representatives have a right to get possession in their allotted Saham with reference to the existing possession of the parties but unless they were brought on record their interests can be said to be properly safeguarded by the action of the Advocate-Commissioner, against whose report written objection had already been filed. Since evidently the final decree was passed against deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam on 3.5.84 i.e. after two months of his death without bringing his legal representatives on record by way of substitution, it is to be held that vital interests of the petitioners have been adversely affected in effecting the final decree in their absence.</u>

8. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, I find that the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge misread and miss-appreciated the provision of Order 22 rule 4(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure and fell in error in passing the impugned order. The impugned order passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge does not appear to be either legal or fair and the same has occasioned failure of justice. For the reason stated above. I find that the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order on an erroneous view of law regarding the provision of Order 22 rule 4(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

9. In the result, the impugned order dated 13.8.86 is set aside and the rule is made absolute. The learned Sub-Ordinate Judge is directed to proceed with the execution case in question in accordance with law and in the light of the observations made in the body of this judgment. There will be no order as to costs. Since this is a very old case it is desirable that the case should be disposed of as expeditiously as possible, preferably within 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of this order. The order of stay granted earlier by this court is vacated.

Let a copy of the order be sent to the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka at once.

End.

caseno: Civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 1212 of 1998
lawyer:
For the petitioner: Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Shamsul Haque Siddique. Advocate-On-Record. 
For the respondent Nos.2 and 5: Mr. Mahmudul Islam. Senior Advocate, Instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossaln Advocate-On-Record
Respondent Nos. 1-3 and 4: Not represented.
parties:
M. Majid Plaintiff ------ Petitioner
Versus
lqbal Bahar Chowdhury and others ------ Defendant Respondents:
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman. J: The plaintiff decree holder petitioner calls in question the judgment and order passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3657 of 1996 on 13.7.98 upholding Order No. 30 dated 2.11.96 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 21 of 1993.

2. The primary question involved in this petition is whether the judgment-debtor-respondents could seek the remedy by filing an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure wherein he challenged the execution proceeding itself as illegal and without jurisdiction and prayed for restoration of possession as an ancillary relief after setting aside the entire execution proceeding. "

3. It will be necessary to narrate in brief the circumstances under which Title Execution Case No. 21 of 1993 arose. The plaintiff petitioner filed Title Suit No.4 of 1994 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 5th Court Dhaka. The said suit was filed for specific performance of contract on the assertion that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 entered into an agreement for sale with predecessor-in interest of the plaintiff. While the process of transfer was continuing in pursuance of the agreement, defendant No.3 the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants purchased the suit land from defendant Nos. 1 and 2 with full knowledge of the earlier contract with the plaintiff for sate of the suit property. Hence the suit.

4. Defendant No.3 contested the suit asserting that she had no knowledge of the plaintiff's earlier contract whatsoever and part of the suit property had already been acquired by the Government. She being a bonafide purchaser for value without notice of the alleged contract the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. The suit was decreed by the trial court on 30.8.55. Against that judgment and decree defendant No.3 preferred First Appeal No. 205 of 1955 before the then High Court of East Pakistan. The said appeal was allowed in part and the decree of the trial court was modified by the High Court on 22.3.1960. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree of the High Court of the then East Pakistan two appeals were preferred before the Supreme Court of the then Pakistan by both the parties wherein both the appeals were dismissed and the judgment and decree of the High Court of East Pakistan was affirmed on 17.3.64.

6. The modified decree was passed by the High Court on 22.3.60 and the plaintiff did not take steps for execution of the appellate decree. On 9,8.93 the plaintiff filed an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for drawing up a modified decree in the light of the judgment of the High Court. The Subordinate judge allowed the application and drew up a modified decree on 22.8.93. Thereafter the plaintiff filed the aforesaid Execution Case No.21 of 1993. Subsequent thereto, the deed was registered through court and on 30.11.93 the decree holder filed an application in the executing Court for getting possession of the suit land by partition after appointing an Advocate Commissioner. The said prayer was allowed. Thereafter by police force the Advocate Commissioner effected partition of the suit land and gave possession to the decree-holder.

7. The main contention of the defendant-judgment-debtors is that the entire execution proceeding was started behind their back and without any notice to them. The defendants came to know of the execution case on 2.11.95 when they were evicted from the suit property. The entire proceeding is a fraudulent one to grab the property by drawing up a modified decree on 22:8.98 by the trial court in order to save limitation. The modified decree of the High Court was drawn on 22.3.60 and there was no execution proceeding within the period of limitation as prescribed under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. The defendants also asserted that the application for partition of the suit property which was filed behind the back and without the knowledge of the defendant is illegal and the executing court has no jurisdiction to partition the suit property in executing the decree for specific performance of contract.

8. As already noticed the trial court allowed the application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and set aside the entire proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 21 of 1993 and restored possession to the defendants thereby status quo ante was restored in favour of the defendants.

9. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim learned Advocate appearing for the decree holder petitioner submits that the executing court has no jurisdiction to set aside the entire execution proceeding in an application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, but the same is to be set aside by filing a separate suit and the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division acted wrongly and illegally in affirming the order of the executing court.

<u>10. It is to be stated at the outset that the decree of the trial court as passed in Title Suit No. 4 of 1994 was modified by the High Court of the then East Pakistan on 22.3.60. The decree of the trial court having been modified by the High Court it merged into the decree of the High Court. Hence, the question of drawing up of a modified decree on 9.8.93 in the light of the judgment and decree of the High Court in First Appeal is wholly illegal and without jurisdiction. It is found that the modified decree was passed on 22.3.1960 and to avoid the question of limitation a modified decree was again drawn up by the trial court on 9.8.93 and which is so obvious that it was obtained from a court by fraudulent means. Even if it is admitted that a mistake was committed by the executing court itself even then there are innumerable authorities of this court to hold that any error or wrong committed by the court itself can be corrected in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to secure the ends of justice and to prevent the abuse of process of court. Thus, the execution proceeding is apparently barred under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. The plaintiff did not take any steps within three years from the modified decree of the High Court nor did he keep alive the decree by taking steps to execute the decree within 12 years from the date of the final modified decree. Thus in order to avoid the bar of limitation the plaintiff fraudulently got the modified decree drawn up by the trial court. Hence the application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is maintainable in the facts of the present case.</u>

11. Further, the plaintiff got decree for 8 Annas share of the suit property as modified by the High Court. In the execution preceding the application was filed by the decree-holder for partition and for possession. Without filing a partition suit the executing court cannot also pass an order for possession when the decree itself does not contemplate such possession by partition of the property by metes and bounds. This exercise of jurisdiction by the executing court is palpably erroneous and without jurisdiction. Hence, we are of the view that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division correctly decided the question of maintainability of the application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

12. The judgment of the High Court Division suffers from no illegality. It may be added that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division deserves credit for wilting out well reasoned and comprehensive judgment in this case.

13. The petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 762 of 1998
lawyer:
For petitioners: Mr. Md. Nazibar Rahman, Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondents: Not represented.
parties:
Ambiya Khatoon and others ------ Petitioners
Versus
Md. Zahirul Islam and others ------ Respondents Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 762 of 1998
Ambiya Khatoon and others ------ Petitioners
Versus
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J.: This petition for leave to appeal is from the judgment and order dated 26-5-98 passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3706 of 1995 making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the concurrent judgment of dismissal of Title Suit No. 175 of 1988 for declaration of title and recovery of possession by the 1st Court of Senior Assistant Judge and on appeal by the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka.

	2. The plaintiff-respondents' case is that the Government allotted the suit property to defendant No. 4 Adam Ali by Memo dated 26-6-76 and handed over possession on 22-9-82 on payment of entire consideration money. A lease deed for 99 years was executed and registered by both the parties on 5-5-86. Adam All obtained a sanctioned plan from the then Dhaka Improvement Trust on 21-6-86 and had made some constructions on the suit property and then the suit property was sold on 13-7-86 to the plaintiff by a registered deed of sale and physical pos-session thereof was delivered. Since then the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property. In December, 1986 defendant Nos. 1-3 trespassed into the suit property and forcibly evicted the plaintiff there from after which the principal defendants filed Title Suit No. 75 of 1987 in the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for permanent injunction against the plaintiffs vendor. The suit was dismissed for default. The defendants did not try to get it restored. The plaintiff then filed the instant suit. 

	3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contended in their written statement that the suit property is their ancestral property. It was requisitioned and acquired in L.A. Case No. 13/59-60. Defendant No. 1 was given an allotment for her rehabilitation as an affected person by a Memo dated 7-3-79 in a different plot (not the suit plot). She claims that she was residing in the suit land inspite of requisition and acquisition since it was her paternal property for a long time and she has submitted an appeal to give allotment of the suit land for her rehabilitation which is pending. Defendant No. 2 is now dead and has been substituted by his heirs. Both the defendants denied the story of possession of the Plaintiff and his dispossession by the defendants. 

	4. The Government in its written statement admitted the allotment of the suit land to Adam All but contended that since Adam All transferred the suit land to the plaintiff without making construction and without prior permission of the Government the sale was made in violation of clause 19 of the lease deed. 

	5. As already noticed both the trial Court and the lower appellate Court dismissed the suit. The High Court Division upon noticing clauses 19 and 23 of the lease deed and noticing some decisions held that as no notice was served upon Adam Ali under the forfeiture clause his lease was subsisting and his transfer to the plaintiff was valid. Possession follows title and the defendants have no title. The Government also does not accept the defendants either as lessees or as owners. 

	6. Mr. Md. Nazibar Rahman, learned Advocate for the defendant petitioners submits that the High Court Division erred in law in characterising the petitioners' possession of the suit property as trespassers and failed to decide the question of limitation in the context of the defendants' possession for a long period over 12 years before the institution of the suit. 

	7. The suit property is a requisitioned and acquired property and the defendants' possession therein will not deprive the plaintiff from maintaining his title and to recover his possession. 

	8. Mr. Nazibar Rahman submits next that the High Court Division misconstrued the relevant clauses of the lease deed. 

	9. We have gone through the discussion of the relevant clauses of the lease deed by the High Court Division and are satisfied that there has been no misconstruction. 

	10. We do not find any ground for interference. 

	11. The petition is dismissed.

	End.

lawyer:
For the Appellant ------ Mr. Faruque Ahmed, Advocate-on-Record. 
For respondent No. I ------ Mr. Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Sajjadul Huq, Advocate-On-Record. 
Respondent Nos. 2-5 ------ Not represented.
parties:
Arosh Ali ------ Appellant.
Versus
Shah Taslimuddin Qurashi and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J. : a This appeal by leave at the instance of defendant No. 5 appellant is against the judgment and order dated 29.6.94 passed by a Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2465 of 1992, making the Rule absolute by setting aside the judgment and order dated 31.8.92 passed by the Assistant Judge, Jagannathpur, Sunamganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1992 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, allowing the said miscellaneous case by setting aside the ex parte decree dated 22.3.92 and restoring Title Suit No. 10 of 1990 to its original file and number. 

	2. The plaintiff-respondents instituted the aforesaid title suit for a declaration of their right of pathway over the suit land as defendant No. 5 and others have created obstruction in their passage through the pathway. 

	3. Defendant No. 5 appellant and others filed a joint written statement denying the claim of the plaintiffs stating, inter alia, that they are the owners of the suit land and it is not a pathway and the plaintiffs have no right of pathway over the suit land. 

	4. During the pendency of the suit, at the instance of the plaintiffs and Advocate Commissioner was appointed for local investigation of the suit land. The Advocate Commissioner after investigation submitted his report on 4.1.92. The report of the Advocate Commissioner was accepted on 4.3.92 by the trial Court after hearing the objections of the parties and the suit was fixed for preemptory hearing on 22.3.92: On 22.3.92 the plaintiffs filed hazira of 5 Witnesses but defendant No. 5 and other Contesting defendants prayed for time on the ground that they would file a revisional application before the High Court Division against the order of accepting the report of the Advocate Commissioner. The learned Assistant Judge rejected the prayer and after examination of witnesses on behalf of the plaintiff decreed the suit ex parte on 22.3.92. 

	5. Thereafter the constituted attorney of defendant No. 5 appellant filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree. 

	6. Defendant No. 5 appellant examined three witnesses and respondent No. 1 examined one witness in support of their respective cases. The learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the evidence on record allowed the miscellaneous case and restored the suit to its original file and number with a direction to the appellant to pay a cost of Tk. 700/- to the respondents. A learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in revision made the Rule absolute and set aside the order of restoration of the suit. 

	7. Leave was granted to consider whether the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in disturbing the finding of fact of the trial Court wherein the trial Court found that there was sufficient cause for filing the application for adjournment of further hearing of the suit and thereby wrongly interfered with the finding of fact of the Court below and whether the learned Single Judge was correct in Setting aside the finding of the trial Court that inspite of sonic laches of the constituted attorney the appellant could make out a case of sufficient cause for filing the application as there was some delay in getting instructions of the principal from London to move the High Court Division. Leave was further granted to consider whether the learned Single Judge wrongly applied the principle of the case of Reazul Hoque Mollah Vs. Afizullah Mollah, 42 DLR (AD) 74, which has no application in the facts of the present case. 

	8. In the miscellaneous case, the trial Judge found that constituted attorney P.W. 1 got instruction from his principal from London over phone on 20.3.92 for challenging the order of the trial Court dated 4.3.92 before the High Court Division. Although the trial Judge found that the constituted attorney was not very diligent in prosecuting the suit but the trial Judge found that the appellant had sufficient cause for not appearing on the date of hearing as the appellant filed an application for time for moving the High Court Division. The trial' Judge found from the materials on record that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing in Court when the suit was taken up for hearing. The trial Court believed from the evidence on record that the appellant had all genuine intention to prefer a revisional application before the High Court Division. It is on record that after getting instruction from the principal from London on 20.3.92 the application for certified copy was filed on 21.3.92. Thereafter an application for time was filed on the next day praying for only 15 days time. The trial Judge believed that the appellant genuinely wanted to move the High Court Division after getting instruction from his principal from London and that was considered to be a sufficient cause and hence allowed the case with a cost of Taka 700/-. 

	9. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division was under an impression that the learned Assistant Judge allowed the application for restoration of the suit mainly upon exercise of inherent power under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and wrongly held that when there is specific provision in the Code for moving an application for setting aside an ex parte decree the learned Assistant Judge should not have allowed the case in exercise of inherent power of the Court. The substantive application for restoration was filed under Order 9 Rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such the observation of the learned Single Judge is not factually and legally correct. The case of Reazul Hoque Mollah Vs. Afizullah Mollah, 42 DLR(AD) 74 relied upon by the learned Single Judge is in applicable in the facts of the present case. Moreover, the learned Single Judge failed to consider that on factual determination the learned Assistant Judge came to a positive finding that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause for not appearing in the case when it was taken up for hearing. In normal circumstances such prayer ought to be allowed and the rejection appears to have baffled the appellant. P.W. 1 has also staled about his telephonic conversation with the appellant in London on 20.3.92 regarding moving the higher Court. It also appears that the order of the Assistant Judge is a well reasoned order. Though he found some laches on the part of the appellant yet he allowed the application for restoration after awarding costs and finding sufficient cause for not appearing on that date. Sufficient cause having been found by the trial Court the learned Single Judge acted wrongly in exercise of his revisional jurisdiction in interfering with a determination of fact. In revision, such interference has in fact caused miscarriage of justice. 

	10. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost and the suit is restored to its original file and number. 

	End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 392 of 2000
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record. 

For the Respondents: Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate, Supreme Court, instructed by Mr. Ataur Rahman Khan, Advocate-on-Record.
parties:
Managing Director, Rupali Bank ------ Petitioner
-Versus-
Haji Jahan Ara Begun and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Mainur Reza Chowdhury, J: This petition for leave to appeal has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 18.5.2000 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 302 of 2000 making the Rule absolute and directing the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1 to proceed with Title Execution Case No. 2 of 1998 expeditiously on setting aside the order dated 29.11.99 and 30.1.2000 passed by the said court in the said execution case serving notice upon judgment debtor.

2. The short facts of the case are that the decree holder respondent instituted Title Suit No. 55 of 1986 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, against the judgment-debtor petitioner as defendants for realization of Tie 84,50,000/-. Subsequently the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 18 of 1997. After several dates the suit was fixed for hearing on 31.8.1999 but since the defendant remained absent and took no step in the matter the suit was decreed exparte against the defendant judgment-debtor for an amount of Tk. 84,50,000/-. The decree was drawn up and signed on 15.9.1999. Thereafter the decree holder respondent that is the plaintiff in the said suit started Execution Case No. 2 of 1999 on 29.11.1999. On that date the execution case was registered and show cause notice was issued upon the defendant fixing 30.1.2000 for taking steps. On 30.1.2000 an order was passed to the effect that notice was returned after service. The decree holder appeared and the defendants No. 1 and 4 filed power and prayed for time to file written objection which the prayers was allowed and 23.2.2000 was fixed for filing objection.

<u>3. The order dated 29.11.1999 for issuance of service of notice upon the judgment-debtors was challenged before the High Court Division and Rule was issued. It was submitted before the High Court Division that the Execution Case was filed under Order 21, Rule 11 of he Code of Civil Procedure and the court was required to proceed with the case and there was no provision for issuing notice upon the judgment-debtors if the execution case had been filed within two years from the date of decree. Order 21, Rule 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that if the execution case is filed after two years from the date of decree then the show cause notice ought to be issued upon the judgment-debtor. In the instant case the decree was drawn up and signed on 15.9.1999 and the execution case was tiled on 29.11.1999. Since the execution case was filed within three months from the date of passing the decree issuance of notices upon the judgment-debtor was absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction. It was further submitted before the High Court Division the suit was filed in the year 1986 and the decree obtained in the year 1999 and in order to cause delay in the execution proceeding and also to obstruct the decree-holders from getting the benefit of the decree the judgment-debtors were taking time to file written objection though in law there was no provision for filing objection. The High Court Division after bearing both the parties accepted the submission made by the decree-holders and held that the court below acted in a manner which was not provided in law and that the process of execution of the decree would be delayed to the prejudice of the decree-holders, As such the High Court Division found that the orders Passed on 29.11.1999 as well as 30.1.2000 by the Executing Court in Execution Case No. 2 of 1999 could not be sustained in law. The executing court in passing on above mentioned orders had committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice and therefore made the Rule absolute with the direction to proceed with the execution ease in accordance with law expeditiously.</u>

4. The learned Counsel for the petitioner has failed to show any illegality in the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 302 of 2000.

5. The petition is, therefore, dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 382 of 2009
lawyer:
Fida M. Kamal, Senior Advocate, instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiya, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Mozaffar Hossain, Senior Advocate, instructed by A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Munshi Abdul Hai ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Sanjoy Kumar Shil ----- Respondent
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 27.10.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1827 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu. Nayeem Mominur Rahman J:- Instant application under Article 103 of the Constitution is for granting leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 27.10.2008 making the Rule absolute issued in Civil Revision No. 1827 of 2004 by the High Court Division and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 29.03.2004 allowing the Title Appeal No. 89 of 2001 by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Laxmipur, by which the judgment and decree dated 26.06.2001 decreeing the Title Suit No.88 of 2000 by the learned Assistant Judge, Ramganj, Laxmipur, was reversed. 

2. The respondent hereof as plaintiff filed the Title Suit No.88 of 2000 for declaration that the Mutation Khatian No. 270 was illegal, inoperative and collusive and made behind his back con-tending, inter alia, that the said Khatian has been prepared in the name of the defendant-petitioner hereof having no right, title and interest or possession in the suit land and that the suit land measuring 57 decimals of land out of 5.50 acres appertaining D.S. Khatian No.  82 corresponding to M. R.R Khatian No. 134 originally belonged to three sons of Doyaram Shil and that the said three sons while owning and possessing the suit land, one of them named Balaram Shil died leaving behind his other two brothers, namely, Rarnkanai Shil and R. amkumar Shil, who being the legal heirs and successor-in-interest inherited Balaramrs share. Subsequently Ramkumar Shil died leaving behind two sons namely, Kalinath Shil and Jadunath Shil to inherit his share and that Jadunath Shil died leaving behind one son Kcshab Chandra Shil and that the plaintiff Sanjoy Kumar Shil by virtue gift deeds dated 01.06.1992 and 28.06.1993 from the legal heirs in succession became owner possessor of 81 decimals of land including the suit land by erecting dwelling house as well as by growing seasonal crops thereon and that the impugned mutation khatian having been created, without notice, collusively in the name of the defendant-petitioner, the plaintiff-respondent has been compelled to file the suit. 

3. The defendant-petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations and asserting that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner as the suit is barred by limitation and that Jadunath-Shil sold 53 decimals of land to the defendant-petitioner by a registered sale deed dated 28.10.1970 within the knowledge of the plaintiff-respondent and that on the basis of said sale deed his name has been recorded in the record of right vide Mutation Case No.289 of 1988-89 and accordingly the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. The learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the materials on record and the pleading framed 4 issues namely:- 
১। অত্রাকারে ও প্রকারে অত্র মোকাদ্দমা চলিতে পারে কিনা? 
২। মোকাদ্দমা তামাদিতে বারিত কিনা? 
৩। বিগত ৮/১২/৮৮ইং তারিখের আদেশবলে সৃজিত নালিশী ২৭০নং নামজারী জমা খারিজ খতিয়ানটি বে-ইউনী, ক্ষমতা বহির্ভৃত বাতিলযোগ্য কিনা? 
৪। বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থিতমতে প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে কিনা? 

5. After discussing the evidence and the materials on record the trial Court decided the issues and accordingly decreed the suit declaring that the impugned orders relating to mutation in respect of the suit land are illegal, without jurisdiction and void holding, amongst others, that the plaintiff has proved his title and possession in the suit land and that the suit land is not a vested or non-resident property and that the sale vide. deed dated 28.10.1970 could-not be executed or registered by Jadhunath Shil since he died in the year 1968 as has been proved by P. W.2 and D.,W,.2 and that in-spite of Court's direction the defendant failed to produce his title deed in respect of the suit property and that the plaintiff by submitting the original gift deed proved his title, which fact was also corroborated by P.W.2, a teacher of a High School, and D.W.2, the Chairman in charge of the Union Parishad, and that the suit was filed within limitation and is maintain-able. 

6. Being aggrieved there-against the defendant preferred Title Appeal No. 89 of 2001 in the Court of District Judge, Laxmipur, and the said appeal on transfer was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Laxmipur, allowing the appeal and thereby dismissing the suit setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court holding that the suit was not maintainable and the suit was bad for defect of party and that the decision of the trial Court that the sale deed dated 28.10.1970, on the basis which of the defendant claims title and possession, was not executed and registered by Jadhunath Shil and therefore is without any basis and that the suit is bad for defect of parties since the officials of the Revenue Department were not impleaded in the suit. 

7. The plaintiff being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below moved the High Court Division with the revisional application and the High Court Division upon hearing the contesting parties made the Rule issued thereon absolute observing, amongst others, that: 
"The Court of appeal below on a misconception of law held that since the plaintiff was not a party in the order mutating the name of the defendant, he was not entitled to challenge that order in failing to consider that the defendant mutated his name in respect of the suit land over Which the plaintiff had acquired right and interest and that the said ex-parte order adversely affected his interest in the suit land and therefore, the plaintiff had the locus standi to challenge this order of mutating the name of the defendant. 
The Court of appeal below further observed that the suit is bad for defect of party in the absence of the Revenue Officer; this observation is also based upon misconception of law, inasmuch as, the Revenue Officer has passed the order while performing his official works and therefore the Revenue Officer having no subsisting interest in the suit land is neither a necessary nor a proper party in the suit. The Court of appeal below further held that the defendant having informed the Court that he had transferred the suit land in favour of Foriduddin, the suit without him is not maintainable. This observation of the Court of appeal below is based upon conjectures and surmises, inasmuch as, the defendant has not appeal below failed to notice that a partition suit is filed against a co-sharer but the defendants are not co-sharers in the suit land; they have no semblance of title in the suit land. This finding is based on hypothesis. The Court of appeal below further held that the suit with lit seeking declaration of title is not legally maintainable. The Court of appeal below failed to consider that the learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record held that the plaintiff has been able to prove his title and possession in the suit land. The Court must have regard to all relevant allegations in the plaint and must look to the Substance of the matter and not its form. Though the plaintiff does not seek declaration of title, if the plaint as a whole is read together it will appear that the plaintiff in fact is seeking title in the suit lands and accordingly, the trial Court has declared plaintiffs title and possession in exercise of powers under Order 7 Rule 7 C.P.C. under this provision a plaintiff ought to be given such relief as he is entitled to get on the facts established upon the evidence in the case even if the plaintiff does not contain a specific prayer for the relief. The judgment of the Court of appeal below is not only based upon misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record, but the same is also based upon conjectures and surmises. He has made some observations without having no basis at all as there is no material on record in support of such observation. The Court of appeal below has made out a third case in finding about non-existence of Keshab and also in finding about non-maintainability of the suit. The Court of appeal below also did not reverse all the findings arrived at by the trial-Court and in that view of the matter; the judgment of the Court of appeal below is not a proper judgment of reversal." 

8. We have perused the leave petition, impugned judgment and order and considered the submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner. It appears that the appellate court below did not consider the fact that the defendant failed to produce the sale deed dated 28.10.1970 in-spite of trial Court's direction given under Order 11 Rule 14 of the 'Code of Civil Procedure vide order dated 18.09.2000 and accordingly as per Order 11 Rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure the written statement filed by the defendant is liable to be struck out and the suit is to proceed as if no defence has been taken in the suit and that the appellate Court in the absence of materials on record held the suit to be had for defect of parties although no issue was suggested or framed therefor in the suit by the Trial Court. 

9. The learned Advocate appearing before us could not satisfy us as to the execution and registration of the sale deed dated 28.10.1970 in favour of the defendant rather the evidence on record goes to show that the alleged executor Jadhunath Shil died in the year 1968. Since the genuineness of sale deed dated 28.10.1970 could not be proved the impugned mutation based on said deed dated 28.10.1970 can not be sustained. 

10. Apart from that the observations as made by the High Court Division, quoted hereinabove, show that the High Court Division has dealt with the issue in detail and braved at its decision on clue consideration of the evidence and materials on record, which is in accordance with law. 

11. Thus we do not find any illegality or infirmity to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division. 

12. The petition is accordingly dismissed.

End.
